  37class EMGMotorUnit:
  38    """
  39    Class for storing data for one motor unit
  40    returned from reconstruction analysis.
  41
  42    """
  43
  44    def __init__(
  45        self,
  46        number: int,
  47        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
  48        fs: float,
  49        chan_xy: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
  50    ):
  51        """
  52        Initialise EMGMotorUnit object.
  53
  54        Parameters
  55        ----------
  56        number: int
  57            This is the motor unit index (0, 1, 2, ...), returned from TK_filter,
  58            which corresponds to the index position of "motor_units" in the
  59            EMGMotorUnits class. When displayed to the user the motor unit label
  60            is displayed which is +1 this number, e.g. motor_unit_number 0 is the
  61            motor unit labelled as "1".
  62        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
  63            Time indices of the motor unit's potentials in the EMG recording.
  64        fs : float
  65            Sampling frequency (Hz) of the data.
  66        chan_xy : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
  67            Channel (electrode) (x,y) coordinates; saved as attribute to facilitate
  68            visualisations.
  69
  70        Returns
  71        -------
  72        None.
  73
  74        """
  75
  76        self.motor_unit_number = number
  77
  78        # Number of potentials (firings) assigned to MU.
  79        self.n_potentials = len(potentials_t_idx)
  80        # Time indices of potentials in EMG.
  81        self.potentials_t_idx = potentials_t_idx
  82
  83        # Set sampling frequency.
  84        self.fs = fs
  85
  86        # Channel/electrode coordinates of the needle.
  87        self.chan_xy = chan_xy
  88
  89        # Store information about analysis that has been performed for this MU
  90        # Note: even if true, may not be results if data was not suitable for analysis
  91        self.analysis_performed = {
  92            "fibres_localised": False,  # localisation step
  93            "fibres_clustered": False,  # clustering fibres step
  94            "fibres_jitter_computed": False,  # jitter analysis step
  95        }
  96
  97        # Localisation attributes.
  98        # Number of fibre potentials (peaks) found across all MUPs.
  99        self.n_fibre_potentials = 0
 100
 101        # Size of window used for localisation.
 102        self.n_samples_window = 0
 103
 104        # Estimated fibre x, y coordinate at each time (size n peaks x 2).
 105        self.fibre_centres = np.array([])
 106
 107        # Onset indices of MUPs that each fibre potential (peak) belongs to.
 108        # One for each fibre potential.
 109        self.mup_onsets = np.array([])
 110
 111        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
 112        # of the corresponding MUP that it belongs to (in indices units, not seconds).
 113        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
 114
 115        # The channel in which each fibre potential has peak amplitude (may be min or max).
 116        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
 117
 118        # Time series for each MUP and channel
 119        # (size: n MU potentials x n chan x time).
 120        self.all_spikes = np.array([])
 121
 122        # Generator potential, represents true underlying potential.
 123        self.generator_potential = np.array([])
 124
 125        # Results for comparing number of clusters for GMM or k-means.
 126        self.cluster_scores = None
 127
 128        # Dictionaries for storing results of clustering and jitter analysis.
 129        self.fibre_clustering_results: dict = {}
 130        self.fibre_jitter_results: dict = {}

 166    def add_fibre_localisation(
 167        self,
 168        fibre_centres: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 169        mup_onsets: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 170        fibre_potential_times: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 171        fibre_potential_peak_chan: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 172        all_spikes: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 173        generator_potential: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 174    ):
 175        """
 176        Add results of the fibre localisation step to the motor unit object. Computes
 177        additional attributes and stores that analysis has been performed.
 178
 179        Called during EMGAnalysisReconstruct method, reconstruct_fibres
 180
 181        Parameters
 182        ----------
 183        fibre_centres : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 184            Estimated location of fibres.
 185        mup_onsets : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 186            Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time
 187        fibre_potential_times : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 188            Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset (overall) time
 189            of the corresponding MUP (listed above in mup_onsets)
 190        fibre_potential_peak_chan : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 191            The channel with the peak amplitude for each fibre potential.
 192        all_spikes : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 193            All peaks from surrounding channels.
 194        generator_potential : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 195            Represents true underlying potential. Used to find MUPs.
 196
 197        Returns
 198        -------
 199        None.
 200
 201        """
 202
 203        # Note analysis performed.
 204        self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = True
 205
 206        # Store number of fibre potentials (i.e., peaks in the MUPs) found.
 207        self.n_fibre_potentials = fibre_centres.shape[0]
 208
 209        # Store provided attributes.
 210        self.fibre_centres = fibre_centres
 211        self.mup_onsets = mup_onsets
 212        self.fibre_potential_times = fibre_potential_times
 213        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = fibre_potential_peak_chan
 214        self.all_spikes = all_spikes
 215        self.generator_potential = generator_potential
 216
 217        # Save the size of the window in number of indices, used later for plots.
 218        # So that all_spikes does not need to be saved with the results, and this
 219        # value can be saved and loaded instead.
 220        self.n_samples_window = self.all_spikes.shape[2]
 221
 222    def get_fibre_localisation_dict(self, save_all_spikes: bool = False) -> dict:
 223        """
 224        Returns dictionary of fibre localisation so that it can be saved
 225
 226        Parameters
 227        ----------
 228        save_all_spikes : bool, optional
 229            Whether to save all_spikes. Uses a lot of data and is not necessary.
 230            The default is False.
 231
 232        Returns
 233        -------
 234        dict
 235
 236        """
 237
 238        # Convert to lists to store as dictionary.
 239        fibre_local_dict = {
 240            "n_fibre_potentials": self.n_fibre_potentials,
 241            "fibre_centres": self.fibre_centres.tolist(),
 242            "mup_onsets": self.mup_onsets.tolist(),
 243            "fibre_potential_times": self.fibre_potential_times.tolist(),
 244            "all_spikes": [],
 245            "n_samples_window": self.n_samples_window,
 246            # "generator_potential" : self.generator_potential.tolist()
 247        }
 248
 249        if save_all_spikes:
 250            fibre_local_dict["all_spikes"] = self.all_spikes.tolist()
 251
 252        return fibre_local_dict

 282    def _cluster_silhouette_score(self, estimator, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> float:
 283        """
 284        Callable to pass to GridSearchCV that will use the silhouette score.
 285
 286        Parameters
 287        ----------
 288        estimator: Any
 289            Estimator class, which will include a "predict" method.
 290
 291        X : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 292            Array of fibre potential data to assign to clusters.
 293
 294        Returns
 295        -------
 296        float
 297
 298        """
 299
 300        return silhouette_score(X, estimator.predict(X))
 301
 302    def _gmm_selection(
 303        self, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64], min_n_clusters: int, max_n_clusters: int
 304    ) -> GridSearchCV:
 305        """
 306        Gaussian Mixture Model Selection.
 307        https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/mixture/plot_gmm_selection.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-mixture-plot-gmm-selection-py
 308        Fit data to clusters from the minimum number of clusters to the maximum number of clusters.
 309
 310        Parameters
 311        ----------
 312        X : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 313            Array of fibre potential data to assign to clusters.
 314        min_n_clusters : int
 315            Minimum number of clusters to try.
 316        max_n_clusters : int
 317            Maximum number of clusters to try.
 318
 319        Returns
 320        -------
 321        float
 322        """
 323
 324        param_grid = {
 325            "n_components": range(min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters + 1),
 326            "covariance_type": [self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type],
 327        }
 328
 329        grid_search = GridSearchCV(
 330            GaussianMixture(), param_grid=param_grid, scoring=self._cluster_silhouette_score
 331        )
 332
 333        grid_search.fit(X)
 334
 335        return grid_search
 336
 337    def _k_means_selection(
 338        self, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64], min_n_clusters: int, max_n_clusters: int
 339    ) -> GridSearchCV:
 340        """
 341        Try out k-means clustering for different numbers of clusters.
 342        Fit data to clusters from the minimum number of clusters to the maximum number of clusters.
 343
 344        """
 345
 346        param_grid = {
 347            "n_clusters": range(min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters + 1),
 348            "random_state": [self.mu_cluster_settings.k_means_random_state],
 349            "n_init": ["auto"],
 350        }
 351
 352        grid_search = GridSearchCV(
 353            KMeans(), param_grid=param_grid, scoring=self._cluster_silhouette_score
 354        )
 355
 356        grid_search.fit(X)
 357
 358        return grid_search

 360    def cluster_fibre_potentials(self, mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings):
 361        """
 362        Cluster the fibre potentials and compute median fibre locations of the
 363        specified motor unit.
 364
 365        Before this analysis is run, the motor unit's fibres potentials must be
 366        identified and localised using the reconstruct_fibres method of the
 367        EMGAnalysisReconstruct class.
 368
 369        Running this method populates the fibre_clustering_results dictionary attribute
 370        with the following key/value pairs:
 371            mean_n_fps (int): mean number of fibre potentials across all motor unit
 372            potentials used in the localisation analysis. Used as input for clustering.
 373
 374            n_fibre_clusters (int): number of clusters found; may slightly differ from
 375            mean_n_fps.
 376
 377            fibre_clusters (npt.NDArray[np.int32], size (self.fibre_potentials,) ):
 378                cluster assignment of each fibre potential
 379
 380            n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 381                                       size (self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters)):
 382            Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each motor unit potential (MUP) that
 383            have the same cluster assignment.
 384
 385            mup_fibre_pos (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 386                           size(self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters)):
 387            Location estimates ((x,y) coordinates) of each fibre based on each MUP. If
 388            the fibre is not found in the MUP, the coordinates are np.nan.
 389
 390            fibre_centres_median (npt.NDArray[np.float64], size(n_fibre_clusters, 2)):
 391            Median coordinates of each fibre.
 392
 393        Parameters
 394        ----------
 395        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 396            Contains all settings for clustering.
 397
 398        Raises
 399        ------
 400        RuntimeError
 401            Raised if localisation analysis has not been performed on requested motor
 402            unit.
 403
 404        Returns
 405        -------
 406        None.
 407
 408        """
 409
 410        # Set settings for cluster analysis.
 411        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
 412
 413        # Check that localisation has been run.
 414        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]:
 415            raise RuntimeError(
 416                "Localisation analysis has not been performed; cannot cluster fibres."
 417            )
 418
 419        # Arrays to store results for median and GMM clustering.
 420        fibre_centres_median = np.array([])
 421        fibre_centres_gmm_mean = np.array([])
 422        fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = np.array([])
 423
 424        # Onset indices of all MUPs that have fibre potentials.
 425        unique_mup_onsets = np.unique(self.mup_onsets)
 426        n_unique_mup_onsets = len(unique_mup_onsets)
 427        mean_n_fps = round(len(self.mup_onsets) / n_unique_mup_onsets)
 428
 429        # Set up data to use for clustering.
 430        if self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale > 0:
 431            # Scale time column.
 432            # Values in (0, 20] for self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale
 433            # are suitable for scaling.
 434            # Do not scale fibre locations as they are in the same units (mm).
 435            time_min = np.min(self.fibre_potential_times)
 436            time_max = np.max(self.fibre_potential_times)
 437
 438            data_to_cluster = np.hstack(
 439                (
 440                    self.fibre_centres,
 441                    (
 442                        (np.atleast_2d(self.fibre_potential_times).T - time_min)
 443                        / (time_max - time_min)
 444                    )
 445                    * self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale,
 446                )
 447            )
 448
 449        else:
 450            data_to_cluster = self.fibre_centres
 451
 452        # Choose clustering method.
 453        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "dbscan":
 454            # Use Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN).
 455            clustering = DBSCAN(
 456                eps=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_eps,
 457                min_samples=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_min_samples,
 458            ).fit(data_to_cluster)
 459            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(clustering.labels_) + 1
 460            fibre_clusters = clustering.labels_
 461
 462        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
 463            # k for clustering.
 464            k = self.mu_cluster_settings.k_means_k
 465
 466            # Use a range if no values of k if not given.
 467            if k == 0:
 468                min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
 469                max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
 470            else:
 471                min_n_clusters = k
 472                max_n_clusters = k
 473
 474            grid_search = self._k_means_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
 475
 476            # fibre cluster assignments.
 477            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
 478            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
 479
 480            # Record results for graph plotting.
 481            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
 482
 483        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 484            # Use Gaussian Mixture Model Selection.
 485            min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
 486            max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
 487
 488            grid_search = self._gmm_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
 489
 490            # Record results for graph plotting.
 491            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
 492
 493            # Fibre cluster assignments.
 494            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
 495            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
 496
 497            fibre_centres_gmm_mean = grid_search.best_estimator_.means_
 498            fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = grid_search.best_estimator_.covariances_
 499
 500        else:
 501            # If no valid clustering method given.
 502            raise Exception(
 503                "Clustering method,"
 504                + str(self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method)
 505                + ", not found!"
 506                + "Valid options are: dbscan, k-means or gmm."
 507            )
 508
 509        # Initialise arrays for storing results.
 510
 511        # Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each MUP that belong to the same
 512        # cluster.
 513        n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster = np.zeros((self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters))
 514
 515        # Location estimates of each fibre based on each MUP.
 516        # Note: unlike original code, data stored so indices match the
 517        # self.potentials_t_idx array.
 518        mup_fibre_pos = np.full((self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters), np.nan)
 519
 520        # Find median location of each fibre.
 521        for cluster_num in np.arange(n_fibre_clusters):
 522            # Sometimes multiple fibre potentials in the same MUP are assigned to
 523            # the same fibre clusters. One of these will be chosen later as the "best"
 524            # to compute the jitter. (One nearest the median over all MUPs)
 525            # If no fibres with that cluster num appear in the MUP, position is
 526            # stored as np.nan.
 527
 528            # Iterate through all MUPs (not just ones
 529            # present in "mup_onsets") so dimensions align to other MUP features.
 530            for mup_num in np.arange(self.n_potentials):
 531                mup_onset = self.potentials_t_idx[mup_num]
 532
 533                # Fibre potentials that belong to the specified onset and cluster.
 534                idx = np.flatnonzero(
 535                    np.all(
 536                        (
 537                            (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset),
 538                            (fibre_clusters == cluster_num),
 539                        ),
 540                        axis=0,
 541                    )
 542                )
 543
 544                # Store number of fibre potentials found.
 545                n_idx = len(idx)
 546                n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster[mup_num, cluster_num] = n_idx
 547
 548                # Compute average position of the fibre based on the specified MUP.
 549                if n_idx > 0:
 550                    pos = self.fibre_centres[idx, :]
 551                    mup_fibre_pos[mup_num, :, cluster_num] = np.mean(pos, axis=0)
 552
 553            # Compute median fibre positions.
 554            with warnings.catch_warnings():
 555                warnings.simplefilter("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
 556                fibre_centres_median = np.transpose(np.nanmedian(mup_fibre_pos, axis=0))
 557
 558        # Store results as dictionary.
 559        self.fibre_clustering_results = {
 560            "mean_n_fps": mean_n_fps,
 561            "n_fibre_clusters": n_fibre_clusters,
 562            "fibre_clusters": fibre_clusters,
 563            "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster,
 564            "mup_fibre_pos": mup_fibre_pos,
 565            "fibre_centres_median": fibre_centres_median,
 566            "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": fibre_centres_gmm_mean,
 567            "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": fibre_centres_gmm_covariance,
 568        }
 569        self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = True
 570
 571    def get_fibre_clusters_dict(self) -> dict:
 572        """
 573        Returns dictionary of fibre clusters so that it can be saved.
 574
 575        Parameters
 576        ----------
 577        None.
 578
 579        Returns
 580        -------
 581        dict
 582            Dictionary containing clustering results.
 583
 584        """
 585
 586        # Get clustering results if they exist and put in a dictionary
 587        # with arrays stored as lists so they can be save in a json format file.
 588        if self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]:
 589            fibre_clusters_dict = {
 590                "mean_n_fps": int(self.fibre_clustering_results["mean_n_fps"]),
 591                "n_fibre_clusters": int(self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]),
 592                "fibre_clusters": self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"].tolist(),
 593                "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 594                    "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster"
 595                ].tolist(),
 596                "mup_fibre_pos": self.fibre_clustering_results["mup_fibre_pos"].tolist(),
 597                "fibre_centres_median": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 598                    "fibre_centres_median"
 599                ].tolist(),
 600                "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 601                    "fibre_centres_gmm_mean"
 602                ].tolist(),
 603                "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 604                    "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"
 605                ].tolist(),
 606            }
 607        else:
 608            fibre_clusters_dict = {}
 609
 610        return fibre_clusters_dict
 611
 612    def set_fibre_clusters_from_dict(
 613        self, fibre_clusters_dict: dict, mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 614    ):
 615        """
 616        Sets fibre localisation results from loaded dictionary.
 617
 618        Parameters
 619        ----------
 620        fibre_clusters_dict : dict
 621            Dictionary containing saved results of clustering
 622
 623        mu_cluster_settings : EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 624            Copy of settings used to do clustering.
 625
 626        Returns
 627        -------
 628        None.
 629
 630        """
 631
 632        # If clustering not done for this MU then do not set anything.
 633        if fibre_clusters_dict:
 634            # Convert lists back to arrays to store results.
 635            self.fibre_clustering_results = {
 636                "mean_n_fps": fibre_clusters_dict["mean_n_fps"],
 637                "n_fibre_clusters": fibre_clusters_dict["n_fibre_clusters"],
 638                "fibre_clusters": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_clusters"]),
 639                "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": np.array(
 640                    fibre_clusters_dict["n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster"]
 641                ),
 642                "mup_fibre_pos": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["mup_fibre_pos"]),
 643                "fibre_centres_median": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_median"]),
 644                "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"]),
 645                "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": np.array(
 646                    fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"]
 647                ),
 648            }
 649
 650            # Note analysis performed.
 651            self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = True
 652
 653            # Set clustering settings also.
 654            self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
 655
 656    def plot_compare_cluster_scores(self) -> sns.FacetGrid:
 657        """
 658
 659        Parameters
 660        ----------
 661        None.
 662
 663        Returns
 664        -------
 665        sns.FacetGrid
 666            Returns the FacetGrid object with the plot on it for further tweaking.
 667
 668        """
 669
 670        # Set variable name of data to retrieve.
 671        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 672            cluster_str = "param_n_components"
 673        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
 674            cluster_str = "param_n_clusters"
 675        else:
 676            cluster_str = ""
 677
 678        # Return blank plot if no data.
 679        if cluster_str == "" or self.cluster_scores is None:
 680            return sns.catplot(kind="bar")
 681
 682        # Create bar plot.
 683        grid = sns.catplot(
 684            kind="bar",
 685            x=self.cluster_scores[cluster_str],
 686            y=self.cluster_scores["mean_test_score"],
 687            legend_out=False,
 688        )
 689
 690        # Set limits and layout.
 691        plt.ylim((0, 1))
 692        plt.tight_layout(pad=5.0)
 693
 694        grid.set_axis_labels("number of clusters", "silhouette score")
 695
 696        return grid

 698    def plot_fibre_locations_setup(
 699        self,
 700        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
 701        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 702        tick_label_size: float = 12,
 703        dpi: int = 100,
 704        threeD: bool = False,
 705    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
 706        """
 707        Sets up plot for showing fibre locations, possibly from different motor units.
 708
 709        Parameters
 710        ----------
 711        figsize : tuple[int, int], optional
 712            Size of the figure. The default is (10, 5).
 713        axis_label_size : int, optional
 714            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
 715        tick_label_size : int, optional
 716            Size of the tick labels. The default is 12.
 717        dpi : int, optional
 718            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
 719        threeD : bool, optional
 720            Create 3D plot if true. The default is False.
 721
 722        Returns
 723        -------
 724        fig : Figure
 725            The figure to which the plot belongs.
 726        ax : Axes
 727            The axes to which the plot belongs.
 728
 729        """
 730
 731        # Create new figure with specified size.
 732        if threeD:
 733            fig = Figure(figsize=figsize)
 734            ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
 735        else:
 736            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
 737
 738        fig.dpi = dpi
 739
 740        # Add axis and tick labels.
 741        ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 742        ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 743        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 744        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 745
 746        # Add time axis if 3D plot.
 747        # Type checking complains for 3D but it is fine.
 748        if threeD:
 749            ax.set_zlabel("time (\u03bc seconds)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
 750            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 751
 752        plt.title(f"Motor Unit {self.motor_unit_number+1}")
 753
 754        return fig, ax

 756    def _plot_electrodes(
 757        self,
 758        ax: Axes,
 759        marker: str = "s",
 760        marker_size: float = 20,
 761        clr: str = "silver",
 762        z: float = None,
 763    ):
 764        """
 765        Plot electrode locations using their (x,y) coordinates.
 766
 767        Electrodes are symbolised by grey squares by default.
 768
 769        Parameters
 770        ----------
 771        ax : Axes
 772            Axes to plot the electrodes onto.
 773        marker : str, optional
 774            The kind of marker to use. The default is "s", square.
 775        marker_size : float, optional
 776            The size of the markers. The default is 20.
 777        clr : str, optional
 778            The colour of the electrodes. Default is "silver".
 779        z : float, optional
 780            z value of electrodes for 3D plot. Default is None.
 781
 782        Returns
 783        -------
 784        None.
 785
 786        """
 787
 788        # Plot electrodes.
 789        if z is None:
 790            ax.scatter(
 791                self.chan_xy[:, 0], self.chan_xy[:, 1], s=marker_size, marker=marker, color=clr
 792            )
 793        else:
 794            # Plot electrodes on 3D graph at set z distance.
 795            ax.scatter(
 796                self.chan_xy[:, 0],
 797                self.chan_xy[:, 1],
 798                np.full(len(self.chan_xy[:, 0]), z),
 799                s=marker_size,
 800                marker=marker,
 801                color=clr,
 802            )

 804    def plot_fibre_potential_clustering(
 805        self,
 806        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
 807        pt_potentials_size: float = 10,
 808        pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4,
 809        pt_mean_size: float = 50,
 810        n_sigma: int = 2,
 811        axis_equal: bool = True,
 812        lw: float = 0.5,
 813        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.2, 5.0),
 814        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 815        tick_label_size: float = 12,
 816        dpi: int = 100,
 817        cmap=None,
 818        max_x: float = 22,
 819        max_y: float = 1,
 820        plot_legend: bool = True,
 821        legend_pt_size: float = 50,
 822        legend_label_size: float = 12,
 823    ):
 824        """
 825        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
 826        with the location of each fibre overlaid. Ellipse confidence regions are plotted
 827        around te fibre locations
 828        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
 829
 830        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
 831
 832        Parameters
 833        ----------
 834        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
 835            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
 836        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
 837            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
 838        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
 839            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
 840        pt_mean_size : float, optional
 841            Size of points for means. The fibre centres. The default is 50.
 842        n_sigma : float, optional
 843            Number of St. Dev. to plot around the fibre centres. The Default is 2.
 844        axis_equal : bool, optional
 845            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
 846        lw : float, optional
 847            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
 848        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
 849            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
 850        axis_label_size : float, optional
 851            size of axis label. The default is 14.
 852        tick_label_size : float, optional
 853            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
 854        dpi : int, optional
 855            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
 856        cmap : Any, optional
 857            Colour map to use. The default is None.
 858        max_x : float, optional
 859            Maximum of x axis. The default is 22.
 860        max_y : float, optional
 861            Maximum of y axis. The default is 1.
 862        plot_legend : bool, optional
 863            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
 864        legend_pt_size : float, optional
 865            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
 866        legend_label_size: float, optional
 867            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
 868
 869        Returns
 870        -------
 871        None.
 872
 873        """
 874
 875        # Setup plot
 876        fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
 877            figsize=figsize,
 878            axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
 879            tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
 880            dpi=dpi,
 881        )
 882
 883        # Add electrodes to plot
 884        if plot_electrodes:
 885            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax)
 886
 887        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
 888
 889        # Plot clusters
 890        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
 891            self._plot_cluster_points(
 892                cluster_no,
 893                n_clusters,
 894                ax,
 895                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
 896                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
 897                cmap=cmap,
 898                lw=lw,
 899            )
 900
 901        # Plot centres and covariance regions (if not GMM).
 902        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
 903            self._plot_fibre_location(
 904                cluster_no,
 905                n_clusters,
 906                ax,
 907                (self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm"),
 908                pt_mean_size,
 909                n_sigma,
 910            )
 911
 912        # Plot fitted covariance regions for GMM.
 913        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 914            self._plot_fitted_gmms(ax, n_sigma)
 915
 916        # Plot legend.
 917        if plot_legend:
 918            lgnd = ax.legend(
 919                bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1),
 920                loc="upper left",
 921                frameon=False,
 922                handletextpad=0.25,
 923                fontsize=legend_label_size,
 924            )
 925            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
 926                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
 927                h.set_alpha(1)
 928
 929        # Set y axis limits.
 930        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
 931
 932        # Set x axis limits.
 933        ax.set_xlim(-1, max_x)
 934
 935        # Equal aspect ratio, (this can mess up the axis limits in Windows)
 936        if axis_equal:
 937            ax.axis("equal")
 938
 939    def get_cluster_colour(self, cluster_no: int, n_clusters: int, cmap=None):
 940        """
 941        Return the colour of a cluster depending on the cluster number and
 942        how many total clusters.
 943
 944        Parameters
 945        ----------
 946        cluster_no : int
 947            Number of the cluster.
 948        n_clusters : int
 949            Total number of clusters.
 950        cmap : Colourmap, optional
 951            Use this colour map if given. The default is None.
 952
 953        Returns
 954        -------
 955        Colour
 956
 957        """
 958
 959        if cmap is None:
 960            if n_clusters <= 10:
 961                cmap = colormaps["tab10"].colors
 962            elif n_clusters <= 20:
 963                cmap = colormaps["tab20"].colors
 964            else:
 965                cmap = plt.cm.rainbow(np.linspace(0, 1, n_clusters))
 966        else:  # if colourmap is specified, check that sufficient colours; if not, repeat
 967            if len(cmap) < n_clusters:
 968                cmap = cmap * int(np.ceil(n_clusters / len(cmap)))
 969
 970        return cmap[cluster_no]
 971
 972    def _plot_cluster_points(
 973        self,
 974        cluster_no: int,
 975        n_clusters: int,
 976        ax: Axes,
 977        pt_size: float,
 978        pt_alpha: float,
 979        cmap=None,
 980        lw: float = 0,
 981        threeD: bool = False,
 982    ):
 983        """
 984        Plot all the points for fibre potentials beloging to the same cluster.
 985
 986        Parameters
 987        ----------
 988        cluster_no : int
 989            Number of the cluster.
 990        n_clusters : int
 991            Total number of clusters.
 992        ax : Axes, optional
 993            Plot to add to. The default is None.
 994        pt_alpha : float, optional
 995            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
 996        cmap : Colourmap, optional
 997            Use this colour map if given. The default is None.
 998        lw : float, optional
 999            Line weight. The default is 0.
1000        threeD : bool, optional
1001            If points are plotted on a 3D axis or not (z axis = time in ms). The default
1002            is False.
1003
1004        Returns
1005        -------
1006        None.
1007
1008        """
1009
1010        # Get x and y coords to plot.
1011        x = self.fibre_centres[(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 0]
1012        y = self.fibre_centres[(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1]
1013
1014        # Get z coords to plot if a 3D plot.
1015        if threeD:
1016            N_MS_PER_SEC = 1000
1017            # Determine shift needed to plot MUP onset at t = 0
1018            n_ms = ((self.n_samples_window - 1) / 2) / self.fs * N_MS_PER_SEC
1019
1020            # Fibre potential times
1021            z = (
1022                self.fibre_potential_times[
1023                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no)
1024                ]
1025                / self.fs
1026            ) * N_MS_PER_SEC
1027            z = z - n_ms
1028
1029        # Get colour of points.
1030        pt_facecolor = self.get_cluster_colour(cluster_no, n_clusters, cmap)
1031
1032        # Plot points for this cluster.
1033        if threeD:
1034            ax.scatter(
1035                x,
1036                y,
1037                z,
1038                s=pt_size,
1039                alpha=pt_alpha,
1040                facecolors=pt_facecolor,
1041                linewidth=lw,
1042                label=f"fibre {cluster_no + 1}",
1043            )
1044        else:
1045            ax.scatter(x, y, pt_size, alpha=pt_alpha, facecolors=pt_facecolor, linewidth=lw)
1046
1047    def _plot_fitted_gmms(self, ax: Axes, n_sigma: float):
1048        """
1049        Plot all the points for fibre potentials beloging to the same cluster.
1050
1051        Parameters
1052        ----------
1053        ax : Axes
1054            Plot to add to.
1055        n_sigma : float
1056            Number of standard deviations to plot confidence ellipses.
1057
1058        Returns
1059        -------
1060        None.
1061
1062        """
1063
1064        # Set up covariance matrix depending on which covariance model was used.
1065        cv = self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"]
1066
1067        # Covariance the same for every cluster if "tied".
1068        if self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "tied":
1069            cov = np.array([[cv[0, 0], cv[0, 1]], [cv[1, 0], cv[1, 1]]])
1070
1071        for i, mean in enumerate(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"]):
1072            # Set covariance matrix from fitted GMM.
1073            if self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "diag":
1074                cov = np.array([[cv[i, 0], 0], [0, cv[i, 1]]])
1075            elif self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "spherical":
1076                cov = np.array([[cv[i], 0], [0, cv[i]]])
1077            elif self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "full":
1078                cov = np.array(cv[i])
1079
1080            v, w = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
1081
1082            angle = np.arctan2(w[0][1], w[0][0])
1083            # Convert to degrees
1084            angle = 180.0 * angle / np.pi
1085            # Multiply radius by 2 to get diameter.
1086            v = n_sigma * 2 * np.sqrt(v)
1087            # Define the ellipse and plot it.
1088            ellipse = Ellipse(
1089                mean, v[0], v[1], angle=180.0 + angle, edgecolor="black", facecolor="none"
1090            )
1091            ax.add_artist(ellipse)
1092
1093    def _confidence_ellipse(
1094        self,
1095        x: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1096        y: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1097        ax: Axes,
1098        n_std: float = 3.0,
1099        facecolor="none",
1100        **kwargs,
1101    ):
1102        """
1103        Taken from matplotlib documentation
1104        https://matplotlib.org/stable/gallery/statistics/confidence_ellipse.html
1105
1106        Create a plot of the covariance confidence ellipse of *x* and *y*.
1107
1108        Parameters
1109        ----------
1110        x, y : npt.NDArray[np.float64], shape (n, )
1111            Input data.
1112        ax : Axes
1113            The Axes object to draw the ellipse into.
1114        n_std : float, optional
1115            The number of standard deviations to determine the ellipse's radiuses.
1116            The default is 3.
1117        facecolor : Any, optional
1118            Face color of ellipse. The default is "none".
1119        **kwargs
1120            Forwarded to `~matplotlib.patches.Ellipse`
1121
1122        Returns
1123        -------
1124        None.
1125        """
1126
1127        if x.size != y.size:
1128            raise ValueError("x and y must be the same size")
1129
1130        # No data to do anything with so return!
1131        if len(x) == 0:
1132            return
1133
1134        cov = np.cov(x, y)
1135        pearson = cov[0, 1] / np.sqrt(cov[0, 0] * cov[1, 1])
1136        # Using a special case to obtain the eigenvalues of this
1137        # two-dimensional dataset.
1138        ell_radius_x = np.sqrt(1 + pearson)
1139        ell_radius_y = np.sqrt(1 - pearson)
1140        ellipse = Ellipse(
1141            (0, 0), width=ell_radius_x * 2, height=ell_radius_y * 2, facecolor=facecolor, **kwargs
1142        )
1143
1144        # Calculate the scale of x from
1145        # the standard deviation and multiply
1146        # with the given number of standard deviations.
1147        scale_x = np.sqrt(cov[0, 0]) * n_std
1148        mean_x = np.mean(x)
1149
1150        # Calculate the scale of y.
1151        scale_y = np.sqrt(cov[1, 1]) * n_std
1152        mean_y = np.mean(y)
1153
1154        transf = (
1155            transforms.Affine2D().rotate_deg(45).scale(scale_x, scale_y).translate(mean_x, mean_y)
1156        )
1157
1158        # Return the Axes object with the ellipse drawn on it.
1159        ellipse.set_transform(transf + ax.transData)
1160        ax.add_patch(ellipse)
1161
1162    def _plot_fibre_location(
1163        self,
1164        cluster_no: int,
1165        n_clusters: int,
1166        ax: Axes,
1167        gmm: bool,
1168        pt_mean_size: float = 10,
1169        n_sigma: float = 1,
1170        pt_facecolor=None,
1171    ):
1172        """
1173        Plots estimated fibre location and confidence ellipse.
1174
1175        Parameters
1176        ----------
1177        cluster_no : int
1178            Number of the cluster.
1179        n_clusters : int
1180            Total number of clusters.
1181        ax : Axes
1182            Plot to add to.
1183        gmm : bool
1184            True if clustering method is GMM.
1185        pt_mean_size : float, optional
1186            Size of mean points. The default is 10.
1187        n_sigma : float, optional
1188            Number of standard deviations for confidence ellipse. The default is 1.
1189        pt_facecolor : Any, optional
1190            Face colour of points, The default is None.
1191
1192        Returns
1193        -------
1194        None.
1195
1196        """
1197
1198        if gmm:
1199            center = self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"][cluster_no]
1200        else:
1201            x = np.array(
1202                self.fibre_centres[
1203                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 0
1204                ]
1205            )
1206            y = np.array(
1207                self.fibre_centres[
1208                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1
1209                ]
1210            )
1211            center = np.array([[np.mean(x)], [np.mean(y)]])
1212
1213        if pt_facecolor is None:
1214            pt_facecolor = self.get_cluster_colour(cluster_no, n_clusters)
1215
1216        ax.scatter(
1217            center[0],
1218            center[1],
1219            pt_mean_size,
1220            color=pt_facecolor,
1221            edgecolors="black",
1222            label=f"fibre {cluster_no + 1}",
1223        )
1224
1225        if not gmm:
1226            self._confidence_ellipse(x, y, ax, n_sigma, edgecolor="black")
1227
1228    def plot_3D_fibre_potential_clustering(
1229        self,
1230        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
1231        pt_potentials_size: float = 10,
1232        pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4,
1233        axis_equal: bool = True,
1234        lw: float = 0.5,
1235        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
1236        axis_label_size: float = 14,
1237        tick_label_size: float = 12,
1238        dpi: int = 100,
1239        cmap=None,
1240        max_y: float = 1,
1241        y_buff: float = 1.75,
1242        plot_legend: bool = True,
1243        legend_pt_size: float = 50,
1244        legend_label_size: float = 12,
1245        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1246    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
1247        """
1248        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
1249        (one point per potential) with z-axis corresponding to the time of each fibre
1250        potential in the motor unit potential (t = 0 ms is MUP onset).
1251
1252        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
1253
1254        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
1255
1256        Parameters
1257        ----------
1258        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
1259            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
1260        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
1261            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
1262        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
1263            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
1264        axis_equal : bool, optional
1265            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
1266        lw : float, optional
1267            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
1268        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
1269            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
1270        axis_label_size : float, optional
1271            size of axis label. The default is 14.
1272        tick_label_size : float, optional
1273            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
1274        dpi : int, optional
1275            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
1276        cmap : Any, optional
1277            Colour map to use. The default is None.
1278        max_y : float, optional
1279            The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute
1280            y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure
1281            that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
1282        y_buff: float, optional
1283            Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to
1284            determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points
1285            along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
1286        plot_legend : bool, optional
1287            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
1288        legend_pt_size : float, optional
1289            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
1290        legend_label_size: float, optional
1291            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
1292        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1293            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1294
1295        Returns
1296        -------
1297        None.
1298
1299        """
1300
1301        # Setup plot.
1302        if ax is None:
1303            fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
1304                figsize=figsize,
1305                axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
1306                tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
1307                dpi=dpi,
1308                threeD=True,
1309            )
1310        else:
1311            fig = None
1312
1313            # Add axis and tick labels.
1314            ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1315            ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1316            ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1317            ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1318            ax.set_zlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
1319            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1320
1321        # Determine z axis limits based on window used to compute motor unit potentials.
1322        N_MS_PER_SEC = 1000
1323        n_ms = (
1324            ((self.n_samples_window - 1) / 2) / self.fs * N_MS_PER_SEC
1325        )  # shift to plot MUP onset at t=0
1326        max_z = n_ms
1327
1328        # Add electrodes to plot at bottom.
1329        if plot_electrodes:
1330            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax, z=-max_z, clr="grey", marker_size=5)
1331
1332        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1333
1334        # Keep track of max absolute y position to ensure data is not cut off by axis limits.
1335        fibre_max_y = 0
1336
1337        # Plot each cluster.
1338        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
1339            self._plot_cluster_points(
1340                cluster_no,
1341                n_clusters,
1342                ax,
1343                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
1344                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
1345                cmap=cmap,
1346                lw=lw,
1347                threeD=True,
1348            )
1349            # Max y
1350            mu_max_y = np.max(
1351                np.abs(
1352                    self.fibre_centres[
1353                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1
1354                    ]
1355                )
1356            )
1357            fibre_max_y = max(fibre_max_y, mu_max_y)
1358
1359        # Add legend.
1360        if plot_legend:
1361            lgnd = ax.legend(
1362                bbox_to_anchor=(1.2, 1.0),
1363                loc="upper left",
1364                frameon=False,
1365                handletextpad=0.25,
1366                fontsize=legend_label_size,
1367            )
1368            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
1369                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
1370                h.set_alpha(1)
1371
1372        # Set y axis and z-axis limits.
1373        max_y = max(fibre_max_y * y_buff, max_y)  # Adjust max_y based on data
1374        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
1375        ax.set_zlim(-max_z, max_z)
1376
1377        # Equal aspect ratio for x and y coordinates
1378        if axis_equal:
1379            ax.set_aspect("equalxy", adjustable="box")
1380
1381        return fig, ax
1382
1383    def remove_outliers_iqr(
1384        self, intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1385    ) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int64], int]:
1386        """
1387        Parameters
1388        ----------
1389        intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int]
1390            Array of time intervals.
1391
1392        Returns
1393        -------
1394        npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1395            Array of time intervals with outliers removed.
1396
1397        """
1398
1399        # Calculate interquartile range.
1400        q25, q75 = np.nanpercentile(intervals, 25), np.nanpercentile(intervals, 75)
1401        iqr = q75 - q25
1402
1403        # Calculate the outlier cutoff.
1404        cut_off = iqr * 1.5
1405        lower, upper = q25 - cut_off, q75 + cut_off
1406
1407        # Replace outliers with nan.
1408        ans = np.array([np.nan if x < lower or x > upper else x for x in intervals])
1409        num_of_outliers = np.count_nonzero(((intervals < lower) | (intervals > upper)))
1410
1411        return ans, num_of_outliers
1412
1413    def _calculate_fibre_potentials_time_diff(self, fib_pot_pos1: int, fib_pot_pos2: int) -> int:
1414        """
1415        Parameters
1416        ----------
1417        fib_pot_pos1: int
1418            Index of the first fibre potential in fibre_potential_times.
1419        fib_pot_pos2: int
1420            Index of the second fibre potential in fibre_potential_times.
1421
1422        Returns
1423        -------
1424        int
1425            Length of time interval between the two fibre potentials
1426            returned as a multiple of the number of time steps i.e. indices.
1427
1428        """
1429
1430        return np.abs(
1431            self.fibre_potential_times[fib_pot_pos2] - self.fibre_potential_times[fib_pot_pos1]
1432        )
1433
1434    def _jitter_analysis_between_two_fibres(
1435        self, fibre1_num: int, fibre2_num: int
1436    ) -> tuple[
1437        float,
1438        float,
1439        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1440        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1441        int,
1442        int,
1443        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1444        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1445    ]:
1446        """
1447        Performs jitter analysis for this motor unit (MU). For the identified
1448        fibres computes the mean consecutive difference (MCD) between each pair
1449        of fibre. Firstly one fibre potential is chosen for each fibre and
1450        then the time difference is taken between them for the first MUP.
1451        This time interval is compared with the time interval for the next MUP
1452        by taking the absolute difference - and so on until the second last MUP.
1453        The mean of these differences is the MCD.
1454
1455        MCD = (1/(N-1)) * sum(|D_k - D_{k+1}|) for k = 1 to N-1, where D_k is the kth
1456        MUP time difference between the fibre potentials for the 2 fibres in question.
1457
1458        The median value of D_k is also recorded to hopefully better account for
1459        the poor quality of data.
1460
1461        Parameters
1462        ----------
1463        fibre1_num : int
1464            Fibre number for the first fibre, given previously from cluster analysis (0,1,2,...).
1465        fibre2_num : int
1466            Fibre number for the second fibre.
1467        remove_outliers: bool
1468            Remove outliers in fibre potential times to avoid probable miss-classifications
1469
1470        Returns
1471        -------
1472        tuple[float,
1473            float,
1474            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1475            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1476            int,
1477            int,
1478            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1479            npt.NDArray[np.int64]]
1480
1481        """
1482
1483        # Calculate medians of all the fibre potentials for fibre 1 and fibre 2.
1484        all_fibre1_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1485            (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre1_num)
1486        )
1487        median_time1 = np.median(self.fibre_potential_times[all_fibre1_potentials_idx])
1488
1489        all_fibre2_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1490            (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre2_num)
1491        )
1492        median_time2 = np.median(self.fibre_potential_times[all_fibre2_potentials_idx])
1493
1494        # Length of time intervals between fibre potentials in the two different fibres.
1495        fibre_potential_time_diffs = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1496
1497        # Taken note of how many outliers there are and which fibre potentials
1498        # were used.
1499        number_of_differences_outliers = 0
1500        number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = 0
1501        fibre1_pots_used_idx = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1502        fibre2_pots_used_idx = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1503
1504        # Compute length of time intervals between fibre potentials.
1505        for mup_num in range(self.n_potentials):
1506            mup_onset_idx = self.potentials_t_idx[mup_num]
1507
1508            # Fibre potentials that belong to the specified MUP and fibre (cluster).
1509            fibre1_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1510                np.all(
1511                    (
1512                        (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset_idx),
1513                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre1_num),
1514                    ),
1515                    axis=0,
1516                )
1517            )
1518
1519            fibre2_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1520                np.all(
1521                    (
1522                        (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset_idx),
1523                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre2_num),
1524                    ),
1525                    axis=0,
1526                )
1527            )
1528
1529            if len(fibre1_potentials_idx) > 0 and len(fibre2_potentials_idx) > 0:
1530                # Pick fibre potentials closest to the medians.
1531                fibre1_potential_to_use = np.argmin(
1532                    np.abs(median_time1 - self.fibre_potential_times[fibre1_potentials_idx])
1533                )
1534                fibre2_potential_to_use = np.argmin(
1535                    np.abs(median_time2 - self.fibre_potential_times[fibre2_potentials_idx])
1536                )
1537
1538                # Get time difference for this MUP between fibre potentials.
1539                fib_pot_pos1 = fibre1_potentials_idx[fibre1_potential_to_use]
1540                fib_pot_pos2 = fibre2_potentials_idx[fibre2_potential_to_use]
1541                fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num] = self._calculate_fibre_potentials_time_diff(
1542                    fib_pot_pos1, fib_pot_pos2
1543                )
1544
1545                # Record which fibre potentials were used to look into later, if desired.
1546                # Note that these fibres include outliers
1547                fibre1_pots_used_idx[mup_num] = fib_pot_pos1
1548                fibre2_pots_used_idx[mup_num] = fib_pot_pos2
1549
1550        # Remove outliers in time intervals.
1551        if self.mu_jitter_settings.remove_outliers:
1552            fibre_potential_time_diffs, number_of_differences_outliers = self.remove_outliers_iqr(
1553                fibre_potential_time_diffs
1554            )
1555
1556        # Compute consecutive differences.
1557        consecutive_diffs = np.full((self.n_potentials - 1), np.nan)
1558
1559        # Loop thro' MUPs.
1560        for mup_num in range(self.n_potentials - 1):
1561            if not np.isnan(fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num]) and not np.isnan(
1562                fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num + 1]
1563            ):
1564                consecutive_diffs[mup_num] = np.abs(
1565                    fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num] - fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num + 1]
1566                )
1567
1568        # Remove outliers.
1569        if self.mu_jitter_settings.remove_outliers:
1570            consecutive_diffs, number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = self.remove_outliers_iqr(
1571                consecutive_diffs
1572            )
1573
1574        # Compute mean consecutive difference.
1575        mean_consecutive_diff = np.nanmean(consecutive_diffs)
1576
1577        # Compute median of consecutive differences.
1578        median_consecutive_diff = np.nanmedian(consecutive_diffs)
1579
1580        # Return many results for the jitter analysis.
1581        return (
1582            mean_consecutive_diff,
1583            median_consecutive_diff,
1584            fibre_potential_time_diffs,
1585            consecutive_diffs,
1586            number_of_differences_outliers,
1587            number_of_cons_diffs_outliers,
1588            fibre1_pots_used_idx,
1589            fibre2_pots_used_idx,
1590        )
1591
1592    def jitter_analysis(self, mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings):
1593        """
1594        Calculate jitter between all pairs of fibres.
1595        For each fibre pair:
1596        Firstly a vector of time differences (intervals) are
1597        calculated, one interval for each MUP. If there is more than one fibre
1598        potential assigned to a fibre for a MUP then the one that is closest to the
1599        median (over all fibre potentials in that fibre) is chose. If there are no
1600        fibre potentials for that fibre and MUP then an interval cannot be record so
1601        is NAN.
1602        Secondly, the consecutive differences are calculated, the difference
1603        between intervals that are in adjacent MUPs. If an interval does not exist
1604        then NAN is recorded.
1605        Finally, the mean consecutive differences is calculated to measure the jitter.
1606        The median consecutive differences is also calculated to try and account
1607        for poor data.
1608
1609        Parameters
1610        ----------
1611        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1612            The setting to use for the jitter analysis.
1613
1614        Returns
1615        -------
1616        None.
1617
1618        """
1619
1620        # Set jitter settings.
1621        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
1622
1623        # Check that localisation and fibre clustering has been run.
1624        if (
1625            not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]
1626            or not self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]
1627        ):
1628            raise RuntimeError(
1629                "Localisation analysis and fibre cluster analysis"
1630                + "must be performed before jitter analysis!"
1631            )
1632
1633        # Check there is data to do the calculation.
1634        if self.n_potentials < 2:
1635            raise RuntimeError("Not enough MUPs to perform jitter analysis!")
1636
1637        # Get the number of clusters.
1638        n_fibre_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1639
1640        # The number of jitter calculations to do between fibres.
1641        number_of_jitter_calcs = int(n_fibre_clusters * (n_fibre_clusters - 1) / 2)
1642
1643        # Calculations to report.
1644        fibre1_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1645        fibre2_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1646        mean_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1647        median_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1648        fibre_potential_time_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1649        consecutive_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials - 1))
1650        number_of_differences = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1651        number_of_cons_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1652        number_of_differences_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1653        number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1654        fibre1_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1655        fibre2_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1656
1657        # Loop thro' each fibre pair and perform the jitter analysis.
1658        # Fibre pair count.
1659        count = 0
1660        for fibre1_num in range(n_fibre_clusters - 1):
1661            for fibre2_num in np.arange(fibre1_num + 1, n_fibre_clusters):
1662                # Do jitter analysis between fibre1 and fibre2.
1663                (
1664                    mean_consecutive_diffs[count],
1665                    median_consecutive_diffs[count],
1666                    fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :],
1667                    consecutive_diffs[count, :],
1668                    number_of_differences_outliers[count],
1669                    number_of_cons_diffs_outliers[count],
1670                    fibre1_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1671                    fibre2_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1672                ) = self._jitter_analysis_between_two_fibres(fibre1_num, fibre2_num)
1673
1674                # Record fibres analysed and some data counts.
1675                fibre1_numbers[count] = fibre1_num
1676                fibre2_numbers[count] = fibre2_num
1677                number_of_differences[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1678                    ~np.isnan(fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :])
1679                )
1680                number_of_cons_diffs[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1681                    ~np.isnan(consecutive_diffs[count, :])
1682                )
1683                count += 1
1684
1685        # Record final jitter analysis results in dictionary.
1686        self.fibre_jitter_results = {
1687            "fibre1_numbers": fibre1_numbers,
1688            "fibre2_numbers": fibre2_numbers,
1689            "mean_consecutive_diffs": mean_consecutive_diffs,
1690            "median_consecutive_diffs": median_consecutive_diffs,
1691            "differences": fibre_potential_time_diffs,
1692            "consecutive_diffs": consecutive_diffs,
1693            "number_of_differences": number_of_differences,
1694            "number_of_differences_outliers": number_of_differences_outliers,
1695            "number_of_cons_diffs": number_of_cons_diffs,
1696            "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": number_of_cons_diffs_outliers,
1697            "fibre1_pots_used_idx": fibre1_pots_used_idx,
1698            "fibre2_pots_used_idx": fibre2_pots_used_idx,
1699        }
1700
1701        # Record that the jitter analysis has been performed for this motor unit.
1702        self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = True
1703
1704    def get_fibre_jitter_dict(self) -> dict:
1705        """
1706        Returns dictionary of fibre jitter results so that it can be saved.
1707
1708        Parameters
1709        ----------
1710        None.
1711
1712        Returns
1713        -------
1714        dict
1715
1716        """
1717
1718        # If jitter analysis is not done then return empty dictionary.
1719        if self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
1720            fibre_jitter_dict = {
1721                "fibre1_numbers": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"].tolist(),
1722                "fibre2_numbers": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"].tolist(),
1723                "mean_consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1724                    "mean_consecutive_diffs"
1725                ].tolist(),
1726                "median_consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1727                    "median_consecutive_diffs"
1728                ].tolist(),
1729                "differences": self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"].tolist(),
1730                "consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"].tolist(),
1731                "number_of_differences": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1732                    "number_of_differences"
1733                ].tolist(),
1734                "number_of_differences_outliers": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1735                    "number_of_differences_outliers"
1736                ].tolist(),
1737                "number_of_cons_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results["number_of_cons_diffs"].tolist(),
1738                "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1739                    "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers"
1740                ].tolist(),
1741                "fibre1_pots_used_idx": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_pots_used_idx"].tolist(),
1742                "fibre2_pots_used_idx": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_pots_used_idx"].tolist(),
1743            }
1744        else:
1745            fibre_jitter_dict = {}
1746
1747        return fibre_jitter_dict
1748
1749    def set_fibre_jitter_from_dict(
1750        self, fibre_jitter_dict: dict, mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1751    ):
1752        """
1753        Sets fibre jitter results from loaded jitter results.
1754
1755        Parameters
1756        ----------
1757        fibre_jitter_dict : dict
1758            Dictionary containing saved results of jitter analysis.
1759
1760        mu_jitter_settings : EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1761            Copy of settings used to do jitter analysis.
1762
1763        Returns
1764        -------
1765        None.
1766
1767        """
1768
1769        # Check jitter analysis results are saved.
1770        if fibre_jitter_dict:
1771            self.fibre_jitter_results = {
1772                "fibre1_numbers": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre1_numbers"]),
1773                "fibre2_numbers": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre2_numbers"]),
1774                "mean_consecutive_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["mean_consecutive_diffs"]),
1775                "median_consecutive_diffs": np.array(
1776                    fibre_jitter_dict["median_consecutive_diffs"]
1777                ),
1778                "differences": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["differences"]),
1779                "consecutive_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["consecutive_diffs"]),
1780                "number_of_differences": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_differences"]),
1781                "number_of_differences_outliers": np.array(
1782                    fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_differences_outliers"]
1783                ),
1784                "number_of_cons_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_cons_diffs"]),
1785                "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": np.array(
1786                    fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_cons_diffs_outliers"]
1787                ),
1788                "fibre1_pots_used_idx": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre1_pots_used_idx"]),
1789                "fibre2_pots_used_idx": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre2_pots_used_idx"]),
1790            }
1791
1792            # Note analysis performed.
1793            self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = True
1794
1795            self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
1796
1797    def plot_fibre_potential_time_diffs(
1798        self, fibre1_num: int, fibre2_num: int, display_counts: bool = True
1799    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
1800        """
1801        Plot a histogram for time differences between fibre potentials.
1802
1803        Parameters
1804        ----------
1805        fibre1_num : int
1806            Fibre number for the first fibre, given previously from cluster analysis (0,1,2,...).
1807        fibre2_num : int
1808            Fibre number for the second fibre.
1809        display_counts : bool, optional
1810            Display amount of non nan data used in histograms on plot. The default is True.
1811
1812        Returns
1813        -------
1814        fig : Figure
1815            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1816        ax : Axes
1817            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1818
1819        """
1820
1821        # Get index for this pair of fibres so that the results can be retreived.
1822        res_idx0 = np.where(
1823            np.all(
1824                (
1825                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"] == fibre1_num),
1826                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"] == fibre2_num),
1827                ),
1828                axis=0,
1829            )
1830        )
1831
1832        # Create plot.
1833        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
1834
1835        if len(res_idx0) > 0:
1836            res_idx = res_idx0[0]
1837        else:
1838            print(f"Jitter results not found for fibres {fibre1_num + 1} and {fibre2_num + 1}!")
1839            return fig, ax
1840
1841        # Get fibre differences and convert to time in seconds.
1842        fibre_pot_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"][res_idx, :] / self.fs
1843        fibre_pot_diffs = fibre_pot_diffs.flatten()
1844
1845        # Plot histogram.
1846        if not np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs).all():
1847            ax.hist(
1848                fibre_pot_diffs,
1849                bins=30,
1850                density=True,
1851                color="lightgrey",
1852                edgecolor="k",
1853                linewidth=0.5,
1854            )
1855
1856        plt.title(
1857            f"Fibre Potential Intervals (Motor Unit {self.motor_unit_number+1}"
1858            + f", Fibres {fibre1_num+1} and {fibre2_num+1})"
1859        )
1860
1861        # Add mean and standard deviation info to plot.
1862        mean = np.nanmean(fibre_pot_diffs)
1863        st_dev = np.nanstd(fibre_pot_diffs, ddof=1)
1864        textstr = "\n".join(
1865            (
1866                r"Mean $= %.0f$ " % (mean * 1e6,) + "\u03bcs",
1867                r"St. dev. $=%.0f$ " % (st_dev * 1e6,) + "\u03bcs",
1868            )
1869        )
1870
1871        # These are matplotlib.patch.Patch properties.
1872        props = dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="wheat", alpha=0.5)
1873
1874        # Place a text box in upper left in axes coords.
1875        ax.text(
1876            0.05,
1877            0.95,
1878            textstr,
1879            transform=ax.transAxes,
1880            fontsize=14,
1881            verticalalignment="top",
1882            bbox=props,
1883        )
1884
1885        # Display counts and percent.
1886        if display_counts:
1887            total_diffs = len(fibre_pot_diffs)
1888            total_non_nan_diffs = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs))
1889            percent = (total_non_nan_diffs / total_diffs) * 100
1890            textstr = (
1891                r"MUPs $= %d$" % (total_diffs,)
1892                + "\n"
1893                + r"Used $=%d (%0.2f$"
1894                % (
1895                    total_non_nan_diffs,
1896                    percent,
1897                )
1898                + r"$\%$)"
1899            )
1900
1901            # Place a text box in upper right in axes coords.
1902            ax.text(
1903                0.95,
1904                0.95,
1905                textstr,
1906                transform=ax.transAxes,
1907                fontsize=14,
1908                verticalalignment="top",
1909                horizontalalignment="right",
1910                bbox=props,
1911            )
1912
1913        return fig, ax
