2034    def plot_jitter_heat_plot(
2035        self,
2036        median: bool = False,
2037        cmap: Any = "magma",
2038        vmax: float = 100,
2039        clr_background: Any = "dimgrey",
2040        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
2041    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
2042        """
2043        Plot a heat map of mean consecutive differences (MCDs) between fibres.
2044        (Or medians of consecutive differences)
2045
2046        Parameters
2047        ----------
2048        median : bool, optional
2049            Plot medians instead of mean consecutive differences. The default is False.
2050        cmap : matplotlib colormap name or object, or list of colors, optional
2051            Colourmap. The default is matplotlib colourmap "magma".
2052        vmax : float, optional
2053            The upper limit for the colourmap, in microseconds. This argument ensures
2054            that outliers do not dramatically skew the colourmap and that colours are
2055            easily comparable across motor units. The default is 100.
2056        clr_background: colour specification, optional
2057            Colour for plot background (recommend similar darkness to low values of the
2058            colourmap). The default is "dimgrey".
2059        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
2060            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
2061
2062        Returns
2063        -------
2064        fig : Figure | None
2065            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2066        ax : matplotlib Axes
2067            Axes object with the heatmap.
2068        """
2069
2070        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2071        if ax is None:
2072            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
2073        else:
2074            fig = None
2075
2076        # Get number of fibre pairs; return early if none.
2077        n_fibre_pairs = len(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"])
2078        if n_fibre_pairs == 0:
2079            ax.set_axis_off()  # remove plot axes
2080            return fig, ax
2081
2082        n_fibres = int(np.max(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"]) + 1)
2083
2084        # Create data array for the heat plot.
2085        data = np.full((n_fibres, n_fibres), np.nan)
2086
2087        for i in range(n_fibre_pairs):
2088            fib1 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"][i])
2089            fib2 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"][i])
2090
2091            if median:
2092                val = self.fibre_jitter_results["median_consecutive_diffs"][i]
2093            else:
2094                val = self.fibre_jitter_results["mean_consecutive_diffs"][i]
2095
2096            # Convert indices to micro seconds.
2097            if not np.isnan(val):
2098                val = int((val / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2099
2100            # Make heat plot symetrical.
2101            data[fib1, fib2] = val
2102            data[fib2, fib1] = val
2103
2104        # Plotting the heatmap.
2105        str_fibres = [str(x) for x in np.arange(1, n_fibres + 1)]
2106
2107        ax = sns.heatmap(
2108            data=data,
2109            vmin=0,
2110            vmax=vmax,
2111            cmap=cmap,
2112            annot=True,
2113            xticklabels=str_fibres,
2114            yticklabels=str_fibres,
2115            cbar_kws={"label": "\u03bc seconds"},
2116            fmt="g",
2117            ax=ax,
2118        )
2119
2120        ax.set_xlabel("fibre number")
2121        ax.set_ylabel("fibre number")
2122
2123        # Titles (line break ensures that plot is the same size as plot_jitter_heat_plot,
2124        # which has a two line title)
2125        if median:
2126            ax.set_title(
2127                f"Median Consecutive Differences\n(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2128                fontweight="bold",
2129            )
2130        else:
2131            ax.set_title(
2132                f"Mean Consecutive Differences\n(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2133                fontweight="bold",
2134            )
2135
2136        # Ensure square, change background colour, and add frame
2137        ax.set_aspect("equal")
2138        ax.set_facecolor(clr_background)
2139        for _, spine in ax.spines.items():
2140            spine.set_visible(True)
2141
2142        return fig, ax
2143
2144    def _get_jitter_totals(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> tuple[int, float, int, float]:
2145        """
2146        Gets counts (and percentage) of non nan time intervals (between fibre potentials)
2147        and consecutive differences between fibres fibre1 and fibre2
2148
2149        Parameters
2150        ----------
2151        fibre1 : int
2152            Index of fibre1.
2153        fibre2 : int
2154            Index of fibre2.
2155
2156        Returns
2157        -------
2158        tuple[int, float, int, float]
2159
2160        """
2161
2162        # Get index for this pair of fibres so that the results can be retreived.
2163        res_idx0 = np.where(
2164            np.all(
2165                (
2166                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"] == fibre1),
2167                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"] == fibre2),
2168                ),
2169                axis=0,
2170            )
2171        )
2172
2173        if len(res_idx0) > 0:
2174            res_idx = res_idx0[0]
2175        else:
2176            print(f"Jitter results not found for fibres {fibre1 + 1} and {fibre2 + 1}!")
2177            return 0, 0, 0, 0
2178
2179        # Get fibre differences.
2180        fibre_pot_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"][res_idx, :]
2181        fibre_pot_diffs = fibre_pot_diffs.flatten()
2182
2183        total_diffs = len(fibre_pot_diffs)
2184        total_non_nan_diffs = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs))
2185        percent_df = round((total_non_nan_diffs / total_diffs) * 100, 2)
2186
2187        # Get consecutive differences.
2188        consecutive_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][res_idx, :]
2189        consecutive_diffs = consecutive_diffs.flatten()
2190
2191        con_diffs = len(consecutive_diffs)
2192        total_non_nan_cd = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(consecutive_diffs))
2193        percent_cd = round((total_non_nan_cd / con_diffs) * 100, 2)
2194
2195        return total_non_nan_diffs, percent_df, total_non_nan_cd, percent_cd
2196
2197    def plot_jitter_totals_heat_plot(
2198        self,
2199        percent: bool = False,
2200        cmap: Any = "viridis",
2201        clr_background: Any = "dimgrey",
2202        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
2203    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
2204        """
2205        Plot a heat map of counts (= number of consecutive differences) used for jitter
2206        analysis.
2207
2208        Parameters
2209        ----------
2210        percent: bool, optional
2211            Plot percentage of non-nan counts of consecutive differences, otherwise plot
2212            the counts. The default is False.
2213        cmap : matplotlib colormap name or object, or list of colors, optional
2214            Colourmap. The default is matplotlib colourmap "viridis".
2215        clr_background: colour specification, optional
2216            Colour for plot background (recommend similar darkness to low values of the
2217            colourmap). The default is "dimgrey".
2218        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
2219            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
2220
2221        Returns
2222        -------
2223
2224        fig : Figure | None
2225            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2226        ax : matplotlib Axes
2227            Axes object with the heatmap.
2228
2229        """
2230
2231        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2232        if ax is None:
2233            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
2234        else:
2235            fig = None
2236
2237        # Get number of fibre pairs; return early if none.
2238        n_fibre_pairs = len(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"])
2239        if n_fibre_pairs == 0:
2240            ax.set_axis_off()  # remove plot axes
2241            return fig, ax
2242
2243        n_fibres = int(np.max(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"]) + 1)
2244
2245        # Create array for heat plot.
2246        data = np.full((n_fibres, n_fibres), np.nan)
2247
2248        for i in range(n_fibre_pairs):
2249            fib1 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"][i])
2250            fib2 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"][i])
2251
2252            (
2253                _,
2254                _,
2255                total_non_nan_cd,
2256                percent_cd,
2257            ) = self._get_jitter_totals(fib1, fib2)
2258
2259            # Set values for heat plot (symmetric)
2260            if percent:
2261                data[fib1, fib2] = percent_cd
2262                data[fib2, fib1] = percent_cd
2263            else:
2264                data[fib1, fib2] = total_non_nan_cd  # number of consecutive differences
2265                data[fib2, fib1] = total_non_nan_cd
2266
2267        # Plotting the heatmap.
2268        str_fibres = [str(x) for x in np.arange(1, n_fibres + 1)]
2269
2270        if percent:
2271            bar_str = "percent"
2272        else:
2273            bar_str = "count"
2274
2275        ax = sns.heatmap(
2276            data=data,
2277            vmin=0,
2278            cmap=cmap,
2279            annot=True,
2280            xticklabels=str_fibres,
2281            yticklabels=str_fibres,
2282            cbar_kws={"label": bar_str},
2283            fmt="g",
2284            ax=ax,
2285        )
2286
2287        ax.set_xlabel("fibre number")
2288        ax.set_ylabel("fibre number")
2289
2290        if percent:
2291            ax.set_title(
2292                "Sample sizes (% of consecutive differences)\n"
2293                + f"(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2294                fontweight="bold",
2295            )
2296        else:
2297            ax.set_title(
2298                "Sample sizes (# consecutive differences)\n"
2299                + f"(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2300                fontweight="bold",
2301            )
2302
2303        # Ensure square, change background colour, and add frame
2304        ax.set_aspect("equal")
2305        ax.set_facecolor(clr_background)
2306        for _, spine in ax.spines.items():
2307            spine.set_visible(True)
2308
2309        return fig, ax

2311    def get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> int | None:
2312        """
2313        Get index of requested fibre pair in the motor unit's jitter results
2314        (fibre_jitter_results attribute). Will return None if the fibre pair is not an
2315        option or if there are multiple matches for that fibre pair in the jitter
2316        results (which should only arrise if there is an error in the analysis code).
2317
2318        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2319
2320        Parameters
2321        ----------
2322        fibre1 : int
2323            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2324        fibre2 : int
2325            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2326
2327        Raises
2328        ------
2329        ValueError
2330            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit.
2331
2332        Returns
2333        -------
2334        fibre_pair_idx : int | None
2335            Index of the specified fibre; can use for extracting the corresponding
2336            results in the motor unit's jitter analysis results. Is None if fibre pair
2337            is not a valid option.
2338        """
2339
2340        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2341        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2342            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2343        else:
2344            # Jitter results
2345            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results
2346
2347        # Determine which fields in jitter_results to use for each fibre
2348        # Lower fibre number is stored in fibre1 results, while higher value is fibre2
2349        if fibre1 < fibre2:
2350            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2351            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2352        else:
2353            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2354            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2355
2356        # Determine index of results for that fibre pair
2357        fibre_pair_idx_bool = np.all(
2358            [
2359                jitter_results[fibre1_numbers_field] == fibre1,
2360                jitter_results[fibre2_numbers_field] == fibre2,
2361            ],
2362            axis=0,
2363        )
2364
2365        # Compute number of matches; if not exactly 1, return None
2366        n_fibre_pair_matches = sum(fibre_pair_idx_bool)
2367        if n_fibre_pair_matches == 1:
2368            fibre_pair_idx = np.flatnonzero(fibre_pair_idx_bool)[0]
2369        else:
2370            fibre_pair_idx = None
2371
2372        # Return fibre pair index
2373        return fibre_pair_idx
2374
2375    def _get_jitter_analysed_mups_and_fibres(
2376        self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int
2377    ) -> (npt.NDArray[np.bool_], npt.NDArray[np.float64]):
2378        """
2379        Returns
2380
2381        1) boolean array of which motor unit potentials were included in the jitter
2382           computation for the specified fibre pair
2383
2384        and
2385
2386        2) float array of the indices (in self.fibre_potential_times)
2387           of the fibre potentials in each motor unit that were used to compute the
2388           jitter of that fibre pair. Float array is used so the indices are nan if that
2389           motor unit potential was not analysed.
2390
2391        Note that MUPs that may have been removed by outlier detection are still marked
2392        as True (= analysed).
2393
2394        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2395
2396        Parameters
2397        ----------
2398        fibre1 : int
2399            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2400        fibre2 : int
2401            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2402
2403        Raises
2404        ------
2405        ValueError
2406            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit.
2407
2408        Returns
2409        -------
2410        analysed_mup : npt.NDArray[np.bool_]
2411            Boolean numpy array of which motor unit potentials were included in the
2412            jitter analysis for this fibre pair. MUPs that produced outlier values are
2413            still included. Shape is (self.n_potentials,).
2414
2415        analysed_fibres_idx : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
2416            Float array of the indices (in self.fibre_potential_times)
2417            of the fibre potentials in each motor unit that were used to compute the
2418            jitter of that fibre pair. The index is set to nan if that motor unit
2419            potential was not analysed. Shape is (2, self.n_potentials), with row 1
2420            corresponding to fibre1 and row 2 corresponding to fibre2.
2421
2422        """
2423
2424        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2425        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2426            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2427        else:
2428            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results  # jitter results dictionary
2429
2430        # Get fibre pair index in jitter results
2431        fibre_pair_idx = self.get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(fibre1, fibre2)
2432
2433        # Initialise array for storing which MUPs were analysed
2434        analysed_mup = np.full(self.n_potentials, False)
2435
2436        # Need to append and prepend NaN to consecutive differences array to determine which
2437        # MUPs are used (since each consecutive difference corresponds to two MUPs)
2438        nan1 = np.isnan(np.append(jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx, :], np.nan))
2439        nan2 = np.isnan(
2440            np.append(np.array(np.nan), jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx, :])
2441        )
2442
2443        # If not nan in at least one, that MUP was analysed
2444        analysed_mup[np.any([~nan1, ~nan2], axis=0)] = True
2445
2446        # Get indices of fibre 1 and fibre 2 (in fibre_potential_times/fibre_potential_peak_chan)
2447        # for each MUP that was analysed.
2448        # First need to determine which fields in jitter_results to use for each fibre
2449        # Lower fibre number is stored in fibre1 results, while higher value is fibre2
2450        if fibre1 < fibre2:
2451            fibre1_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre1_pots_used_idx"
2452            fibre2_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre2_pots_used_idx"
2453        else:
2454            fibre2_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre1_pots_used_idx"
2455            fibre1_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre2_pots_used_idx"
2456
2457        analysed_fibres_idx = np.vstack(
2458            (
2459                jitter_results[fibre1_pots_used_idx_field][fibre_pair_idx, :],
2460                jitter_results[fibre2_pots_used_idx_field][fibre_pair_idx, :],
2461            )
2462        )
2463        analysed_fibres_idx[:, ~analysed_mup] = np.nan  # Set to nan if fibre not analysed
2464
2465        return analysed_mup, analysed_fibres_idx
2466
2467    def plot_jitter_fibre_pair_EMG_and_times(
2468        self,
2469        fibre1: int,
2470        fibre2: int,
2471        fibre_clrs: list[Any] | None = None,
2472        emg_line_lw: float = 1,
2473        emg_line_alpha: float = 0.25,
2474        emg_y_perc: float = 95,
2475        emg_y_buff_prop: float = 0.2,
2476        time_marker_size: float = 2,
2477        align_times_to_fibre1: bool = True,
2478        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 10),
2479        axis_label_size: float = 12,
2480        title_size: float = 12,
2481        dpi: int = 100,
2482        downsample_factor: int = 1,
2483    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes | None]:
2484        """
2485        Creates a figure that visualises the jitter analysis of the specified fibre
2486        pair, fibre1 and fibre2. The figure contains three subplots: the EMG traces of
2487        fibre1's and fibre2's potentials (in separate plots) and a raster plot of the
2488        times of the potentials in each motor unit potential. The x-axes of the plots
2489        are aligned.
2490
2491        By default, all times are relative to the timing of fibre1's
2492        potentials in each motor unit.
2493
2494        If there are no jitter results for that fibre pair (e.g., if there were no
2495        consecutive motor unit potentials containing potentials for both fibres),
2496        returns (None, None) instead of the figure and axes.
2497
2498        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2499
2500        Note that these plots still visualise outlier differences that may be removed
2501        from the final mean consecutive difference calculation.
2502
2503        Parameters
2504        ----------
2505        fibre1 : int
2506            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2507        fibre2 : int
2508            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2509        fibre_clrs : list[Any] | None, optional
2510            List, length two, indicate the colour for the EMG traces for each fibre.
2511            The default is None, in which case default colours (using CartoColor's
2512            "Geyser" palette) are set.
2513        emg_line_lw : float, optional
2514            Linewidth of the EMG traces. The default is 1.
2515        emg_line_alpha : float, optional
2516            Alpha of the EMG traces. The default is 0.25.
2517        emg_y_perc : float, optional
2518            The percentile (across MUPs) of the min and max EMG values to use for
2519            determining the y-axis range for the EMG plots (so outlier values are
2520            ignored). 100 - emg_y_perc is used to find the min value. Must be between
2521            0 and 100 inclusive. The default is 95.
2522        emg_y_buff_prop : float, optional
2523            The buffer to add around the min and max y values computed using emg_y_perc.
2524            The final y axis limits for the EMG traces are computed by multiplying the
2525            difference of those values by emg_y_buff_prop. The default is 0.2.
2526        time_marker_size : float, optional
2527            Size of the markers for the fibre potential times. The default is 2.
2528        align_times_to_fibre1 : bool, optional
2529            Whether to re-align the times so fibre1's potentials always occur at 0. If
2530            false, times are instead relative to each MUP's onset. The default is True.
2531        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
2532            Size of the figure, in inches. The default is (10, 10).
2533        axis_label_size : float, optional
2534            Font size of the axis labels. The default is 12.
2535        title_size : float, optional
2536            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
2537        dpi : int, optional
2538            Plot resolution (dots per inch). The default is 100.
2539        downsample_factor : int, optional
2540            How much to downsample the EMG traces (recommend max of 2). The default is 1.
2541
2542        Raises
2543        ------
2544        ValueError
2545            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit or
2546            if the requested fibre pair is not a valid option.
2547
2548        Returns
2549        -------
2550        fig : Figure | None
2551            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2552        ax : Axes | None
2553            The axes to which the plot belongs.
2554
2555        """
2556
2557        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2558        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2559            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2560        else:
2561            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results  # jitter results dictionary
2562
2563        # Default colours for fibre EMG traces
2564        if fibre_clrs is None:
2565            fibre_clrs = ["#008080", "#ca562c"]
2566
2567        # Get index of the fibre pair in the jitter results
2568        fibre_pair_idx = self.get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(fibre1, fibre2)
2569        if fibre_pair_idx is None:
2570            raise ValueError("Requested fibre pair is not an option.")
2571
2572        # Get mean consecutive difference of that fibre pair
2573        # If doesn't exist, return early with no figure
2574        mcd = jitter_results["mean_consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx]
2575        if np.isnan(mcd):
2576            return None, None
2577        else:  # convert to microseconds
2578            mcd = int((mcd / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2579
2580        # Boolean array of which MUPs were analysed and the indices (in
2581        # fibre_potential_times) of the corresponding fibre potentials
2582        analysed_mup, analysed_fibres_idx = self._get_jitter_analysed_mups_and_fibres(
2583            fibre1, fibre2
2584        )
2585
2586        # Get
2587        # 1) mode of the peak channels of fibre 1 and fibre 2 and
2588        # 2) times of the fibre potentials in the each MUP (nan if not analysed)
2589        n_fibres = 2
2590        fibres_peak_chan = np.full(n_fibres, 0)
2591        analysed_fibre_t = np.full((self.n_potentials, n_fibres), np.nan)
2592        for i in range(n_fibres):  # for each fibre
2593            # int indices of the analysed fibres, without nan (so can use for indexing)
2594            idx = analysed_fibres_idx[i, :]
2595            idx_no_nan = idx[~np.isnan(idx)]
2596            idx_no_nan = idx_no_nan.astype(int)
2597
2598            # Peak channel for each fibre and mode of peak channels
2599            chan = self.fibre_potential_peak_chan[idx_no_nan]
2600            mode_i = scipy.stats.mode(chan)
2601            fibres_peak_chan[i] = int(mode_i[0])
2602
2603            # Fibre times for each mup if mup was analysed (i.e., idx is not nan)
2604            # Otherwise, set to nan
2605            analysed_fibre_t[~np.isnan(idx), i] = self.fibre_potential_times[idx_no_nan]
2606
2607        # Convert fibre times to ms
2608        MS_MULTIPLIER = 1000
2609        analysed_fibre_t = (analysed_fibre_t / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2610
2611        # Create time vectors for EMG traces
2612
2613        # Create time vectors (ms) for x-axis of MUP EMG traces (analysed MUP only)
2614        # Will create a separate column for each trace so can align based on fibre potential
2615        # times if requested
2616        mup_t = (np.arange(1, self.n_samples_window + 1) / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2617        mup_t = np.transpose(
2618            np.tile(mup_t, [self.n_potentials, 1])
2619        )  # repeat and transpose (column = mup)
2620
2621        # If requested, re-align times so fibre1 times = 0 ms
2622        if align_times_to_fibre1:
2623            # Subtract fibre1 times from MUP times
2624            n_t = mup_t.shape[0]
2625            mup_t = mup_t - np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_t, 1])
2626
2627            # Subtract fibre1 times from analysed fibre times
2628            # (must be done second since need original fibres times for changing MUP times)
2629            analysed_fibre_t = analysed_fibre_t - np.transpose(
2630                np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_fibres, 1])
2631            )
2632
2633        # Plot EMG traces
2634
2635        # Set up plot
2636        fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=figsize, height_ratios=[1, 1, 4], sharex=True)
2637        fig.dpi = dpi
2638
2639        # Labels for fibres (add 1 to count from 1)
2640        fibre_labels = [fibre1 + 1, fibre2 + 1]
2641
2642        # Arrays for storing a percentile of the min max values of each EMG trace in
2643        # each fibre
2644        perc_of_max_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2645        perc_of_min_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2646
2647        # Plot MUPs of each fibre in each fibre's "peak" channel
2648        for i in range(n_fibres):
2649            fibre_mups = np.squeeze(
2650                self.all_spikes[analysed_mup, fibres_peak_chan[i], 0::downsample_factor]
2651            )
2652            axs[i].plot(
2653                mup_t[0::downsample_factor, analysed_mup],
2654                np.transpose(fibre_mups),
2655                lw=emg_line_lw,
2656                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2657                alpha=emg_line_alpha,
2658            )
2659
2660            # Compute min and max and the specified percentiles
2661            perc_of_max_y[i] = np.percentile(np.max(fibre_mups, axis=1), emg_y_perc)
2662            perc_of_min_y[i] = np.percentile(np.min(fibre_mups, axis=1), 100 - emg_y_perc)
2663
2664            # Title/axis labels (add one to channel indices so count is from 1)
2665            # No x-axis label since shared across all plots
2666            axs[i].set_title(
2667                f"Motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1}, "
2668                + f"fibre {fibre_labels[i]}, channel {fibres_peak_chan[i] + 1}",
2669                fontsize=title_size,
2670                fontweight="bold",
2671            )
2672            axs[i].set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2673
2674        # Link y-axes of two EMG plots
2675        axs[1].sharey(axs[0])
2676
2677        # Set limits based on percentiles of min/max
2678        emg_y_min = np.min(perc_of_min_y)
2679        emg_y_max = np.max(perc_of_max_y)
2680        emg_y_buff = (emg_y_max - emg_y_min) * emg_y_buff_prop
2681        axs[0].set_ylim([emg_y_min - emg_y_buff, emg_y_max + emg_y_buff])
2682
2683        # Fibre timing
2684
2685        # Plot times of the two fibre potentials in each MUP
2686        mup_number = np.arange(self.n_potentials) + 1  # sets y axis location of each tick
2687        ax_times = 2  # axis to use for plot
2688        for i in range(n_fibres):
2689            axs[ax_times].scatter(
2690                analysed_fibre_t[:, i],
2691                mup_number,
2692                s=time_marker_size,
2693                marker="|",
2694                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2695            )
2696
2697        # Axes (x-axis changes will apply to all plots)
2698        axs[ax_times].set_ylim([1, max(mup_number)])
2699        axs[ax_times].set_yticks([])  # no ticks
2700        axs[ax_times].invert_yaxis()  # first MUP at the top of the plot
2701        axs[ax_times].set_xlim([np.nanmin(mup_t), np.nanmax(mup_t)])  # tight x-axis limits
2702
2703        # Labels
2704        axs[ax_times].set_title(
2705            f"Fibre potential times (mean consecutive difference: {round(mcd, 2)} \u03bcs)",
2706            fontsize=title_size,
2707            fontweight="bold",
2708        )
2709        axs[ax_times].set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2710
2711        return fig, axs
2712
2713    def delete_fibre_localisation(self):
2714        """
2715        Deletes fibre localisation results (added by add_fibre_localisation method) and
2716        marks that fibre localisation analysis has not been performed.
2717
2718        Also removes downstream analysis (fibre clustering and jitter).
2719
2720        Returns
2721        -------
2722        None.
2723
2724        """
2725        print("Removing localisation results")
2726
2727        # Note analysis not performed.
2728        self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = False
2729
2730        # Set number of fibre potentials to zero.
2731        self.n_fibre_potentials = 0
2732
2733        # Store provided attributes.
2734        self.fibre_centres = np.array([])
2735        self.mup_onsets = np.array([])
2736        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
2737        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
2738        self.all_spikes = np.array([])
2739        self.generator_potential = np.array([])
2740
2741        # Also remove any downstream analysis.
2742        self.delete_fibre_clustering()  # will also delete jitter
2743
2744    def delete_fibre_clustering(self):
2745        """
2746        Deletes fibre clustering results (added by cluster_fibre_potentials method) and
2747        marks that fibre clustering analysis has not been performed.
2748
2749        Also removes downstream analysis (fibre jitter).
2750
2751        Returns
2752        -------
2753        None.
2754
2755        """
2756        print("Removing clustering results")
2757
2758        # Mark analysis as not performed.
2759        self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = False
2760
2761        # Delete results.
2762        self.fibre_clustering_results: dict = {}
2763
2764        # Also remove downstream analysis (jitter)
2765        self.delete_fibre_jitter()
2766
2767    def delete_fibre_jitter(self):
2768        """
2769        Deletes fibre jitter results (added by jitter_analysis method) and
2770        marks that fibre jitter analysis has not been performed.
2771
2772        Returns
2773        -------
2774        None.
2775
2776        """
2777        print("Removing jitter results")
2778
2779        # Mark analysis as not performed.
2780        self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = False
2781
2782        self.fibre_jitter_results: dict = {}
2783
2784
2785class EMGMotorUnits:
2786    """
2787    Class for storing and visualising all motor unit data returned from reconstruction
2788    analysis.
2789
2790    Only includes visualisations that do not require the recording time series.
2791
2792    """
2793
2794    def __init__(self, motor_units: list[EMGMotorUnit]):
2795        """
2796        Initialise EMGMotorUnits object.
2797
2798        Parameters
2799        ----------
2800        motor_units : list[EMGMotorUnit]
2801            List of motor units (class EMGMotorUnit) to add to the EMGMotorUnits object.
2802
2803        Returns
2804        -------
2805        None.
2806
2807        """
2808
2809        self.motor_units = motor_units
2810        self.n_motor_units = len(motor_units)
2811
2812        # Get and store number of potentials of each motor unit.
2813        self.n_potentials = [mu.n_potentials for mu in self.motor_units]
2814
2815    def __str__(self):
2816        """
2817        Return a string for the object.
2818
2819        Returns
2820        -------
2821        String
2822
2823        """
2824
2825        ans = "EMG Motor Units"
2826        ans += "\nNumber of motor units: "
2827        ans += str(self.n_motor_units)
2828
2829        ans += "\n"
2830
2831        return ans
2832
2833    def __len__(self) -> int:
2834        """
2835        Return the number of motor units.
2836
2837        Returns
2838        -------
2839        int
2840            Number of motor units stored in object.
2841
2842        """
2843        return self.n_motor_units
2844
2845    def plot_fibre_locations(
2846        self,
2847        location_type: str,
2848        motor_unit_idx: Optional[int] = None,
2849        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
2850        pt_size: float | None = None,
2851        pt_alpha: float | None = None,
2852        pt_facecolor=None,
2853        pt_edgecolor=None,
2854        pt_linewidth: float = 3,
2855        axis_equal: bool = True,
2856        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
2857        axis_label_size: float = 14,
2858        tick_label_size: float = 12,
2859        plot_legend: bool = True,
2860        min_legend_pt_size: float = 30,
2861        legend_label_size: float = 12,
2862        dpi: int = 100,
2863        cmap=None,
2864        max_y: float = 1,
2865        y_buff: float = 1.75,
2866        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
2867    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
2868        """
2869        Create 2D scatter plot of either
2870
2871        1) fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials (i.e., before
2872        clustering step).
2873
2874        or
2875
2876        2) fibre locations (median locations determined by clustering step, with one
2877        location per fibre).
2878
2879        The data plotted is determined by location_type: location_type = "potentials"
2880        returns the fibre potential localisations, while location_type = "fibres"
2881        returns the final estimated location of each fibre.
2882
2883        Can either plot fibre locations of all motor units or one, specified motor unit
2884        potential.
2885
2886        Default point colour depends on the motor unit number.
2887
2888        Parameters
2889        ----------
2890        location_type : str
2891            Either "potentials" or "fibres" (see above).
2892        motor_unit_idx : int, optional
2893            Motor unit index. The default is None.
2894        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
2895            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
2896        pt_size : float, optional
2897            Size of the points for the fibre locations. The default is 10 for potentials
2898            and 75 for fibres.
2899        pt_alpha : float, optional
2900            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.5 for
2901            potentials and 1 for fibres.
2902        pt_facecolor : Any, optional
2903            Colour of point centres. The default is None. If fibre potential locations
2904            are plotted, the default colour scheme or given cmap is used.
2905        pt_edgecolor : Any, optional
2906            Colour of point outlines. The default is None. If fibre locations are
2907            plotted, the default colour scheme or given cmap is used.
2908        pt_linewidth : float, optional
2909            Linewidth of points. Only used if pt_edgecolor is not None. The default is
2910            3.
2911        axis_equal : bool, optional
2912            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
2913        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
2914            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
2915        axis_label_size : float, optional
2916            size of axis label. The default is 14.
2917        tick_label_size : float, optional
2918            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
2919        plot_legend : bool, optional
2920            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
2921        min_legend_pt_size : float, optional
2922            Minimum size of points in legend - if pt_size is less
2923            than min_legend_pt_size, this value will be used for the legend point size.
2924            The default is 30.
2925        legend_label_size: float, optional
2926            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
2927        dpi : int, optional, optional
2928            Dots per inch. The default is 300.
2929        cmap : Any, optional, optional
2930            Colour map to use. The default is None.
2931        max_y : float, optional
2932            The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute
2933            y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure
2934            that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
2935        y_buff: float, optional
2936            Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to
2937            determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points
2938            along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
2939        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
2940            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
2941
2942        Returns
2943        -------
2944        fig : Figure
2945            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2946        ax : Axes
2947            The axes to which the plot belongs.
2948
2949        """
2950
2951        # Check value of location_type is valid
2952        if location_type not in ["potentials", "fibres"]:
2953            raise ValueError(
2954                f"location_type of {location_type} is not valid - must be 'potentials' or 'fibres'"
2955            )
2956
2957        # If not specified, determine point style based on location_type
2958        match location_type:
2959            case "potentials":
2960                if not pt_size:
2961                    pt_size = 10
2962                if not pt_alpha:
2963                    pt_alpha = 0.5
2964            case "fibres":
2965                if not pt_size:
2966                    pt_size = 75
2967                if not pt_alpha:
2968                    pt_alpha = 1
2969
2970        # Default colormap - will use if colors not specified.
2971        if cmap is None:
2972            cmap = colormaps["tab10"].colors
2973
2974        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2975        if ax is None:
2976            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
2977            fig.dpi = dpi
2978        else:
2979            fig = None
2980
2981        # Motor unit(s) to plot.
2982        if motor_unit_idx is not None:
2983            if motor_unit_idx < 0:
2984                motor_units = []
2985            else:
2986                motor_units = [self.motor_units[motor_unit_idx]]
2987        else:
2988            motor_units = self.motor_units
2989
2990        # Add electrodes to plot.
2991        if plot_electrodes and len(motor_units) > 0:
2992            motor_units[0]._plot_electrodes(ax=ax)
2993
2994        # Keep track of max absolute y position to ensure data is not cut off by axis limits
2995        fibre_max_y = 0
2996
2997        for mu in motor_units:
2998            # Colour for motor unit - differs depending on motor unit.
2999            # Face colour: default only used for plotting potentials
3000            if (pt_facecolor is None) and (location_type == "potentials"):
3001                # Use same colour scheme as cluster colours for motor units.
3002                mu_pt_facecolor = mu.get_cluster_colour(
3003                    mu.motor_unit_number, self.n_motor_units, cmap
3004                )
3005            elif not pt_facecolor:
3006                mu_pt_facecolor = "none"
3007            else:
3008                mu_pt_facecolor = pt_facecolor
3009
3010            # Edge colour: default only used for plotting fibres
3011            if (pt_edgecolor is None) and (location_type == "fibres"):
3012                # Use same colour scheme as cluster colours for motor units.
3013                mu_pt_edgecolor = mu.get_cluster_colour(
3014                    mu.motor_unit_number, self.n_motor_units, cmap
3015                )
3016            elif not pt_facecolor:
3017                mu_pt_edgecolor = "none"
3018            else:
3019                mu_pt_edgecolor = pt_edgecolor
3020
3021            # Data to plot
3022            if (location_type == "potentials") and (mu.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]):
3023                # Use fibre potential locations
3024                mu_fibre_locations = mu.fibre_centres
3025
3026            elif (location_type == "fibres") and (mu.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]):
3027                # Use fibre locations
3028                mu_fibre_locations = mu.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_median"]
3029
3030            else:
3031                # if analyses have not been performed, no fibres locations
3032                mu_fibre_locations = None
3033
3034            # Plot locations and compute max absolute y location
3035            if mu_fibre_locations is not None:
3036                ax.scatter(
3037                    mu_fibre_locations[:, 0],
3038                    mu_fibre_locations[:, 1],
3039                    pt_size,
3040                    alpha=pt_alpha,
3041                    linewidth=pt_linewidth,
3042                    facecolor=mu_pt_facecolor,
3043                    edgecolor=mu_pt_edgecolor,
3044                    label=f"motor unit {mu.motor_unit_number + 1}",
3045                )
3046
3047                # Max absolute y location
3048                mu_max_y = np.max(np.abs(mu_fibre_locations[:, 1]))
3049                fibre_max_y = max(fibre_max_y, mu_max_y)
3050
3051        # Plot legend
3052        if plot_legend:
3053            lgnd = ax.legend(
3054                bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1),
3055                loc="upper left",
3056                frameon=False,
3057                handletextpad=0.25,
3058                fontsize=legend_label_size,
3059            )
3060            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
3061                h._sizes = [max(min_legend_pt_size, pt_size)]
3062                h.set_alpha(1)
3063
3064        # Axis and tick labels.
3065        ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
3066        ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
3067        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
3068        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
3069        max_y = max(fibre_max_y * y_buff, max_y)  # Adjust max_y based on data
3070        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
3071
3072        # Equal aspect ratio.
3073        if axis_equal:
3074            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
3075
3076        return fig, ax
class EMGMotorUnit: 
  38class EMGMotorUnit:
  39    """
  40    Class for storing data for one motor unit
  41    returned from reconstruction analysis.
  42
  43    """
  44
  45    def __init__(
  46        self,
  47        number: int,
  48        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
  49        fs: float,
  50        chan_xy: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
  51    ):
  52        """
  53        Initialise EMGMotorUnit object.
  54
  55        Parameters
  56        ----------
  57        number: int
  58            This is the motor unit index (0, 1, 2, ...), returned from TK_filter,
  59            which corresponds to the index position of "motor_units" in the
  60            EMGMotorUnits class. When displayed to the user the motor unit label
  61            is displayed which is +1 this number, e.g. motor_unit_number 0 is the
  62            motor unit labelled as "1".
  63        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
  64            Time indices of the motor unit's potentials in the EMG recording.
  65        fs : float
  66            Sampling frequency (Hz) of the data.
  67        chan_xy : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
  68            Channel (electrode) (x,y) coordinates; saved as attribute to facilitate
  69            visualisations.
  70
  71        Returns
  72        -------
  73        None.
  74
  75        """
  76
  77        self.motor_unit_number = number
  78
  79        # Number of potentials (firings) assigned to MU.
  80        self.n_potentials = len(potentials_t_idx)
  81        # Time indices of potentials in EMG.
  82        self.potentials_t_idx = potentials_t_idx
  83
  84        # Set sampling frequency.
  85        self.fs = fs
  86
  87        # Channel/electrode coordinates of the needle.
  88        self.chan_xy = chan_xy
  89
  90        # Store information about analysis that has been performed for this MU
  91        # Note: even if true, may not be results if data was not suitable for analysis
  92        self.analysis_performed = {
  93            "fibres_localised": False,  # localisation step
  94            "fibres_clustered": False,  # clustering fibres step
  95            "fibres_jitter_computed": False,  # jitter analysis step
  96        }
  97
  98        # Localisation attributes.
  99        # Number of fibre potentials (peaks) found across all MUPs.
 100        self.n_fibre_potentials = 0
 101
 102        # Size of window used for localisation.
 103        self.n_samples_window = 0
 104
 105        # Estimated fibre x, y coordinate at each time (size n peaks x 2).
 106        self.fibre_centres = np.array([])
 107
 108        # Onset indices of MUPs that each fibre potential (peak) belongs to.
 109        # One for each fibre potential.
 110        self.mup_onsets = np.array([])
 111
 112        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
 113        # of the corresponding MUP that it belongs to (in indices units, not seconds).
 114        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
 115
 116        # The channel in which each fibre potential has peak amplitude (may be min or max).
 117        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
 118
 119        # Time series for each MUP and channel
 120        # (size: n MU potentials x n chan x time).
 121        self.all_spikes = np.array([])
 122
 123        # Generator potential, represents true underlying potential.
 124        self.generator_potential = np.array([])
 125
 126        # Results for comparing number of clusters for GMM or k-means.
 127        self.cluster_scores = None
 128
 129        # Dictionaries for storing results of clustering and jitter analysis.
 130        self.fibre_clustering_results: dict = {}
 131        self.fibre_jitter_results: dict = {}
 132
 133    def __str__(self) -> str:
 134        """
 135        Return a string for the object
 136
 137        Parameters
 138        ----------
 139        None.
 140
 141        Returns
 142        -------
 143        str
 144
 145        """
 146
 147        ans = "EMG Motor Unit"
 148        ans += "\nMotor unit number: "
 149        ans += str(self.motor_unit_number + 1)
 150        ans += "\nNumber of potentials: "
 151        ans += str(self.n_potentials)
 152        ans += "\nFibre centres dimensions: "
 153        ans += str(self.fibre_centres.shape)
 154        ans += "\nMUP onsets dimensions: "
 155        ans += str(self.mup_onsets.shape)
 156        ans += "\nFibre potential times dimensions: "
 157        ans += str(self.fibre_potential_times.shape)
 158        ans += "\nAll spikes dimensions: "
 159        ans += str(self.all_spikes.shape)
 160        ans += "\nGenerator potential dimensions: "
 161        ans += str(self.generator_potential.shape)
 162
 163        ans += "\n"
 164
 165        return ans

 167    def add_fibre_localisation(
 168        self,
 169        fibre_centres: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 170        mup_onsets: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 171        fibre_potential_times: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 172        fibre_potential_peak_chan: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 173        all_spikes: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 174        generator_potential: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 175    ):
 176        """
 177        Add results of the fibre localisation step to the motor unit object. Computes
 178        additional attributes and stores that analysis has been performed.
 179
 180        Called during EMGAnalysisReconstruct method, reconstruct_fibres
 181
 182        Parameters
 183        ----------
 184        fibre_centres : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 185            Estimated location of fibres.
 186        mup_onsets : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 187            Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time
 188        fibre_potential_times : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 189            Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset (overall) time
 190            of the corresponding MUP (listed above in mup_onsets)
 191        fibre_potential_peak_chan : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 192            The channel with the peak amplitude for each fibre potential.
 193        all_spikes : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 194            All peaks from surrounding channels.
 195        generator_potential : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 196            Represents true underlying potential. Used to find MUPs.
 197
 198        Returns
 199        -------
 200        None.
 201
 202        """
 203
 204        # Note analysis performed.
 205        self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = True
 206
 207        # Store number of fibre potentials (i.e., peaks in the MUPs) found.
 208        self.n_fibre_potentials = fibre_centres.shape[0]
 209
 210        # Store provided attributes.
 211        self.fibre_centres = fibre_centres
 212        self.mup_onsets = mup_onsets
 213        self.fibre_potential_times = fibre_potential_times
 214        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = fibre_potential_peak_chan
 215        self.all_spikes = all_spikes
 216        self.generator_potential = generator_potential
 217
 218        # Save the size of the window in number of indices, used later for plots.
 219        # So that all_spikes does not need to be saved with the results, and this
 220        # value can be saved and loaded instead.
 221        self.n_samples_window = self.all_spikes.shape[2]
 222
 223    def get_fibre_localisation_dict(self, save_all_spikes: bool = False) -> dict:
 224        """
 225        Returns dictionary of fibre localisation so that it can be saved
 226
 227        Parameters
 228        ----------
 229        save_all_spikes : bool, optional
 230            Whether to save all_spikes. Uses a lot of data and is not necessary.
 231            The default is False.
 232
 233        Returns
 234        -------
 235        dict
 236
 237        """
 238
 239        # Convert to lists to store as dictionary.
 240        fibre_local_dict = {
 241            "n_fibre_potentials": self.n_fibre_potentials,
 242            "fibre_centres": self.fibre_centres.tolist(),
 243            "mup_onsets": self.mup_onsets.tolist(),
 244            "fibre_potential_times": self.fibre_potential_times.tolist(),
 245            "all_spikes": [],
 246            "n_samples_window": self.n_samples_window,
 247            # "generator_potential" : self.generator_potential.tolist()
 248        }
 249
 250        if save_all_spikes:
 251            fibre_local_dict["all_spikes"] = self.all_spikes.tolist()
 252
 253        return fibre_local_dict
 254
 255    def set_fibre_localisation_from_dict(self, fibre_local_dict: dict):
 256        """
 257        Sets fibre localisation results from loaded dictionary.
 258
 259        Parameters
 260        ----------
 261        fibre_local_dict : dict
 262            Dictionary containing saved results of clustering.
 263
 264        Returns
 265        -------
 266        None.
 267
 268        """
 269
 270        # Convert data back to arrays.
 271        self.n_fibre_potentials = fibre_local_dict["n_fibre_potentials"]
 272        self.fibre_centres = np.array(fibre_local_dict["fibre_centres"])
 273        self.mup_onsets = np.array(fibre_local_dict["mup_onsets"])
 274        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array(fibre_local_dict["fibre_potential_times"])
 275        self.all_spikes = np.array(fibre_local_dict["all_spikes"])
 276        self.n_samples_window = fibre_local_dict["n_samples_window"]
 277        # self.generator_potential = np.array(fibre_local_dict["generator_potential"])
 278
 279        # Note analysis performed.
 280        if self.n_fibre_potentials is not None and len(self.fibre_centres) > 0:
 281            self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = True
 282
 283    def _cluster_silhouette_score(self, estimator, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> float:
 284        """
 285        Callable to pass to GridSearchCV that will use the silhouette score.
 286
 287        Parameters
 288        ----------
 289        estimator: Any
 290            Estimator class, which will include a "predict" method.
 291
 292        X : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 293            Array of fibre potential data to assign to clusters.
 294
 295        Returns
 296        -------
 297        float
 298
 299        """
 300
 301        return silhouette_score(X, estimator.predict(X))
 302
 303    def _gmm_selection(
 304        self, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64], min_n_clusters: int, max_n_clusters: int
 305    ) -> GridSearchCV:
 306        """
 307        Gaussian Mixture Model Selection.
 308        https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/mixture/plot_gmm_selection.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-mixture-plot-gmm-selection-py
 309        Fit data to clusters from the minimum number of clusters to the maximum number of clusters.
 310
 311        Parameters
 312        ----------
 313        X : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 314            Array of fibre potential data to assign to clusters.
 315        min_n_clusters : int
 316            Minimum number of clusters to try.
 317        max_n_clusters : int
 318            Maximum number of clusters to try.
 319
 320        Returns
 321        -------
 322        float
 323        """
 324
 325        param_grid = {
 326            "n_components": range(min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters + 1),
 327            "covariance_type": [self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type],
 328        }
 329
 330        grid_search = GridSearchCV(
 331            GaussianMixture(), param_grid=param_grid, scoring=self._cluster_silhouette_score
 332        )
 333
 334        grid_search.fit(X)
 335
 336        return grid_search
 337
 338    def _k_means_selection(
 339        self, X: npt.NDArray[np.float64], min_n_clusters: int, max_n_clusters: int
 340    ) -> GridSearchCV:
 341        """
 342        Try out k-means clustering for different numbers of clusters.
 343        Fit data to clusters from the minimum number of clusters to the maximum number of clusters.
 344
 345        """
 346
 347        param_grid = {
 348            "n_clusters": range(min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters + 1),
 349            "random_state": [self.mu_cluster_settings.k_means_random_state],
 350            "n_init": ["auto"],
 351        }
 352
 353        grid_search = GridSearchCV(
 354            KMeans(), param_grid=param_grid, scoring=self._cluster_silhouette_score
 355        )
 356
 357        grid_search.fit(X)
 358
 359        return grid_search
 360
 361    def cluster_fibre_potentials(self, mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings):
 362        """
 363        Cluster the fibre potentials and compute median fibre locations of the
 364        specified motor unit.
 365
 366        Before this analysis is run, the motor unit's fibres potentials must be
 367        identified and localised using the reconstruct_fibres method of the
 368        EMGAnalysisReconstruct class.
 369
 370        Running this method populates the fibre_clustering_results dictionary attribute
 371        with the following key/value pairs:
 372            mean_n_fps (int): mean number of fibre potentials across all motor unit
 373            potentials used in the localisation analysis. Used as input for clustering.
 374
 375            n_fibre_clusters (int): number of clusters found; may slightly differ from
 376            mean_n_fps.
 377
 378            fibre_clusters (npt.NDArray[np.int32], size (self.fibre_potentials,) ):
 379                cluster assignment of each fibre potential
 380
 381            n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 382                                       size (self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters)):
 383            Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each motor unit potential (MUP) that
 384            have the same cluster assignment.
 385
 386            mup_fibre_pos (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 387                           size(self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters)):
 388            Location estimates ((x,y) coordinates) of each fibre based on each MUP. If
 389            the fibre is not found in the MUP, the coordinates are np.nan.
 390
 391            fibre_centres_median (npt.NDArray[np.float64], size(n_fibre_clusters, 2)):
 392            Median coordinates of each fibre.
 393
 394        Parameters
 395        ----------
 396        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 397            Contains all settings for clustering.
 398
 399        Raises
 400        ------
 401        RuntimeError
 402            Raised if localisation analysis has not been performed on requested motor
 403            unit.
 404
 405        Returns
 406        -------
 407        None.
 408
 409        """
 410
 411        # Set settings for cluster analysis.
 412        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
 413
 414        # Check that localisation has been run.
 415        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]:
 416            raise RuntimeError(
 417                "Localisation analysis has not been performed; cannot cluster fibres."
 418            )
 419
 420        # Arrays to store results for median and GMM clustering.
 421        fibre_centres_median = np.array([])
 422        fibre_centres_gmm_mean = np.array([])
 423        fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = np.array([])
 424
 425        # Onset indices of all MUPs that have fibre potentials.
 426        unique_mup_onsets = np.unique(self.mup_onsets)
 427        n_unique_mup_onsets = len(unique_mup_onsets)
 428        mean_n_fps = round(len(self.mup_onsets) / n_unique_mup_onsets)
 429
 430        # Set up data to use for clustering.
 431        if self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale > 0:
 432            # Scale time column.
 433            # Values in (0, 20] for self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale
 434            # are suitable for scaling.
 435            # Do not scale fibre locations as they are in the same units (mm).
 436            time_min = np.min(self.fibre_potential_times)
 437            time_max = np.max(self.fibre_potential_times)
 438
 439            data_to_cluster = np.hstack(
 440                (
 441                    self.fibre_centres,
 442                    (
 443                        (np.atleast_2d(self.fibre_potential_times).T - time_min)
 444                        / (time_max - time_min)
 445                    )
 446                    * self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale,
 447                )
 448            )
 449
 450        else:
 451            data_to_cluster = self.fibre_centres
 452
 453        # Choose clustering method.
 454        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "dbscan":
 455            # Use Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN).
 456            clustering = DBSCAN(
 457                eps=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_eps,
 458                min_samples=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_min_samples,
 459            ).fit(data_to_cluster)
 460            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(clustering.labels_) + 1
 461            fibre_clusters = clustering.labels_
 462
 463        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
 464            # k for clustering.
 465            k = self.mu_cluster_settings.k_means_k
 466
 467            # Use a range if no values of k if not given.
 468            if k == 0:
 469                min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
 470                max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
 471            else:
 472                min_n_clusters = k
 473                max_n_clusters = k
 474
 475            grid_search = self._k_means_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
 476
 477            # fibre cluster assignments.
 478            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
 479            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
 480
 481            # Record results for graph plotting.
 482            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
 483
 484        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 485            # Use Gaussian Mixture Model Selection.
 486            min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
 487            max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
 488
 489            grid_search = self._gmm_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
 490
 491            # Record results for graph plotting.
 492            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
 493
 494            # Fibre cluster assignments.
 495            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
 496            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
 497
 498            fibre_centres_gmm_mean = grid_search.best_estimator_.means_
 499            fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = grid_search.best_estimator_.covariances_
 500
 501        else:
 502            # If no valid clustering method given.
 503            raise Exception(
 504                "Clustering method,"
 505                + str(self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method)
 506                + ", not found!"
 507                + "Valid options are: dbscan, k-means or gmm."
 508            )
 509
 510        # Initialise arrays for storing results.
 511
 512        # Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each MUP that belong to the same
 513        # cluster.
 514        n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster = np.zeros((self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters))
 515
 516        # Location estimates of each fibre based on each MUP.
 517        # Note: unlike original code, data stored so indices match the
 518        # self.potentials_t_idx array.
 519        mup_fibre_pos = np.full((self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters), np.nan)
 520
 521        # Find median location of each fibre.
 522        for cluster_num in np.arange(n_fibre_clusters):
 523            # Sometimes multiple fibre potentials in the same MUP are assigned to
 524            # the same fibre clusters. One of these will be chosen later as the "best"
 525            # to compute the jitter. (One nearest the median over all MUPs)
 526            # If no fibres with that cluster num appear in the MUP, position is
 527            # stored as np.nan.
 528
 529            # Iterate through all MUPs (not just ones
 530            # present in "mup_onsets") so dimensions align to other MUP features.
 531            for mup_num in np.arange(self.n_potentials):
 532                mup_onset = self.potentials_t_idx[mup_num]
 533
 534                # Fibre potentials that belong to the specified onset and cluster.
 535                idx = np.flatnonzero(
 536                    np.all(
 537                        (
 538                            (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset),
 539                            (fibre_clusters == cluster_num),
 540                        ),
 541                        axis=0,
 542                    )
 543                )
 544
 545                # Store number of fibre potentials found.
 546                n_idx = len(idx)
 547                n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster[mup_num, cluster_num] = n_idx
 548
 549                # Compute average position of the fibre based on the specified MUP.
 550                if n_idx > 0:
 551                    pos = self.fibre_centres[idx, :]
 552                    mup_fibre_pos[mup_num, :, cluster_num] = np.mean(pos, axis=0)
 553
 554            # Compute median fibre positions.
 555            with warnings.catch_warnings():
 556                warnings.simplefilter("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
 557                fibre_centres_median = np.transpose(np.nanmedian(mup_fibre_pos, axis=0))
 558
 559        # Store results as dictionary.
 560        self.fibre_clustering_results = {
 561            "mean_n_fps": mean_n_fps,
 562            "n_fibre_clusters": n_fibre_clusters,
 563            "fibre_clusters": fibre_clusters,
 564            "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster,
 565            "mup_fibre_pos": mup_fibre_pos,
 566            "fibre_centres_median": fibre_centres_median,
 567            "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": fibre_centres_gmm_mean,
 568            "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": fibre_centres_gmm_covariance,
 569        }
 570        self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = True
 571
 572    def get_fibre_clusters_dict(self) -> dict:
 573        """
 574        Returns dictionary of fibre clusters so that it can be saved.
 575
 576        Parameters
 577        ----------
 578        None.
 579
 580        Returns
 581        -------
 582        dict
 583            Dictionary containing clustering results.
 584
 585        """
 586
 587        # Get clustering results if they exist and put in a dictionary
 588        # with arrays stored as lists so they can be save in a json format file.
 589        if self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]:
 590            fibre_clusters_dict = {
 591                "mean_n_fps": int(self.fibre_clustering_results["mean_n_fps"]),
 592                "n_fibre_clusters": int(self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]),
 593                "fibre_clusters": self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"].tolist(),
 594                "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 595                    "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster"
 596                ].tolist(),
 597                "mup_fibre_pos": self.fibre_clustering_results["mup_fibre_pos"].tolist(),
 598                "fibre_centres_median": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 599                    "fibre_centres_median"
 600                ].tolist(),
 601                "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 602                    "fibre_centres_gmm_mean"
 603                ].tolist(),
 604                "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": self.fibre_clustering_results[
 605                    "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"
 606                ].tolist(),
 607            }
 608        else:
 609            fibre_clusters_dict = {}
 610
 611        return fibre_clusters_dict
 612
 613    def set_fibre_clusters_from_dict(
 614        self, fibre_clusters_dict: dict, mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 615    ):
 616        """
 617        Sets fibre localisation results from loaded dictionary.
 618
 619        Parameters
 620        ----------
 621        fibre_clusters_dict : dict
 622            Dictionary containing saved results of clustering
 623
 624        mu_cluster_settings : EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 625            Copy of settings used to do clustering.
 626
 627        Returns
 628        -------
 629        None.
 630
 631        """
 632
 633        # If clustering not done for this MU then do not set anything.
 634        if fibre_clusters_dict:
 635            # Convert lists back to arrays to store results.
 636            self.fibre_clustering_results = {
 637                "mean_n_fps": fibre_clusters_dict["mean_n_fps"],
 638                "n_fibre_clusters": fibre_clusters_dict["n_fibre_clusters"],
 639                "fibre_clusters": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_clusters"]),
 640                "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": np.array(
 641                    fibre_clusters_dict["n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster"]
 642                ),
 643                "mup_fibre_pos": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["mup_fibre_pos"]),
 644                "fibre_centres_median": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_median"]),
 645                "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": np.array(fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"]),
 646                "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": np.array(
 647                    fibre_clusters_dict["fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"]
 648                ),
 649            }
 650
 651            # Note analysis performed.
 652            self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = True
 653
 654            # Set clustering settings also.
 655            self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
 656
 657    def plot_compare_cluster_scores(self) -> sns.FacetGrid:
 658        """
 659
 660        Parameters
 661        ----------
 662        None.
 663
 664        Returns
 665        -------
 666        sns.FacetGrid
 667            Returns the FacetGrid object with the plot on it for further tweaking.
 668
 669        """
 670
 671        # Set variable name of data to retrieve.
 672        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 673            cluster_str = "param_n_components"
 674        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
 675            cluster_str = "param_n_clusters"
 676        else:
 677            cluster_str = ""
 678
 679        # Return blank plot if no data.
 680        if cluster_str == "" or self.cluster_scores is None:
 681            return sns.catplot(kind="bar")
 682
 683        # Create bar plot.
 684        grid = sns.catplot(
 685            kind="bar",
 686            x=self.cluster_scores[cluster_str],
 687            y=self.cluster_scores["mean_test_score"],
 688            legend_out=False,
 689        )
 690
 691        # Set limits and layout.
 692        plt.ylim((0, 1))
 693        plt.tight_layout(pad=5.0)
 694
 695        grid.set_axis_labels("number of clusters", "silhouette score")
 696
 697        return grid

 699    def plot_fibre_locations_setup(
 700        self,
 701        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
 702        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 703        tick_label_size: float = 12,
 704        dpi: int = 100,
 705        threeD: bool = False,
 706    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
 707        """
 708        Sets up plot for showing fibre locations, possibly from different motor units.
 709
 710        Parameters
 711        ----------
 712        figsize : tuple[int, int], optional
 713            Size of the figure. The default is (10, 5).
 714        axis_label_size : int, optional
 715            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
 716        tick_label_size : int, optional
 717            Size of the tick labels. The default is 12.
 718        dpi : int, optional
 719            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
 720        threeD : bool, optional
 721            Create 3D plot if true. The default is False.
 722
 723        Returns
 724        -------
 725        fig : Figure
 726            The figure to which the plot belongs.
 727        ax : Axes
 728            The axes to which the plot belongs.
 729
 730        """
 731
 732        # Create new figure with specified size.
 733        if threeD:
 734            fig = Figure(figsize=figsize)
 735            ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
 736        else:
 737            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
 738
 739        fig.dpi = dpi
 740
 741        # Add axis and tick labels.
 742        ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 743        ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 744        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 745        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 746
 747        # Add time axis if 3D plot.
 748        # Type checking complains for 3D but it is fine.
 749        if threeD:
 750            ax.set_zlabel("time (\u03bc seconds)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
 751            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
 752
 753        plt.title(f"Motor Unit {self.motor_unit_number+1}")
 754
 755        return fig, ax

 757    def _plot_electrodes(
 758        self,
 759        ax: Axes,
 760        marker: str = "s",
 761        marker_size: float = 20,
 762        clr: str = "silver",
 763        z: float = None,
 764    ):
 765        """
 766        Plot electrode locations using their (x,y) coordinates.
 767
 768        Electrodes are symbolised by grey squares by default.
 769
 770        Parameters
 771        ----------
 772        ax : Axes
 773            Axes to plot the electrodes onto.
 774        marker : str, optional
 775            The kind of marker to use. The default is "s", square.
 776        marker_size : float, optional
 777            The size of the markers. The default is 20.
 778        clr : str, optional
 779            The colour of the electrodes. Default is "silver".
 780        z : float, optional
 781            z value of electrodes for 3D plot. Default is None.
 782
 783        Returns
 784        -------
 785        None.
 786
 787        """
 788
 789        # Plot electrodes.
 790        if z is None:
 791            ax.scatter(
 792                self.chan_xy[:, 0], self.chan_xy[:, 1], s=marker_size, marker=marker, color=clr
 793            )
 794        else:
 795            # Plot electrodes on 3D graph at set z distance.
 796            ax.scatter(
 797                self.chan_xy[:, 0],
 798                self.chan_xy[:, 1],
 799                np.full(len(self.chan_xy[:, 0]), z),
 800                s=marker_size,
 801                marker=marker,
 802                color=clr,
