 805    def plot_fibre_potential_clustering(
 806        self,
 807        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
 808        pt_potentials_size: float = 10,
 809        pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4,
 810        pt_mean_size: float = 50,
 811        n_sigma: int = 2,
 812        axis_equal: bool = True,
 813        lw: float = 0.5,
 814        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.2, 5.0),
 815        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 816        tick_label_size: float = 12,
 817        dpi: int = 100,
 818        cmap=None,
 819        max_x: float = 22,
 820        max_y: float = 1,
 821        plot_legend: bool = True,
 822        legend_pt_size: float = 50,
 823        legend_label_size: float = 12,
 824    ):
 825        """
 826        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
 827        with the location of each fibre overlaid. Ellipse confidence regions are plotted
 828        around te fibre locations
 829        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
 830
 831        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
 832
 833        Parameters
 834        ----------
 835        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
 836            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
 837        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
 838            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
 839        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
 840            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
 841        pt_mean_size : float, optional
 842            Size of points for means. The fibre centres. The default is 50.
 843        n_sigma : float, optional
 844            Number of St. Dev. to plot around the fibre centres. The Default is 2.
 845        axis_equal : bool, optional
 846            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
 847        lw : float, optional
 848            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
 849        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
 850            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
 851        axis_label_size : float, optional
 852            size of axis label. The default is 14.
 853        tick_label_size : float, optional
 854            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
 855        dpi : int, optional
 856            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
 857        cmap : Any, optional
 858            Colour map to use. The default is None.
 859        max_x : float, optional
 860            Maximum of x axis. The default is 22.
 861        max_y : float, optional
 862            Maximum of y axis. The default is 1.
 863        plot_legend : bool, optional
 864            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
 865        legend_pt_size : float, optional
 866            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
 867        legend_label_size: float, optional
 868            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
 869
 870        Returns
 871        -------
 872        None.
 873
 874        """
 875
 876        # Setup plot
 877        fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
 878            figsize=figsize,
 879            axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
 880            tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
 881            dpi=dpi,
 882        )
 883
 884        # Add electrodes to plot
 885        if plot_electrodes:
 886            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax)
 887
 888        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
 889
 890        # Plot clusters
 891        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
 892            self._plot_cluster_points(
 893                cluster_no,
 894                n_clusters,
 895                ax,
 896                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
 897                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
 898                cmap=cmap,
 899                lw=lw,
 900            )
 901
 902        # Plot centres and covariance regions (if not GMM).
 903        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
 904            self._plot_fibre_location(
 905                cluster_no,
 906                n_clusters,
 907                ax,
 908                (self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm"),
 909                pt_mean_size,
 910                n_sigma,
 911            )
 912
 913        # Plot fitted covariance regions for GMM.
 914        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
 915            self._plot_fitted_gmms(ax, n_sigma)
 916
 917        # Plot legend.
 918        if plot_legend:
 919            lgnd = ax.legend(
 920                bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1),
 921                loc="upper left",
 922                frameon=False,
 923                handletextpad=0.25,
 924                fontsize=legend_label_size,
 925            )
 926            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
 927                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
 928                h.set_alpha(1)
 929
 930        # Set y axis limits.
 931        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
 932
 933        # Set x axis limits.
 934        ax.set_xlim(-1, max_x)
 935
 936        # Equal aspect ratio, (this can mess up the axis limits in Windows)
 937        if axis_equal:
 938            ax.axis("equal")
 939
 940    def get_cluster_colour(self, cluster_no: int, n_clusters: int, cmap=None):
 941        """
 942        Return the colour of a cluster depending on the cluster number and
 943        how many total clusters.
 944
 945        Parameters
 946        ----------
 947        cluster_no : int
 948            Number of the cluster.
 949        n_clusters : int
 950            Total number of clusters.
 951        cmap : Colourmap, optional
 952            Use this colour map if given. The default is None.
 953
 954        Returns
 955        -------
 956        Colour
 957
 958        """
 959
 960        if cmap is None:
 961            if n_clusters <= 10:
 962                cmap = colormaps["tab10"].colors
 963            elif n_clusters <= 20:
 964                cmap = colormaps["tab20"].colors
 965            else:
 966                cmap = plt.cm.rainbow(np.linspace(0, 1, n_clusters))
 967        else:  # if colourmap is specified, check that sufficient colours; if not, repeat
 968            if len(cmap) < n_clusters:
 969                cmap = cmap * int(np.ceil(n_clusters / len(cmap)))
 970
 971        return cmap[cluster_no]
 972
 973    def _plot_cluster_points(
 974        self,
 975        cluster_no: int,
 976        n_clusters: int,
 977        ax: Axes,
 978        pt_size: float,
 979        pt_alpha: float,
 980        cmap=None,
 981        lw: float = 0,
 982        threeD: bool = False,
 983    ):
 984        """
 985        Plot all the points for fibre potentials beloging to the same cluster.
 986
 987        Parameters
 988        ----------
 989        cluster_no : int
 990            Number of the cluster.
 991        n_clusters : int
 992            Total number of clusters.
 993        ax : Axes, optional
 994            Plot to add to. The default is None.
 995        pt_alpha : float, optional
 996            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
 997        cmap : Colourmap, optional
 998            Use this colour map if given. The default is None.
 999        lw : float, optional
1000            Line weight. The default is 0.
1001        threeD : bool, optional
1002            If points are plotted on a 3D axis or not (z axis = time in ms). The default
1003            is False.
1004
1005        Returns
1006        -------
1007        None.
1008
1009        """
1010
1011        # Get x and y coords to plot.
1012        x = self.fibre_centres[(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 0]
1013        y = self.fibre_centres[(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1]
1014
1015        # Get z coords to plot if a 3D plot.
1016        if threeD:
1017            N_MS_PER_SEC = 1000
1018            # Determine shift needed to plot MUP onset at t = 0
1019            n_ms = ((self.n_samples_window - 1) / 2) / self.fs * N_MS_PER_SEC
1020
1021            # Fibre potential times
1022            z = (
1023                self.fibre_potential_times[
1024                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no)
1025                ]
1026                / self.fs
1027            ) * N_MS_PER_SEC
1028            z = z - n_ms
1029
1030        # Get colour of points.
1031        pt_facecolor = self.get_cluster_colour(cluster_no, n_clusters, cmap)
1032
1033        # Plot points for this cluster.
1034        if threeD:
1035            ax.scatter(
1036                x,
1037                y,
1038                z,
1039                s=pt_size,
1040                alpha=pt_alpha,
1041                facecolors=pt_facecolor,
1042                linewidth=lw,
1043                label=f"fibre {cluster_no + 1}",
1044            )
1045        else:
1046            ax.scatter(x, y, pt_size, alpha=pt_alpha, facecolors=pt_facecolor, linewidth=lw)
1047
1048    def _plot_fitted_gmms(self, ax: Axes, n_sigma: float):
1049        """
1050        Plot all the points for fibre potentials beloging to the same cluster.
1051
1052        Parameters
1053        ----------
1054        ax : Axes
1055            Plot to add to.
1056        n_sigma : float
1057            Number of standard deviations to plot confidence ellipses.
1058
1059        Returns
1060        -------
1061        None.
1062
1063        """
1064
1065        # Set up covariance matrix depending on which covariance model was used.
1066        cv = self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_covariance"]
1067
1068        # Covariance the same for every cluster if "tied".
1069        if self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "tied":
1070            cov = np.array([[cv[0, 0], cv[0, 1]], [cv[1, 0], cv[1, 1]]])
1071
1072        for i, mean in enumerate(self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"]):
1073            # Set covariance matrix from fitted GMM.
1074            if self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "diag":
1075                cov = np.array([[cv[i, 0], 0], [0, cv[i, 1]]])
1076            elif self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "spherical":
1077                cov = np.array([[cv[i], 0], [0, cv[i]]])
1078            elif self.mu_cluster_settings.gmm_covariance_type == "full":
1079                cov = np.array(cv[i])
1080
1081            v, w = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
1082
1083            angle = np.arctan2(w[0][1], w[0][0])
1084            # Convert to degrees
1085            angle = 180.0 * angle / np.pi
1086            # Multiply radius by 2 to get diameter.
1087            v = n_sigma * 2 * np.sqrt(v)
1088            # Define the ellipse and plot it.
1089            ellipse = Ellipse(
1090                mean, v[0], v[1], angle=180.0 + angle, edgecolor="black", facecolor="none"
1091            )
1092            ax.add_artist(ellipse)
1093
1094    def _confidence_ellipse(
1095        self,
1096        x: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1097        y: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1098        ax: Axes,
1099        n_std: float = 3.0,
1100        facecolor="none",
1101        **kwargs,
1102    ):
1103        """
1104        Taken from matplotlib documentation
1105        https://matplotlib.org/stable/gallery/statistics/confidence_ellipse.html
1106
1107        Create a plot of the covariance confidence ellipse of *x* and *y*.
1108
1109        Parameters
1110        ----------
1111        x, y : npt.NDArray[np.float64], shape (n, )
1112            Input data.
1113        ax : Axes
1114            The Axes object to draw the ellipse into.
1115        n_std : float, optional
1116            The number of standard deviations to determine the ellipse's radiuses.
1117            The default is 3.
1118        facecolor : Any, optional
1119            Face color of ellipse. The default is "none".
1120        **kwargs
1121            Forwarded to `~matplotlib.patches.Ellipse`
1122
1123        Returns
1124        -------
1125        None.
1126        """
1127
1128        if x.size != y.size:
1129            raise ValueError("x and y must be the same size")
1130
1131        # No data to do anything with so return!
1132        if len(x) == 0:
1133            return
1134
1135        cov = np.cov(x, y)
1136        pearson = cov[0, 1] / np.sqrt(cov[0, 0] * cov[1, 1])
1137        # Using a special case to obtain the eigenvalues of this
1138        # two-dimensional dataset.
1139        ell_radius_x = np.sqrt(1 + pearson)
1140        ell_radius_y = np.sqrt(1 - pearson)
1141        ellipse = Ellipse(
1142            (0, 0), width=ell_radius_x * 2, height=ell_radius_y * 2, facecolor=facecolor, **kwargs
1143        )
1144
1145        # Calculate the scale of x from
1146        # the standard deviation and multiply
1147        # with the given number of standard deviations.
1148        scale_x = np.sqrt(cov[0, 0]) * n_std
1149        mean_x = np.mean(x)
1150
1151        # Calculate the scale of y.
1152        scale_y = np.sqrt(cov[1, 1]) * n_std
1153        mean_y = np.mean(y)
1154
1155        transf = (
1156            transforms.Affine2D().rotate_deg(45).scale(scale_x, scale_y).translate(mean_x, mean_y)
1157        )
1158
1159        # Return the Axes object with the ellipse drawn on it.
1160        ellipse.set_transform(transf + ax.transData)
1161        ax.add_patch(ellipse)
1162
1163    def _plot_fibre_location(
1164        self,
1165        cluster_no: int,
1166        n_clusters: int,
1167        ax: Axes,
1168        gmm: bool,
1169        pt_mean_size: float = 10,
1170        n_sigma: float = 1,
1171        pt_facecolor=None,
1172    ):
1173        """
1174        Plots estimated fibre location and confidence ellipse.
1175
1176        Parameters
1177        ----------
1178        cluster_no : int
1179            Number of the cluster.
1180        n_clusters : int
1181            Total number of clusters.
1182        ax : Axes
1183            Plot to add to.
1184        gmm : bool
1185            True if clustering method is GMM.
1186        pt_mean_size : float, optional
1187            Size of mean points. The default is 10.
1188        n_sigma : float, optional
1189            Number of standard deviations for confidence ellipse. The default is 1.
1190        pt_facecolor : Any, optional
1191            Face colour of points, The default is None.
1192
1193        Returns
1194        -------
1195        None.
1196
1197        """
1198
1199        if gmm:
1200            center = self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_gmm_mean"][cluster_no]
1201        else:
1202            x = np.array(
1203                self.fibre_centres[
1204                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 0
1205                ]
1206            )
1207            y = np.array(
1208                self.fibre_centres[
1209                    (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1
1210                ]
1211            )
1212            center = np.array([[np.mean(x)], [np.mean(y)]])
1213
1214        if pt_facecolor is None:
1215            pt_facecolor = self.get_cluster_colour(cluster_no, n_clusters)
1216
1217        ax.scatter(
1218            center[0],
1219            center[1],
1220            pt_mean_size,
1221            color=pt_facecolor,
1222            edgecolors="black",
1223            label=f"fibre {cluster_no + 1}",
1224        )
1225
1226        if not gmm:
1227            self._confidence_ellipse(x, y, ax, n_sigma, edgecolor="black")
1228
1229    def plot_3D_fibre_potential_clustering(
1230        self,
1231        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
1232        pt_potentials_size: float = 10,
1233        pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4,
1234        axis_equal: bool = True,
1235        lw: float = 0.5,
1236        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
1237        axis_label_size: float = 14,
1238        tick_label_size: float = 12,
1239        dpi: int = 100,
1240        cmap=None,
1241        max_y: float = 1,
1242        y_buff: float = 1.75,
1243        plot_legend: bool = True,
1244        legend_pt_size: float = 50,
1245        legend_label_size: float = 12,
1246        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1247    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
1248        """
1249        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
1250        (one point per potential) with z-axis corresponding to the time of each fibre
1251        potential in the motor unit potential (t = 0 ms is MUP onset).
1252
1253        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
1254
1255        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
1256
1257        Parameters
1258        ----------
1259        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
1260            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
1261        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
1262            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
1263        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
1264            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
1265        axis_equal : bool, optional
1266            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
1267        lw : float, optional
1268            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
1269        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
1270            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
1271        axis_label_size : float, optional
1272            size of axis label. The default is 14.
1273        tick_label_size : float, optional
1274            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
1275        dpi : int, optional
1276            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
1277        cmap : Any, optional
1278            Colour map to use. The default is None.
1279        max_y : float, optional
1280            The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute
1281            y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure
1282            that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
1283        y_buff: float, optional
1284            Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to
1285            determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points
1286            along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
1287        plot_legend : bool, optional
1288            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
1289        legend_pt_size : float, optional
1290            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
1291        legend_label_size: float, optional
1292            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
1293        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1294            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1295
1296        Returns
1297        -------
1298        None.
1299
1300        """
1301
1302        # Setup plot.
1303        if ax is None:
1304            fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
1305                figsize=figsize,
1306                axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
1307                tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
1308                dpi=dpi,
1309                threeD=True,
1310            )
1311        else:
1312            fig = None
1313
1314            # Add axis and tick labels.
1315            ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1316            ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1317            ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1318            ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1319            ax.set_zlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
1320            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1321
1322        # Determine z axis limits based on window used to compute motor unit potentials.
1323        N_MS_PER_SEC = 1000
1324        n_ms = (
1325            ((self.n_samples_window - 1) / 2) / self.fs * N_MS_PER_SEC
1326        )  # shift to plot MUP onset at t=0
1327        max_z = n_ms
1328
1329        # Add electrodes to plot at bottom.
1330        if plot_electrodes:
1331            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax, z=-max_z, clr="grey", marker_size=5)
1332
1333        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1334
1335        # Keep track of max absolute y position to ensure data is not cut off by axis limits.
1336        fibre_max_y = 0
1337
1338        # Plot each cluster.
1339        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
1340            self._plot_cluster_points(
1341                cluster_no,
1342                n_clusters,
1343                ax,
1344                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
1345                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
1346                cmap=cmap,
1347                lw=lw,
1348                threeD=True,
1349            )
1350            # Max y
1351            mu_max_y = np.max(
1352                np.abs(
1353                    self.fibre_centres[
1354                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1
1355                    ]
1356                )
1357            )
1358            fibre_max_y = max(fibre_max_y, mu_max_y)
1359
1360        # Add legend.
1361        if plot_legend:
1362            lgnd = ax.legend(
1363                bbox_to_anchor=(1.2, 1.0),
1364                loc="upper left",
1365                frameon=False,
1366                handletextpad=0.25,
1367                fontsize=legend_label_size,
1368            )
1369            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
1370                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
1371                h.set_alpha(1)
1372
1373        # Set y axis and z-axis limits.
1374        max_y = max(fibre_max_y * y_buff, max_y)  # Adjust max_y based on data
1375        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
1376        ax.set_zlim(-max_z, max_z)
1377
1378        # Equal aspect ratio for x and y coordinates
1379        if axis_equal:
1380            ax.set_aspect("equalxy", adjustable="box")
1381
1382        return fig, ax
1383
1384    def remove_outliers_iqr(
1385        self, intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1386    ) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int64], int]:
1387        """
1388        Parameters
1389        ----------
1390        intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int]
1391            Array of time intervals.
1392
1393        Returns
1394        -------
1395        npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1396            Array of time intervals with outliers removed.
1397
1398        """
1399
1400        # Calculate interquartile range.
1401        q25, q75 = np.nanpercentile(intervals, 25), np.nanpercentile(intervals, 75)
1402        iqr = q75 - q25
1403
1404        # Calculate the outlier cutoff.
1405        cut_off = iqr * 1.5
1406        lower, upper = q25 - cut_off, q75 + cut_off
1407
1408        # Replace outliers with nan.
1409        ans = np.array([np.nan if x < lower or x > upper else x for x in intervals])
1410        num_of_outliers = np.count_nonzero(((intervals < lower) | (intervals > upper)))
1411
1412        return ans, num_of_outliers
1413
1414    def _calculate_fibre_potentials_time_diff(self, fib_pot_pos1: int, fib_pot_pos2: int) -> int:
1415        """
1416        Parameters
1417        ----------
1418        fib_pot_pos1: int
1419            Index of the first fibre potential in fibre_potential_times.
1420        fib_pot_pos2: int
1421            Index of the second fibre potential in fibre_potential_times.
1422
1423        Returns
1424        -------
1425        int
1426            Length of time interval between the two fibre potentials
1427            returned as a multiple of the number of time steps i.e. indices.
1428
1429        """
1430
1431        return np.abs(
1432            self.fibre_potential_times[fib_pot_pos2] - self.fibre_potential_times[fib_pot_pos1]
1433        )
1434
1435    def _jitter_analysis_between_two_fibres(
1436        self, fibre1_num: int, fibre2_num: int
1437    ) -> tuple[
1438        float,
1439        float,
1440        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1441        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1442        int,
1443        int,
1444        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1445        npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1446    ]:
1447        """
1448        Performs jitter analysis for this motor unit (MU). For the identified
1449        fibres computes the mean consecutive difference (MCD) between each pair
1450        of fibre. Firstly one fibre potential is chosen for each fibre and
1451        then the time difference is taken between them for the first MUP.
1452        This time interval is compared with the time interval for the next MUP
1453        by taking the absolute difference - and so on until the second last MUP.
1454        The mean of these differences is the MCD.
1455
1456        MCD = (1/(N-1)) * sum(|D_k - D_{k+1}|) for k = 1 to N-1, where D_k is the kth
1457        MUP time difference between the fibre potentials for the 2 fibres in question.
1458
1459        The median value of D_k is also recorded to hopefully better account for
1460        the poor quality of data.
1461
1462        Parameters
1463        ----------
1464        fibre1_num : int
1465            Fibre number for the first fibre, given previously from cluster analysis (0,1,2,...).
1466        fibre2_num : int
1467            Fibre number for the second fibre.
1468        remove_outliers: bool
1469            Remove outliers in fibre potential times to avoid probable miss-classifications
1470
1471        Returns
1472        -------
1473        tuple[float,
1474            float,
1475            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1476            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1477            int,
1478            int,
1479            npt.NDArray[np.int64],
1480            npt.NDArray[np.int64]]
1481
1482        """
1483
1484        # Calculate medians of all the fibre potentials for fibre 1 and fibre 2.
1485        all_fibre1_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1486            (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre1_num)
1487        )
1488        median_time1 = np.median(self.fibre_potential_times[all_fibre1_potentials_idx])
1489
1490        all_fibre2_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1491            (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre2_num)
1492        )
1493        median_time2 = np.median(self.fibre_potential_times[all_fibre2_potentials_idx])
1494
1495        # Length of time intervals between fibre potentials in the two different fibres.
1496        fibre_potential_time_diffs = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1497
1498        # Taken note of how many outliers there are and which fibre potentials
1499        # were used.
1500        number_of_differences_outliers = 0
1501        number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = 0
1502        fibre1_pots_used_idx = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1503        fibre2_pots_used_idx = np.full(self.n_potentials, np.nan)
1504
1505        # Compute length of time intervals between fibre potentials.
1506        for mup_num in range(self.n_potentials):
1507            mup_onset_idx = self.potentials_t_idx[mup_num]
1508
1509            # Fibre potentials that belong to the specified MUP and fibre (cluster).
1510            fibre1_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1511                np.all(
1512                    (
1513                        (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset_idx),
1514                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre1_num),
1515                    ),
1516                    axis=0,
1517                )
1518            )
1519
1520            fibre2_potentials_idx = np.flatnonzero(
1521                np.all(
1522                    (
1523                        (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset_idx),
1524                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == fibre2_num),
1525                    ),
1526                    axis=0,
1527                )
1528            )
1529
1530            if len(fibre1_potentials_idx) > 0 and len(fibre2_potentials_idx) > 0:
1531                # Pick fibre potentials closest to the medians.
1532                fibre1_potential_to_use = np.argmin(
1533                    np.abs(median_time1 - self.fibre_potential_times[fibre1_potentials_idx])
1534                )
1535                fibre2_potential_to_use = np.argmin(
1536                    np.abs(median_time2 - self.fibre_potential_times[fibre2_potentials_idx])
1537                )
1538
1539                # Get time difference for this MUP between fibre potentials.
1540                fib_pot_pos1 = fibre1_potentials_idx[fibre1_potential_to_use]
1541                fib_pot_pos2 = fibre2_potentials_idx[fibre2_potential_to_use]
1542                fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num] = self._calculate_fibre_potentials_time_diff(
1543                    fib_pot_pos1, fib_pot_pos2
1544                )
1545
1546                # Record which fibre potentials were used to look into later, if desired.
1547                # Note that these fibres include outliers
1548                fibre1_pots_used_idx[mup_num] = fib_pot_pos1
1549                fibre2_pots_used_idx[mup_num] = fib_pot_pos2
1550
1551        # Remove outliers in time intervals.
1552        if self.mu_jitter_settings.remove_outliers:
1553            fibre_potential_time_diffs, number_of_differences_outliers = self.remove_outliers_iqr(
1554                fibre_potential_time_diffs
1555            )
1556
1557        # Compute consecutive differences.
1558        consecutive_diffs = np.full((self.n_potentials - 1), np.nan)
1559
1560        # Loop thro' MUPs.
1561        for mup_num in range(self.n_potentials - 1):
1562            if not np.isnan(fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num]) and not np.isnan(
1563                fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num + 1]
1564            ):
1565                consecutive_diffs[mup_num] = np.abs(
1566                    fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num] - fibre_potential_time_diffs[mup_num + 1]
1567                )
1568
1569        # Remove outliers.
1570        if self.mu_jitter_settings.remove_outliers:
1571            consecutive_diffs, number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = self.remove_outliers_iqr(
1572                consecutive_diffs
1573            )
1574
1575        # Compute mean consecutive difference.
1576        mean_consecutive_diff = np.nanmean(consecutive_diffs)
1577
1578        # Compute median of consecutive differences.
1579        median_consecutive_diff = np.nanmedian(consecutive_diffs)
1580
1581        # Return many results for the jitter analysis.
1582        return (
1583            mean_consecutive_diff,
1584            median_consecutive_diff,
1585            fibre_potential_time_diffs,
1586            consecutive_diffs,
1587            number_of_differences_outliers,
1588            number_of_cons_diffs_outliers,
1589            fibre1_pots_used_idx,
1590            fibre2_pots_used_idx,
1591        )
1592
1593    def jitter_analysis(self, mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings):
1594        """
1595        Calculate jitter between all pairs of fibres.
1596        For each fibre pair:
1597        Firstly a vector of time differences (intervals) are
1598        calculated, one interval for each MUP. If there is more than one fibre
1599        potential assigned to a fibre for a MUP then the one that is closest to the
1600        median (over all fibre potentials in that fibre) is chose. If there are no
1601        fibre potentials for that fibre and MUP then an interval cannot be record so
1602        is NAN.
1603        Secondly, the consecutive differences are calculated, the difference
1604        between intervals that are in adjacent MUPs. If an interval does not exist
1605        then NAN is recorded.
1606        Finally, the mean consecutive differences is calculated to measure the jitter.
1607        The median consecutive differences is also calculated to try and account
1608        for poor data.
1609
1610        Parameters
1611        ----------
1612        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1613            The setting to use for the jitter analysis.
1614
1615        Returns
1616        -------
1617        None.
1618
1619        """
1620
1621        # Set jitter settings.
1622        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
1623
1624        # Check that localisation and fibre clustering has been run.
1625        if (
1626            not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]
1627            or not self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]
1628        ):
1629            raise RuntimeError(
1630                "Localisation analysis and fibre cluster analysis"
1631                + "must be performed before jitter analysis!"
1632            )
1633
1634        # Check there is data to do the calculation.
1635        if self.n_potentials < 2:
1636            raise RuntimeError("Not enough MUPs to perform jitter analysis!")
1637
1638        # Get the number of clusters.
1639        n_fibre_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1640
1641        # The number of jitter calculations to do between fibres.
1642        number_of_jitter_calcs = int(n_fibre_clusters * (n_fibre_clusters - 1) / 2)
1643
1644        # Calculations to report.
1645        fibre1_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1646        fibre2_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1647        mean_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1648        median_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1649        fibre_potential_time_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1650        consecutive_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials - 1))
1651        number_of_differences = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1652        number_of_cons_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1653        number_of_differences_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1654        number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1655        fibre1_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1656        fibre2_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1657
1658        # Loop thro' each fibre pair and perform the jitter analysis.
1659        # Fibre pair count.
1660        count = 0
1661        for fibre1_num in range(n_fibre_clusters - 1):
1662            for fibre2_num in np.arange(fibre1_num + 1, n_fibre_clusters):
1663                # Do jitter analysis between fibre1 and fibre2.
1664                (
1665                    mean_consecutive_diffs[count],
1666                    median_consecutive_diffs[count],
1667                    fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :],
1668                    consecutive_diffs[count, :],
1669                    number_of_differences_outliers[count],
1670                    number_of_cons_diffs_outliers[count],
1671                    fibre1_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1672                    fibre2_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1673                ) = self._jitter_analysis_between_two_fibres(fibre1_num, fibre2_num)
1674
1675                # Record fibres analysed and some data counts.
1676                fibre1_numbers[count] = fibre1_num
1677                fibre2_numbers[count] = fibre2_num
1678                number_of_differences[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1679                    ~np.isnan(fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :])
1680                )
1681                number_of_cons_diffs[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1682                    ~np.isnan(consecutive_diffs[count, :])
1683                )
1684                count += 1
1685
1686        # Record final jitter analysis results in dictionary.
1687        self.fibre_jitter_results = {
1688            "fibre1_numbers": fibre1_numbers,
1689            "fibre2_numbers": fibre2_numbers,
1690            "mean_consecutive_diffs": mean_consecutive_diffs,
1691            "median_consecutive_diffs": median_consecutive_diffs,
1692            "differences": fibre_potential_time_diffs,
1693            "consecutive_diffs": consecutive_diffs,
1694            "number_of_differences": number_of_differences,
1695            "number_of_differences_outliers": number_of_differences_outliers,
1696            "number_of_cons_diffs": number_of_cons_diffs,
1697            "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": number_of_cons_diffs_outliers,
1698            "fibre1_pots_used_idx": fibre1_pots_used_idx,
1699            "fibre2_pots_used_idx": fibre2_pots_used_idx,
1700        }
1701
1702        # Record that the jitter analysis has been performed for this motor unit.
1703        self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = True
1704
1705    def get_fibre_jitter_dict(self) -> dict:
1706        """
1707        Returns dictionary of fibre jitter results so that it can be saved.
1708
1709        Parameters
1710        ----------
1711        None.
1712
1713        Returns
1714        -------
1715        dict
1716
1717        """
1718
1719        # If jitter analysis is not done then return empty dictionary.
1720        if self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
1721            fibre_jitter_dict = {
1722                "fibre1_numbers": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"].tolist(),
1723                "fibre2_numbers": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"].tolist(),
1724                "mean_consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1725                    "mean_consecutive_diffs"
1726                ].tolist(),
1727                "median_consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1728                    "median_consecutive_diffs"
1729                ].tolist(),
1730                "differences": self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"].tolist(),
1731                "consecutive_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"].tolist(),
1732                "number_of_differences": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1733                    "number_of_differences"
1734                ].tolist(),
1735                "number_of_differences_outliers": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1736                    "number_of_differences_outliers"
1737                ].tolist(),
1738                "number_of_cons_diffs": self.fibre_jitter_results["number_of_cons_diffs"].tolist(),
1739                "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": self.fibre_jitter_results[
1740                    "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers"
1741                ].tolist(),
1742                "fibre1_pots_used_idx": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_pots_used_idx"].tolist(),
1743                "fibre2_pots_used_idx": self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_pots_used_idx"].tolist(),
1744            }
1745        else:
1746            fibre_jitter_dict = {}
1747
1748        return fibre_jitter_dict
1749
1750    def set_fibre_jitter_from_dict(
1751        self, fibre_jitter_dict: dict, mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1752    ):
1753        """
1754        Sets fibre jitter results from loaded jitter results.
1755
1756        Parameters
1757        ----------
1758        fibre_jitter_dict : dict
1759            Dictionary containing saved results of jitter analysis.
1760
1761        mu_jitter_settings : EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1762            Copy of settings used to do jitter analysis.
1763
1764        Returns
1765        -------
1766        None.
1767
1768        """
1769
1770        # Check jitter analysis results are saved.
1771        if fibre_jitter_dict:
1772            self.fibre_jitter_results = {
1773                "fibre1_numbers": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre1_numbers"]),
1774                "fibre2_numbers": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre2_numbers"]),
1775                "mean_consecutive_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["mean_consecutive_diffs"]),
1776                "median_consecutive_diffs": np.array(
1777                    fibre_jitter_dict["median_consecutive_diffs"]
1778                ),
1779                "differences": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["differences"]),
1780                "consecutive_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["consecutive_diffs"]),
1781                "number_of_differences": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_differences"]),
1782                "number_of_differences_outliers": np.array(
1783                    fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_differences_outliers"]
1784                ),
1785                "number_of_cons_diffs": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_cons_diffs"]),
1786                "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": np.array(
1787                    fibre_jitter_dict["number_of_cons_diffs_outliers"]
1788                ),
1789                "fibre1_pots_used_idx": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre1_pots_used_idx"]),
1790                "fibre2_pots_used_idx": np.array(fibre_jitter_dict["fibre2_pots_used_idx"]),
1791            }
1792
1793            # Note analysis performed.
1794            self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = True
1795
1796            self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
1797
1798    def plot_fibre_potential_time_diffs(
1799        self, fibre1_num: int, fibre2_num: int, display_counts: bool = True
1800    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
1801        """
1802        Plot a histogram for time differences between fibre potentials.
1803
1804        Parameters
1805        ----------
1806        fibre1_num : int
1807            Fibre number for the first fibre, given previously from cluster analysis (0,1,2,...).
1808        fibre2_num : int
1809            Fibre number for the second fibre.
1810        display_counts : bool, optional
1811            Display amount of non nan data used in histograms on plot. The default is True.
1812
1813        Returns
1814        -------
1815        fig : Figure
1816            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1817        ax : Axes
1818            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1819
1820        """
1821
1822        # Get index for this pair of fibres so that the results can be retreived.
1823        res_idx0 = np.where(
1824            np.all(
1825                (
1826                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"] == fibre1_num),
1827                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"] == fibre2_num),
1828                ),
1829                axis=0,
1830            )
1831        )
1832
1833        # Create plot.
1834        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
1835
1836        if len(res_idx0) > 0:
1837            res_idx = res_idx0[0]
1838        else:
1839            print(f"Jitter results not found for fibres {fibre1_num + 1} and {fibre2_num + 1}!")
1840            return fig, ax
1841
1842        # Get fibre differences and convert to time in seconds.
1843        fibre_pot_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"][res_idx, :] / self.fs
1844        fibre_pot_diffs = fibre_pot_diffs.flatten()
1845
1846        # Plot histogram.
1847        if not np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs).all():
1848            ax.hist(
1849                fibre_pot_diffs,
1850                bins=30,
1851                density=True,
1852                color="lightgrey",
1853                edgecolor="k",
1854                linewidth=0.5,
1855            )
1856
1857        plt.title(
1858            f"Fibre Potential Intervals (Motor Unit {self.motor_unit_number+1}"
1859            + f", Fibres {fibre1_num+1} and {fibre2_num+1})"
1860        )
1861
1862        # Add mean and standard deviation info to plot.
1863        mean = np.nanmean(fibre_pot_diffs)
1864        st_dev = np.nanstd(fibre_pot_diffs, ddof=1)
1865        textstr = "\n".join(
1866            (
1867                r"Mean $= %.0f$ " % (mean * 1e6,) + "\u03bcs",
1868                r"St. dev. $=%.0f$ " % (st_dev * 1e6,) + "\u03bcs",
1869            )
1870        )
1871
1872        # These are matplotlib.patch.Patch properties.
1873        props = dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="wheat", alpha=0.5)
1874
1875        # Place a text box in upper left in axes coords.
1876        ax.text(
1877            0.05,
1878            0.95,
1879            textstr,
1880            transform=ax.transAxes,
1881            fontsize=14,
1882            verticalalignment="top",
1883            bbox=props,
1884        )
1885
1886        # Display counts and percent.
1887        if display_counts:
1888            total_diffs = len(fibre_pot_diffs)
1889            total_non_nan_diffs = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs))
1890            percent = (total_non_nan_diffs / total_diffs) * 100
1891            textstr = (
1892                r"MUPs $= %d$" % (total_diffs,)
1893                + "\n"
1894                + r"Used $=%d (%0.2f$"
1895                % (
1896                    total_non_nan_diffs,
1897                    percent,
1898                )
1899                + r"$\%$)"
1900            )
1901
1902            # Place a text box in upper right in axes coords.
1903            ax.text(
1904                0.95,
1905                0.95,
1906                textstr,
1907                transform=ax.transAxes,
1908                fontsize=14,
1909                verticalalignment="top",
1910                horizontalalignment="right",
1911                bbox=props,
1912            )
1913
1914        return fig, ax

1916    def plot_fibre_consecutive_diffs(

2035    def plot_jitter_heat_plot(
2036        self,
2037        median: bool = False,
2038        cmap: Any = "magma",
2039        vmax: float = 100,
2040        clr_background: Any = "dimgrey",
2041        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
2042    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
2043        """
2044        Plot a heat map of mean consecutive differences (MCDs) between fibres.
2045        (Or medians of consecutive differences)
2046
2047        Parameters
2048        ----------
2049        median : bool, optional
2050            Plot medians instead of mean consecutive differences. The default is False.
2051        cmap : matplotlib colormap name or object, or list of colors, optional
2052            Colourmap. The default is matplotlib colourmap "magma".
2053        vmax : float, optional
2054            The upper limit for the colourmap, in microseconds. This argument ensures
2055            that outliers do not dramatically skew the colourmap and that colours are
2056            easily comparable across motor units. The default is 100.
2057        clr_background: colour specification, optional
2058            Colour for plot background (recommend similar darkness to low values of the
2059            colourmap). The default is "dimgrey".
2060        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
2061            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
2062
2063        Returns
2064        -------
2065        fig : Figure | None
2066            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2067        ax : matplotlib Axes
2068            Axes object with the heatmap.
2069        """
2070
2071        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2072        if ax is None:
2073            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
2074        else:
2075            fig = None
2076
2077        # Get number of fibre pairs; return early if none.
2078        n_fibre_pairs = len(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"])
2079        if n_fibre_pairs == 0:
2080            ax.set_axis_off()  # remove plot axes
2081            return fig, ax
2082
2083        n_fibres = int(np.max(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"]) + 1)
2084
2085        # Create data array for the heat plot.
2086        data = np.full((n_fibres, n_fibres), np.nan)
2087
2088        for i in range(n_fibre_pairs):
2089            fib1 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"][i])
2090            fib2 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"][i])
2091
2092            if median:
2093                val = self.fibre_jitter_results["median_consecutive_diffs"][i]
2094            else:
2095                val = self.fibre_jitter_results["mean_consecutive_diffs"][i]
2096
2097            # Convert indices to micro seconds.
2098            if not np.isnan(val):
2099                val = int((val / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2100
2101            # Make heat plot symetrical.
2102            data[fib1, fib2] = val
2103            data[fib2, fib1] = val
2104
2105        # Plotting the heatmap.
2106        str_fibres = [str(x) for x in np.arange(1, n_fibres + 1)]
2107
2108        ax = sns.heatmap(
2109            data=data,
2110            vmin=0,
2111            vmax=vmax,
2112            cmap=cmap,
2113            annot=True,
2114            xticklabels=str_fibres,
2115            yticklabels=str_fibres,
2116            cbar_kws={"label": "\u03bc seconds"},
2117            fmt="g",
2118            ax=ax,
2119        )
2120
2121        ax.set_xlabel("fibre number")
2122        ax.set_ylabel("fibre number")
2123
2124        # Titles (line break ensures that plot is the same size as plot_jitter_heat_plot,
2125        # which has a two line title)
2126        if median:
2127            ax.set_title(
2128                f"Median Consecutive Differences\n(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2129                fontweight="bold",
2130            )
2131        else:
2132            ax.set_title(
2133                f"Mean Consecutive Differences\n(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2134                fontweight="bold",
2135            )
2136
2137        # Ensure square, change background colour, and add frame
2138        ax.set_aspect("equal")
2139        ax.set_facecolor(clr_background)
2140        for _, spine in ax.spines.items():
2141            spine.set_visible(True)
2142
2143        return fig, ax
2144
2145    def _get_jitter_totals(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> tuple[int, float, int, float]:
2146        """
2147        Gets counts (and percentage) of non nan time intervals (between fibre potentials)
2148        and consecutive differences between fibres fibre1 and fibre2
2149
2150        Parameters
2151        ----------
2152        fibre1 : int
2153            Index of fibre1.
2154        fibre2 : int
2155            Index of fibre2.
2156
2157        Returns
2158        -------
2159        tuple[int, float, int, float]
2160
2161        """
2162
2163        # Get index for this pair of fibres so that the results can be retreived.
2164        res_idx0 = np.where(
2165            np.all(
2166                (
2167                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"] == fibre1),
2168                    (self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"] == fibre2),
2169                ),
2170                axis=0,
2171            )
2172        )
2173
2174        if len(res_idx0) > 0:
2175            res_idx = res_idx0[0]
2176        else:
2177            print(f"Jitter results not found for fibres {fibre1 + 1} and {fibre2 + 1}!")
2178            return 0, 0, 0, 0
2179
2180        # Get fibre differences.
2181        fibre_pot_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["differences"][res_idx, :]
2182        fibre_pot_diffs = fibre_pot_diffs.flatten()
2183
2184        total_diffs = len(fibre_pot_diffs)
2185        total_non_nan_diffs = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(fibre_pot_diffs))
2186        percent_df = round((total_non_nan_diffs / total_diffs) * 100, 2)
2187
2188        # Get consecutive differences.
2189        consecutive_diffs = self.fibre_jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][res_idx, :]
2190        consecutive_diffs = consecutive_diffs.flatten()
2191
2192        con_diffs = len(consecutive_diffs)
2193        total_non_nan_cd = np.count_nonzero(~np.isnan(consecutive_diffs))
2194        percent_cd = round((total_non_nan_cd / con_diffs) * 100, 2)
2195
2196        return total_non_nan_diffs, percent_df, total_non_nan_cd, percent_cd
2197
2198    def plot_jitter_totals_heat_plot(
2199        self,
2200        percent: bool = False,
2201        cmap: Any = "viridis",
2202        clr_background: Any = "dimgrey",
2203        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
2204    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes]:
2205        """
2206        Plot a heat map of counts (= number of consecutive differences) used for jitter
2207        analysis.
2208
2209        Parameters
2210        ----------
2211        percent: bool, optional
2212            Plot percentage of non-nan counts of consecutive differences, otherwise plot
2213            the counts. The default is False.
2214        cmap : matplotlib colormap name or object, or list of colors, optional
2215            Colourmap. The default is matplotlib colourmap "viridis".
2216        clr_background: colour specification, optional
2217            Colour for plot background (recommend similar darkness to low values of the
2218            colourmap). The default is "dimgrey".
2219        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
2220            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
2221
2222        Returns
2223        -------
2224
2225        fig : Figure | None
2226            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2227        ax : matplotlib Axes
2228            Axes object with the heatmap.
2229
2230        """
2231
2232        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2233        if ax is None:
2234            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
2235        else:
2236            fig = None
2237
2238        # Get number of fibre pairs; return early if none.
2239        n_fibre_pairs = len(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"])
2240        if n_fibre_pairs == 0:
2241            ax.set_axis_off()  # remove plot axes
2242            return fig, ax
2243
2244        n_fibres = int(np.max(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"]) + 1)
2245
2246        # Create array for heat plot.
2247        data = np.full((n_fibres, n_fibres), np.nan)
2248
2249        for i in range(n_fibre_pairs):
2250            fib1 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre1_numbers"][i])
2251            fib2 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"][i])
2252
2253            (
2254                _,
2255                _,
2256                total_non_nan_cd,
2257                percent_cd,
2258            ) = self._get_jitter_totals(fib1, fib2)
2259
2260            # Set values for heat plot (symmetric)
2261            if percent:
2262                data[fib1, fib2] = percent_cd
2263                data[fib2, fib1] = percent_cd
2264            else:
2265                data[fib1, fib2] = total_non_nan_cd  # number of consecutive differences
2266                data[fib2, fib1] = total_non_nan_cd
2267
2268        # Plotting the heatmap.
2269        str_fibres = [str(x) for x in np.arange(1, n_fibres + 1)]
2270
2271        if percent:
2272            bar_str = "percent"
2273        else:
2274            bar_str = "count"
2275
2276        ax = sns.heatmap(
2277            data=data,
2278            vmin=0,
2279            cmap=cmap,
2280            annot=True,
2281            xticklabels=str_fibres,
2282            yticklabels=str_fibres,
2283            cbar_kws={"label": bar_str},
2284            fmt="g",
2285            ax=ax,
2286        )
2287
2288        ax.set_xlabel("fibre number")
2289        ax.set_ylabel("fibre number")
2290
2291        if percent:
2292            ax.set_title(
2293                "Sample sizes (% of consecutive differences)\n"
2294                + f"(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2295                fontweight="bold",
2296            )
2297        else:
2298            ax.set_title(
2299                "Sample sizes (# consecutive differences)\n"
2300                + f"(motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1})",
2301                fontweight="bold",
2302            )
2303
2304        # Ensure square, change background colour, and add frame
2305        ax.set_aspect("equal")
2306        ax.set_facecolor(clr_background)
2307        for _, spine in ax.spines.items():
2308            spine.set_visible(True)
2309
2310        return fig, ax

2312    def get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> int | None:
2313        """
2314        Get index of requested fibre pair in the motor unit's jitter results
2315        (fibre_jitter_results attribute). Will return None if the fibre pair is not an
2316        option or if there are multiple matches for that fibre pair in the jitter
2317        results (which should only arrise if there is an error in the analysis code).
2318
2319        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2320
2321        Parameters
2322        ----------
2323        fibre1 : int
2324            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2325        fibre2 : int
2326            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2327
2328        Raises
2329        ------
2330        ValueError
2331            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit.
2332
2333        Returns
2334        -------
2335        fibre_pair_idx : int | None
2336            Index of the specified fibre; can use for extracting the corresponding
2337            results in the motor unit's jitter analysis results. Is None if fibre pair
2338            is not a valid option.
2339        """
2340
2341        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2342        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2343            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2344        else:
2345            # Jitter results
2346            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results
2347
2348        # Determine which fields in jitter_results to use for each fibre
2349        # Lower fibre number is stored in fibre1 results, while higher value is fibre2
2350        if fibre1 < fibre2:
2351            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2352            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2353        else:
2354            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2355            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2356
2357        # Determine index of results for that fibre pair
2358        fibre_pair_idx_bool = np.all(
2359            [
2360                jitter_results[fibre1_numbers_field] == fibre1,
2361                jitter_results[fibre2_numbers_field] == fibre2,
2362            ],
2363            axis=0,
2364        )
2365
2366        # Compute number of matches; if not exactly 1, return None
2367        n_fibre_pair_matches = sum(fibre_pair_idx_bool)
2368        if n_fibre_pair_matches == 1:
2369            fibre_pair_idx = np.flatnonzero(fibre_pair_idx_bool)[0]
2370        else:
2371            fibre_pair_idx = None
2372
2373        # Return fibre pair index
2374        return fibre_pair_idx
2375
2376    def _get_jitter_analysed_mups_and_fibres(
2377        self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int
2378    ) -> (npt.NDArray[np.bool_], npt.NDArray[np.float64]):
2379        """
2380        Returns
2381
2382        1) boolean array of which motor unit potentials were included in the jitter
2383           computation for the specified fibre pair
2384
2385        and
2386
2387        2) float array of the indices (in self.fibre_potential_times)
2388           of the fibre potentials in each motor unit that were used to compute the
2389           jitter of that fibre pair. Float array is used so the indices are nan if that
2390           motor unit potential was not analysed.
2391
2392        Note that MUPs that may have been removed by outlier detection are still marked
2393        as True (= analysed).
2394
2395        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2396
2397        Parameters
2398        ----------
2399        fibre1 : int
2400            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2401        fibre2 : int
2402            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2403
2404        Raises
2405        ------
2406        ValueError
2407            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit.
2408
2409        Returns
2410        -------
2411        analysed_mup : npt.NDArray[np.bool_]
2412            Boolean numpy array of which motor unit potentials were included in the
2413            jitter analysis for this fibre pair. MUPs that produced outlier values are
2414            still included. Shape is (self.n_potentials,).
2415
2416        analysed_fibres_idx : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
2417            Float array of the indices (in self.fibre_potential_times)
2418            of the fibre potentials in each motor unit that were used to compute the
2419            jitter of that fibre pair. The index is set to nan if that motor unit
2420            potential was not analysed. Shape is (2, self.n_potentials), with row 1
2421            corresponding to fibre1 and row 2 corresponding to fibre2.
2422
2423        """
2424
2425        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2426        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2427            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2428        else:
2429            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results  # jitter results dictionary
2430
2431        # Get fibre pair index in jitter results
2432        fibre_pair_idx = self.get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(fibre1, fibre2)
2433
2434        # Initialise array for storing which MUPs were analysed
2435        analysed_mup = np.full(self.n_potentials, False)
2436
2437        # Need to append and prepend NaN to consecutive differences array to determine which
2438        # MUPs are used (since each consecutive difference corresponds to two MUPs)
2439        nan1 = np.isnan(np.append(jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx, :], np.nan))
2440        nan2 = np.isnan(
2441            np.append(np.array(np.nan), jitter_results["consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx, :])
2442        )
2443
2444        # If not nan in at least one, that MUP was analysed
2445        analysed_mup[np.any([~nan1, ~nan2], axis=0)] = True
2446
2447        # Get indices of fibre 1 and fibre 2 (in fibre_potential_times/fibre_potential_peak_chan)
2448        # for each MUP that was analysed.
2449        # First need to determine which fields in jitter_results to use for each fibre
2450        # Lower fibre number is stored in fibre1 results, while higher value is fibre2
2451        if fibre1 < fibre2:
2452            fibre1_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre1_pots_used_idx"
2453            fibre2_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre2_pots_used_idx"
2454        else:
2455            fibre2_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre1_pots_used_idx"
2456            fibre1_pots_used_idx_field = "fibre2_pots_used_idx"
2457
2458        analysed_fibres_idx = np.vstack(
2459            (
2460                jitter_results[fibre1_pots_used_idx_field][fibre_pair_idx, :],
2461                jitter_results[fibre2_pots_used_idx_field][fibre_pair_idx, :],
2462            )
2463        )
2464        analysed_fibres_idx[:, ~analysed_mup] = np.nan  # Set to nan if fibre not analysed
2465
2466        return analysed_mup, analysed_fibres_idx
2467
2468    def plot_jitter_fibre_pair_EMG_and_times(
2469        self,
2470        fibre1: int,
2471        fibre2: int,
2472        fibre_clrs: list[Any] | None = None,
2473        emg_line_lw: float = 1,
2474        emg_line_alpha: float = 0.25,
2475        emg_y_perc: float = 95,
2476        emg_y_buff_prop: float = 0.2,
2477        time_marker_size: float = 2,
2478        align_times_to_fibre1: bool = True,
2479        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 10),
2480        axis_label_size: float = 12,
2481        title_size: float = 12,
2482        dpi: int = 100,
2483        downsample_factor: int = 1,
2484    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes | None]:
2485        """
2486        Creates a figure that visualises the jitter analysis of the specified fibre
2487        pair, fibre1 and fibre2. The figure contains three subplots: the EMG traces of
2488        fibre1's and fibre2's potentials (in separate plots) and a raster plot of the
2489        times of the potentials in each motor unit potential. The x-axes of the plots
2490        are aligned.
2491
2492        By default, all times are relative to the timing of fibre1's
2493        potentials in each motor unit.
2494
2495        If there are no jitter results for that fibre pair (e.g., if there were no
2496        consecutive motor unit potentials containing potentials for both fibres),
2497        returns (None, None) instead of the figure and axes.
2498
2499        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2500
2501        Note that these plots still visualise outlier differences that may be removed
2502        from the final mean consecutive difference calculation.
2503
2504        Parameters
2505        ----------
2506        fibre1 : int
2507            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2508        fibre2 : int
2509            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2510        fibre_clrs : list[Any] | None, optional
2511            List, length two, indicate the colour for the EMG traces for each fibre.
2512            The default is None, in which case default colours (using CartoColor's
2513            "Geyser" palette) are set.
2514        emg_line_lw : float, optional
2515            Linewidth of the EMG traces. The default is 1.
2516        emg_line_alpha : float, optional
2517            Alpha of the EMG traces. The default is 0.25.
2518        emg_y_perc : float, optional
2519            The percentile (across MUPs) of the min and max EMG values to use for
2520            determining the y-axis range for the EMG plots (so outlier values are
2521            ignored). 100 - emg_y_perc is used to find the min value. Must be between
2522            0 and 100 inclusive. The default is 95.
2523        emg_y_buff_prop : float, optional
2524            The buffer to add around the min and max y values computed using emg_y_perc.
2525            The final y axis limits for the EMG traces are computed by multiplying the
2526            difference of those values by emg_y_buff_prop. The default is 0.2.
2527        time_marker_size : float, optional
2528            Size of the markers for the fibre potential times. The default is 2.
2529        align_times_to_fibre1 : bool, optional
2530            Whether to re-align the times so fibre1's potentials always occur at 0. If
2531            false, times are instead relative to each MUP's onset. The default is True.
2532        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
2533            Size of the figure, in inches. The default is (10, 10).
2534        axis_label_size : float, optional
2535            Font size of the axis labels. The default is 12.
2536        title_size : float, optional
2537            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
2538        dpi : int, optional
2539            Plot resolution (dots per inch). The default is 100.
2540        downsample_factor : int, optional
2541            How much to downsample the EMG traces (recommend max of 2). The default is 1.
2542
2543        Raises
2544        ------
2545        ValueError
2546            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit or
2547            if the requested fibre pair is not a valid option.
2548
2549        Returns
2550        -------
2551        fig : Figure | None
2552            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2553        ax : Axes | None
2554            The axes to which the plot belongs.
2555
2556        """
2557
2558        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2559        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2560            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2561        else:
2562            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results  # jitter results dictionary
2563
2564        # Default colours for fibre EMG traces
2565        if fibre_clrs is None:
2566            fibre_clrs = ["#008080", "#ca562c"]
2567
2568        # Get index of the fibre pair in the jitter results
2569        fibre_pair_idx = self.get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(fibre1, fibre2)
2570        if fibre_pair_idx is None:
2571            raise ValueError("Requested fibre pair is not an option.")
2572
2573        # Get mean consecutive difference of that fibre pair
2574        # If doesn't exist, return early with no figure
2575        mcd = jitter_results["mean_consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx]
2576        if np.isnan(mcd):
2577            return None, None
2578        else:  # convert to microseconds
2579            mcd = int((mcd / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2580
2581        # Boolean array of which MUPs were analysed and the indices (in
2582        # fibre_potential_times) of the corresponding fibre potentials
2583        analysed_mup, analysed_fibres_idx = self._get_jitter_analysed_mups_and_fibres(
2584            fibre1, fibre2
2585        )
2586
2587        # Get
2588        # 1) mode of the peak channels of fibre 1 and fibre 2 and
2589        # 2) times of the fibre potentials in the each MUP (nan if not analysed)
2590        n_fibres = 2
2591        fibres_peak_chan = np.full(n_fibres, 0)
2592        analysed_fibre_t = np.full((self.n_potentials, n_fibres), np.nan)
2593        for i in range(n_fibres):  # for each fibre
2594            # int indices of the analysed fibres, without nan (so can use for indexing)
2595            idx = analysed_fibres_idx[i, :]
2596            idx_no_nan = idx[~np.isnan(idx)]
2597            idx_no_nan = idx_no_nan.astype(int)
2598
2599            # Peak channel for each fibre and mode of peak channels
2600            chan = self.fibre_potential_peak_chan[idx_no_nan]
2601            mode_i = scipy.stats.mode(chan)
2602            fibres_peak_chan[i] = int(mode_i[0])
2603
2604            # Fibre times for each mup if mup was analysed (i.e., idx is not nan)
2605            # Otherwise, set to nan
2606            analysed_fibre_t[~np.isnan(idx), i] = self.fibre_potential_times[idx_no_nan]
2607
2608        # Convert fibre times to ms
2609        MS_MULTIPLIER = 1000
2610        analysed_fibre_t = (analysed_fibre_t / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2611
2612        # Create time vectors for EMG traces
2613
2614        # Create time vectors (ms) for x-axis of MUP EMG traces (analysed MUP only)
2615        # Will create a separate column for each trace so can align based on fibre potential
2616        # times if requested
2617        mup_t = (np.arange(1, self.n_samples_window + 1) / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2618        mup_t = np.transpose(
2619            np.tile(mup_t, [self.n_potentials, 1])
2620        )  # repeat and transpose (column = mup)
2621
2622        # If requested, re-align times so fibre1 times = 0 ms
2623        if align_times_to_fibre1:
2624            # Subtract fibre1 times from MUP times
2625            n_t = mup_t.shape[0]
2626            mup_t = mup_t - np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_t, 1])
2627
2628            # Subtract fibre1 times from analysed fibre times
2629            # (must be done second since need original fibres times for changing MUP times)
2630            analysed_fibre_t = analysed_fibre_t - np.transpose(
2631                np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_fibres, 1])
2632            )
2633
2634        # Plot EMG traces
2635
2636        # Set up plot
2637        fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=figsize, height_ratios=[1, 1, 4], sharex=True)
2638        fig.dpi = dpi
2639
2640        # Labels for fibres (add 1 to count from 1)
2641        fibre_labels = [fibre1 + 1, fibre2 + 1]
2642
2643        # Arrays for storing a percentile of the min max values of each EMG trace in
2644        # each fibre
2645        perc_of_max_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2646        perc_of_min_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2647
2648        # Plot MUPs of each fibre in each fibre's "peak" channel
2649        for i in range(n_fibres):
2650            fibre_mups = np.squeeze(
2651                self.all_spikes[analysed_mup, fibres_peak_chan[i], 0::downsample_factor]
2652            )
2653            axs[i].plot(
2654                mup_t[0::downsample_factor, analysed_mup],
2655                np.transpose(fibre_mups),
2656                lw=emg_line_lw,
2657                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2658                alpha=emg_line_alpha,
2659            )
2660
2661            # Compute min and max and the specified percentiles
2662            perc_of_max_y[i] = np.percentile(np.max(fibre_mups, axis=1), emg_y_perc)
2663            perc_of_min_y[i] = np.percentile(np.min(fibre_mups, axis=1), 100 - emg_y_perc)
2664
2665            # Title/axis labels (add one to channel indices so count is from 1)
2666            # No x-axis label since shared across all plots
2667            axs[i].set_title(
2668                f"Motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1}, "
2669                + f"fibre {fibre_labels[i]}, channel {fibres_peak_chan[i] + 1}",
2670                fontsize=title_size,
2671                fontweight="bold",
2672            )
2673            axs[i].set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2674
2675        # Link y-axes of two EMG plots
2676        axs[1].sharey(axs[0])
2677
2678        # Set limits based on percentiles of min/max
2679        emg_y_min = np.min(perc_of_min_y)
2680        emg_y_max = np.max(perc_of_max_y)
2681        emg_y_buff = (emg_y_max - emg_y_min) * emg_y_buff_prop
2682        axs[0].set_ylim([emg_y_min - emg_y_buff, emg_y_max + emg_y_buff])
2683
2684        # Fibre timing
2685
2686        # Plot times of the two fibre potentials in each MUP
2687        mup_number = np.arange(self.n_potentials) + 1  # sets y axis location of each tick
2688        ax_times = 2  # axis to use for plot
2689        for i in range(n_fibres):
2690            axs[ax_times].scatter(
2691                analysed_fibre_t[:, i],
2692                mup_number,
2693                s=time_marker_size,
2694                marker="|",
2695                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2696            )
2697
2698        # Axes (x-axis changes will apply to all plots)
2699        axs[ax_times].set_ylim([1, max(mup_number)])
2700        axs[ax_times].set_yticks([])  # no ticks
2701        axs[ax_times].invert_yaxis()  # first MUP at the top of the plot
2702        axs[ax_times].set_xlim([np.nanmin(mup_t), np.nanmax(mup_t)])  # tight x-axis limits
2703
2704        # Labels
2705        axs[ax_times].set_title(
2706            f"Fibre potential times (mean consecutive difference: {round(mcd, 2)} \u03bcs)",
2707            fontsize=title_size,
2708            fontweight="bold",
2709        )
2710        axs[ax_times].set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2711
2712        return fig, axs

Class for storing data for one motor unit returned from reconstruction analysis.

EMGMotorUnit( number: int, potentials_t_idx: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]], fs: float, chan_xy: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]]) 
 45    def __init__(
 46        self,
 47        number: int,
 48        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
 49        fs: float,
 50        chan_xy: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
 51    ):
 52        """
 53        Initialise EMGMotorUnit object.
 54
 55        Parameters
 56        ----------
 57        number: int
 58            This is the motor unit index (0, 1, 2, ...), returned from TK_filter,
 59            which corresponds to the index position of "motor_units" in the
 60            EMGMotorUnits class. When displayed to the user the motor unit label
 61            is displayed which is +1 this number, e.g. motor_unit_number 0 is the
 62            motor unit labelled as "1".
 63        potentials_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 64            Time indices of the motor unit's potentials in the EMG recording.
 65        fs : float
 66            Sampling frequency (Hz) of the data.
 67        chan_xy : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 68            Channel (electrode) (x,y) coordinates; saved as attribute to facilitate
 69            visualisations.
 70
 71        Returns
 72        -------
 73        None.
 74
 75        """
 76
 77        self.motor_unit_number = number
 78
 79        # Number of potentials (firings) assigned to MU.
 80        self.n_potentials = len(potentials_t_idx)
 81        # Time indices of potentials in EMG.
 82        self.potentials_t_idx = potentials_t_idx
 83
 84        # Set sampling frequency.
 85        self.fs = fs
 86
 87        # Channel/electrode coordinates of the needle.
 88        self.chan_xy = chan_xy
 89
 90        # Store information about analysis that has been performed for this MU
 91        # Note: even if true, may not be results if data was not suitable for analysis
 92        self.analysis_performed = {
 93            "fibres_localised": False,  # localisation step
 94            "fibres_clustered": False,  # clustering fibres step
 95            "fibres_jitter_computed": False,  # jitter analysis step
 96        }
 97
 98        # Localisation attributes.
 99        # Number of fibre potentials (peaks) found across all MUPs.
100        self.n_fibre_potentials = 0
101
102        # Size of window used for localisation.
103        self.n_samples_window = 0
104
105        # Estimated fibre x, y coordinate at each time (size n peaks x 2).
106        self.fibre_centres = np.array([])
107
108        # Onset indices of MUPs that each fibre potential (peak) belongs to.
109        # One for each fibre potential.
110        self.mup_onsets = np.array([])
111
112        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
113        # of the corresponding MUP that it belongs to (in indices units, not seconds).
114        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
115
116        # The channel in which each fibre potential has peak amplitude (may be min or max).
117        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
118
119        # Time series for each MUP and channel
120        # (size: n MU potentials x n chan x time).
121        self.all_spikes = np.array([])
122
123        # Generator potential, represents true underlying potential.
124        self.generator_potential = np.array([])
125
126        # Results for comparing number of clusters for GMM or k-means.
127        self.cluster_scores = None
128
129        # Dictionaries for storing results of clustering and jitter analysis.
130        self.fibre_clustering_results: dict = {}
131        self.fibre_jitter_results: dict = {}
