def add_fibre_localisation( self, fibre_centres: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]], mup_onsets: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]], fibre_potential_times: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]], fibre_potential_peak_chan: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]], all_spikes: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]], generator_potential: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]]): 
167    def add_fibre_localisation(
168        self,
169        fibre_centres: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
170        mup_onsets: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
171        fibre_potential_times: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
172        fibre_potential_peak_chan: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
173        all_spikes: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
174        generator_potential: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
175    ):
176        """
177        Add results of the fibre localisation step to the motor unit object. Computes
178        additional attributes and stores that analysis has been performed.
179
180        Called during EMGAnalysisReconstruct method, reconstruct_fibres
181
182        Parameters
183        ----------
184        fibre_centres : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
185            Estimated location of fibres.
186        mup_onsets : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
187            Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time
188        fibre_potential_times : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
189            Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset (overall) time
190            of the corresponding MUP (listed above in mup_onsets)
191        fibre_potential_peak_chan : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
192            The channel with the peak amplitude for each fibre potential.
193        all_spikes : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
194            All peaks from surrounding channels.
195        generator_potential : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
196            Represents true underlying potential. Used to find MUPs.
197
198        Returns
199        -------
200        None.
201
202        """
203
204        # Note analysis performed.
205        self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = True
206
207        # Store number of fibre potentials (i.e., peaks in the MUPs) found.
208        self.n_fibre_potentials = fibre_centres.shape[0]
209
210        # Store provided attributes.
211        self.fibre_centres = fibre_centres
212        self.mup_onsets = mup_onsets
213        self.fibre_potential_times = fibre_potential_times
214        self.fibre_potential_peak_chan = fibre_potential_peak_chan
215        self.all_spikes = all_spikes
216        self.generator_potential = generator_potential
217
218        # Save the size of the window in number of indices, used later for plots.
219        # So that all_spikes does not need to be saved with the results, and this
220        # value can be saved and loaded instead.
221        self.n_samples_window = self.all_spikes.shape[2]

224        """
225        Returns dictionary of fibre localisation so that it can be saved
226
227        Parameters

230            Whether to save all_spikes. Uses a lot of data and is not necessary.
231            The default is False.

237        """

243            "mup_onsets": self.mup_onsets.tolist(),

247            # "generator_potential" : self.generator_potential.tolist()
248        }
249
250        if save_all_spikes:
251            fibre_local_dict["all_spikes"] = self.all_spikes.tolist()
252
253        return fibre_local_dict

def set_fibre_localisation_from_dict(self, fibre_local_dict: dict): 
255    def set_fibre_localisation_from_dict(self, fibre_local_dict: dict):
256        """
257        Sets fibre localisation results from loaded dictionary.
258
259        Parameters
260        ----------
261        fibre_local_dict : dict
262            Dictionary containing saved results of clustering.
263
264        Returns
265        -------
266        None.
267
268        """
269
270        # Convert data back to arrays.
271        self.n_fibre_potentials = fibre_local_dict["n_fibre_potentials"]
272        self.fibre_centres = np.array(fibre_local_dict["fibre_centres"])
273        self.mup_onsets = np.array(fibre_local_dict["mup_onsets"])
274        self.fibre_potential_times = np.array(fibre_local_dict["fibre_potential_times"])
275        self.all_spikes = np.array(fibre_local_dict["all_spikes"])
276        self.n_samples_window = fibre_local_dict["n_samples_window"]
277        # self.generator_potential = np.array(fibre_local_dict["generator_potential"])
278
279        # Note analysis performed.
280        if self.n_fibre_potentials is not None and len(self.fibre_centres) > 0:
281            self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"] = True

Returns

def cluster_fibre_potentials( self, mu_cluster_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings): 
361    def cluster_fibre_potentials(self, mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings):
362        """
363        Cluster the fibre potentials and compute median fibre locations of the
364        specified motor unit.
365
366        Before this analysis is run, the motor unit's fibres potentials must be
367        identified and localised using the reconstruct_fibres method of the
368        EMGAnalysisReconstruct class.
369
370        Running this method populates the fibre_clustering_results dictionary attribute
371        with the following key/value pairs:
372            mean_n_fps (int): mean number of fibre potentials across all motor unit
373            potentials used in the localisation analysis. Used as input for clustering.
374
375            n_fibre_clusters (int): number of clusters found; may slightly differ from
376            mean_n_fps.
377
378            fibre_clusters (npt.NDArray[np.int32], size (self.fibre_potentials,) ):
379                cluster assignment of each fibre potential
380
381            n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
382                                       size (self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters)):
383            Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each motor unit potential (MUP) that
384            have the same cluster assignment.
385
386            mup_fibre_pos (npt.NDArray[np.float64],
387                           size(self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters)):
388            Location estimates ((x,y) coordinates) of each fibre based on each MUP. If
389            the fibre is not found in the MUP, the coordinates are np.nan.
390
391            fibre_centres_median (npt.NDArray[np.float64], size(n_fibre_clusters, 2)):
392            Median coordinates of each fibre.
393
394        Parameters
395        ----------
396        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
397            Contains all settings for clustering.
398
399        Raises
400        ------
401        RuntimeError
402            Raised if localisation analysis has not been performed on requested motor
403            unit.
404
405        Returns
406        -------
407        None.
408
409        """
410
411        # Set settings for cluster analysis.
412        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
413
414        # Check that localisation has been run.
415        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]:
416            raise RuntimeError(
417                "Localisation analysis has not been performed; cannot cluster fibres."
418            )
419
420        # Arrays to store results for median and GMM clustering.
421        fibre_centres_median = np.array([])
422        fibre_centres_gmm_mean = np.array([])
423        fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = np.array([])
424
425        # Onset indices of all MUPs that have fibre potentials.
426        unique_mup_onsets = np.unique(self.mup_onsets)
427        n_unique_mup_onsets = len(unique_mup_onsets)
428        mean_n_fps = round(len(self.mup_onsets) / n_unique_mup_onsets)
429
430        # Set up data to use for clustering.
431        if self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale > 0:
432            # Scale time column.
433            # Values in (0, 20] for self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale
434            # are suitable for scaling.
435            # Do not scale fibre locations as they are in the same units (mm).
436            time_min = np.min(self.fibre_potential_times)
437            time_max = np.max(self.fibre_potential_times)
438
439            data_to_cluster = np.hstack(
440                (
441                    self.fibre_centres,
442                    (
443                        (np.atleast_2d(self.fibre_potential_times).T - time_min)
444                        / (time_max - time_min)
445                    )
446                    * self.mu_cluster_settings.time_scale,
447                )
448            )
449
450        else:
451            data_to_cluster = self.fibre_centres
452
453        # Choose clustering method.
454        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "dbscan":
455            # Use Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN).
456            clustering = DBSCAN(
457                eps=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_eps,
458                min_samples=self.mu_cluster_settings.dbscan_min_samples,
459            ).fit(data_to_cluster)
460            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(clustering.labels_) + 1
461            fibre_clusters = clustering.labels_
462
463        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
464            # k for clustering.
465            k = self.mu_cluster_settings.k_means_k
466
467            # Use a range if no values of k if not given.
468            if k == 0:
469                min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
470                max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
471            else:
472                min_n_clusters = k
473                max_n_clusters = k
474
475            grid_search = self._k_means_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
476
477            # fibre cluster assignments.
478            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
479            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
480
481            # Record results for graph plotting.
482            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
483
484        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
485            # Use Gaussian Mixture Model Selection.
486            min_n_clusters = np.max([2, mean_n_fps - 2])
487            max_n_clusters = mean_n_fps + 2
488
489            grid_search = self._gmm_selection(data_to_cluster, min_n_clusters, max_n_clusters)
490
491            # Record results for graph plotting.
492            self.cluster_scores = grid_search.cv_results_
493
494            # Fibre cluster assignments.
495            fibre_clusters = grid_search.predict(data_to_cluster)
496            n_fibre_clusters = np.max(fibre_clusters) + 1
497
498            fibre_centres_gmm_mean = grid_search.best_estimator_.means_
499            fibre_centres_gmm_covariance = grid_search.best_estimator_.covariances_
500
501        else:
502            # If no valid clustering method given.
503            raise Exception(
504                "Clustering method,"
505                + str(self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method)
506                + ", not found!"
507                + "Valid options are: dbscan, k-means or gmm."
508            )
509
510        # Initialise arrays for storing results.
511
512        # Number of fibre potentials (FPs) in each MUP that belong to the same
513        # cluster.
514        n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster = np.zeros((self.n_potentials, n_fibre_clusters))
515
516        # Location estimates of each fibre based on each MUP.
517        # Note: unlike original code, data stored so indices match the
518        # self.potentials_t_idx array.
519        mup_fibre_pos = np.full((self.n_potentials, 2, n_fibre_clusters), np.nan)
520
521        # Find median location of each fibre.
522        for cluster_num in np.arange(n_fibre_clusters):
523            # Sometimes multiple fibre potentials in the same MUP are assigned to
524            # the same fibre clusters. One of these will be chosen later as the "best"
525            # to compute the jitter. (One nearest the median over all MUPs)
526            # If no fibres with that cluster num appear in the MUP, position is
527            # stored as np.nan.
528
529            # Iterate through all MUPs (not just ones
530            # present in "mup_onsets") so dimensions align to other MUP features.
531            for mup_num in np.arange(self.n_potentials):
532                mup_onset = self.potentials_t_idx[mup_num]
533
534                # Fibre potentials that belong to the specified onset and cluster.
535                idx = np.flatnonzero(
536                    np.all(
537                        (
538                            (self.mup_onsets == mup_onset),
539                            (fibre_clusters == cluster_num),
540                        ),
541                        axis=0,
542                    )
543                )
544
545                # Store number of fibre potentials found.
546                n_idx = len(idx)
547                n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster[mup_num, cluster_num] = n_idx
548
549                # Compute average position of the fibre based on the specified MUP.
550                if n_idx > 0:
551                    pos = self.fibre_centres[idx, :]
552                    mup_fibre_pos[mup_num, :, cluster_num] = np.mean(pos, axis=0)
553
554            # Compute median fibre positions.
555            with warnings.catch_warnings():
556                warnings.simplefilter("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
557                fibre_centres_median = np.transpose(np.nanmedian(mup_fibre_pos, axis=0))
558
559        # Store results as dictionary.
560        self.fibre_clustering_results = {
561            "mean_n_fps": mean_n_fps,
562            "n_fibre_clusters": n_fibre_clusters,
563            "fibre_clusters": fibre_clusters,
564            "n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster": n_fps_per_mup_and_cluster,
565            "mup_fibre_pos": mup_fibre_pos,
566            "fibre_centres_median": fibre_centres_median,
567            "fibre_centres_gmm_mean": fibre_centres_gmm_mean,
568            "fibre_centres_gmm_covariance": fibre_centres_gmm_covariance,
569        }
570        self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"] = True

Cluster the fibre potentials and compute median fibre locations of the specified motor unit.

Before this analysis is run, the motor unit's fibres potentials must be identified and localised using the reconstruct_fibres method of the EMGAnalysisReconstruct class.

Running this method populates the fibre_clustering_results dictionary attribute with the following key/value pairs: mean_n_fps (int): mean number of fibre potentials across all motor unit potentials used in the localisation analysis. Used as input for clustering.

n_fibre_clusters (int): number of clusters found; may slightly differ from
mean_n_fps.

def plot_compare_cluster_scores(self) -> seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid: 
657    def plot_compare_cluster_scores(self) -> sns.FacetGrid:
658        """
659
660        Parameters
661        ----------
662        None.
663
664        Returns
665        -------
666        sns.FacetGrid
667            Returns the FacetGrid object with the plot on it for further tweaking.
668
669        """
670
671        # Set variable name of data to retrieve.
672        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
673            cluster_str = "param_n_components"
674        elif self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "k-means":
675            cluster_str = "param_n_clusters"
676        else:
677            cluster_str = ""
678
679        # Return blank plot if no data.
680        if cluster_str == "" or self.cluster_scores is None:
681            return sns.catplot(kind="bar")
682
683        # Create bar plot.
684        grid = sns.catplot(
685            kind="bar",
686            x=self.cluster_scores[cluster_str],
687            y=self.cluster_scores["mean_test_score"],
688            legend_out=False,
689        )
690
691        # Set limits and layout.
692        plt.ylim((0, 1))
693        plt.tight_layout(pad=5.0)
694
695        grid.set_axis_labels("number of clusters", "silhouette score")
696
697        return grid

def plot_fibre_locations_setup( self, figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0), axis_label_size: float = 14, tick_label_size: float = 12, dpi: int = 100, threeD: bool = False) -> tuple[matplotlib.figure.Figure, matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes]: 
699    def plot_fibre_locations_setup(
700        self,
701        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.0, 5.0),
702        axis_label_size: float = 14,
703        tick_label_size: float = 12,
704        dpi: int = 100,
705        threeD: bool = False,
706    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
707        """
708        Sets up plot for showing fibre locations, possibly from different motor units.
709
710        Parameters
711        ----------
712        figsize : tuple[int, int], optional
713            Size of the figure. The default is (10, 5).
714        axis_label_size : int, optional
715            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
716        tick_label_size : int, optional
717            Size of the tick labels. The default is 12.
718        dpi : int, optional
719            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
720        threeD : bool, optional
721            Create 3D plot if true. The default is False.
722
723        Returns
724        -------
725        fig : Figure
726            The figure to which the plot belongs.
727        ax : Axes
728            The axes to which the plot belongs.
729
730        """
731
732        # Create new figure with specified size.
733        if threeD:
734            fig = Figure(figsize=figsize)
735            ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
736        else:
737            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
738
739        fig.dpi = dpi
740
741        # Add axis and tick labels.
742        ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
743        ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
744        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
745        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
746
747        # Add time axis if 3D plot.
748        # Type checking complains for 3D but it is fine.
749        if threeD:
750            ax.set_zlabel("time (\u03bc seconds)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
751            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
752
753        plt.title(f"Motor Unit {self.motor_unit_number+1}")
754
755        return fig, ax

def plot_fibre_potential_clustering( self, plot_electrodes: bool = True, pt_potentials_size: float = 10, pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4, pt_mean_size: float = 50, n_sigma: int = 2, axis_equal: bool = True, lw: float = 0.5, figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.2, 5.0), axis_label_size: float = 14, tick_label_size: float = 12, dpi: int = 100, cmap=None, max_x: float = 22, max_y: float = 1, plot_legend: bool = True, legend_pt_size: float = 50, legend_label_size: float = 12): 
805    def plot_fibre_potential_clustering(
806        self,
807        plot_electrodes: bool = True,
808        pt_potentials_size: float = 10,
809        pt_potentials_alpha: float = 0.4,
810        pt_mean_size: float = 50,
811        n_sigma: int = 2,
812        axis_equal: bool = True,
813        lw: float = 0.5,
814        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10.2, 5.0),
815        axis_label_size: float = 14,
816        tick_label_size: float = 12,
817        dpi: int = 100,
818        cmap=None,
819        max_x: float = 22,
820        max_y: float = 1,
821        plot_legend: bool = True,
822        legend_pt_size: float = 50,
823        legend_label_size: float = 12,
824    ):
825        """
826        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
827        with the location of each fibre overlaid. Ellipse confidence regions are plotted
828        around te fibre locations
829        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
830
831        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
832
833        Parameters
834        ----------
835        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
836            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
837        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
838            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
839        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
840            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
841        pt_mean_size : float, optional
842            Size of points for means. The fibre centres. The default is 50.
843        n_sigma : float, optional
844            Number of St. Dev. to plot around the fibre centres. The Default is 2.
845        axis_equal : bool, optional
846            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
847        lw : float, optional
848            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
849        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
850            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
851        axis_label_size : float, optional
852            size of axis label. The default is 14.
853        tick_label_size : float, optional
854            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
855        dpi : int, optional
856            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
857        cmap : Any, optional
858            Colour map to use. The default is None.
859        max_x : float, optional
860            Maximum of x axis. The default is 22.
861        max_y : float, optional
862            Maximum of y axis. The default is 1.
863        plot_legend : bool, optional
864            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
865        legend_pt_size : float, optional
866            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
867        legend_label_size: float, optional
868            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
869
870        Returns
871        -------
872        None.
873
874        """
875
876        # Setup plot
877        fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
878            figsize=figsize,
879            axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
880            tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
881            dpi=dpi,
882        )
883
884        # Add electrodes to plot
885        if plot_electrodes:
886            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax)
887
888        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
889
890        # Plot clusters
891        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
892            self._plot_cluster_points(
893                cluster_no,
894                n_clusters,
895                ax,
896                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
897                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
898                cmap=cmap,
899                lw=lw,
900            )
901
902        # Plot centres and covariance regions (if not GMM).
903        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
904            self._plot_fibre_location(
905                cluster_no,
906                n_clusters,
907                ax,
908                (self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm"),
909                pt_mean_size,
910                n_sigma,
911            )
912
913        # Plot fitted covariance regions for GMM.
914        if self.mu_cluster_settings.clustering_method == "gmm":
915            self._plot_fitted_gmms(ax, n_sigma)
916
917        # Plot legend.
918        if plot_legend:
919            lgnd = ax.legend(
920                bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1),
921                loc="upper left",
922                frameon=False,
923                handletextpad=0.25,
924                fontsize=legend_label_size,
925            )
926            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
927                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
928                h.set_alpha(1)
929
930        # Set y axis limits.
931        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
932
933        # Set x axis limits.
934        ax.set_xlim(-1, max_x)
935
936        # Equal aspect ratio, (this can mess up the axis limits in Windows)
937        if axis_equal:
938            ax.axis("equal")

940    def get_cluster_colour(self, cluster_no: int, n_clusters: int, cmap=None):
941        """
942        Return the colour of a cluster depending on the cluster number and
943        how many total clusters.
944
945        Parameters
946        ----------
947        cluster_no : int
948            Number of the cluster.
949        n_clusters : int
950            Total number of clusters.
951        cmap : Colourmap, optional
952            Use this colour map if given. The default is None.
953
954        Returns
955        -------
956        Colour
957
958        """
959
960        if cmap is None:
961            if n_clusters <= 10:
962                cmap = colormaps["tab10"].colors
963            elif n_clusters <= 20:
964                cmap = colormaps["tab20"].colors
965            else:
966                cmap = plt.cm.rainbow(np.linspace(0, 1, n_clusters))
967        else:  # if colourmap is specified, check that sufficient colours; if not, repeat
968            if len(cmap) < n_clusters:
969                cmap = cmap * int(np.ceil(n_clusters / len(cmap)))
970
971        return cmap[cluster_no]

1248        """
1249        Create scatter plot of fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials
1250        (one point per potential) with z-axis corresponding to the time of each fibre
1251        potential in the motor unit potential (t = 0 ms is MUP onset).
1252
1253        Plots results from one motor unit at a time.
1254
1255        Default point colour depends on the fibre cluster.
1256
1257        Parameters
1258        ----------
1259        plot_electrodes : bool, optional
1260            Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
1261        pt_potentials_size : float, optional
1262            Size of the points for the fibre potentials. The default is 10.
1263        pt_potentials_alpha : float, optional
1264            Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.4.
1265        axis_equal : bool, optional
1266            Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
1267        lw : float, optional
1268            Line weight. The default is 0.5.
1269        figsize tuple[float, float], optional
1270            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
1271        axis_label_size : float, optional
1272            size of axis label. The default is 14.
1273        tick_label_size : float, optional
1274            Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
1275        dpi : int, optional
1276            Dots per inch. The default is 100.
1277        cmap : Any, optional
1278            Colour map to use. The default is None.
1279        max_y : float, optional
1280            The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute
1281            y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure
1282            that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
1283        y_buff: float, optional
1284            Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to
1285            determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points
1286            along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
1287        plot_legend : bool, optional
1288            Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
1289        legend_pt_size : float, optional
1290            Size of points in legend. The default is 50.
1291        legend_label_size: float, optional
1292            Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
1293        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1294            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1295
1296        Returns
1297        -------
1298        None.
1299
1300        """
1301
1302        # Setup plot.
1303        if ax is None:
1304            fig, ax = self.plot_fibre_locations_setup(
1305                figsize=figsize,
1306                axis_label_size=axis_label_size,
1307                tick_label_size=tick_label_size,
1308                dpi=dpi,
1309                threeD=True,
1310            )
1311        else:
1312            fig = None
1313
1314            # Add axis and tick labels.
1315            ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1316            ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1317            ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1318            ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1319            ax.set_zlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size, labelpad=8.0)
1320            ax.tick_params(axis="z", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
1321
1322        # Determine z axis limits based on window used to compute motor unit potentials.
1323        N_MS_PER_SEC = 1000
1324        n_ms = (
1325            ((self.n_samples_window - 1) / 2) / self.fs * N_MS_PER_SEC
1326        )  # shift to plot MUP onset at t=0
1327        max_z = n_ms
1328
1329        # Add electrodes to plot at bottom.
1330        if plot_electrodes:
1331            self._plot_electrodes(ax=ax, z=-max_z, clr="grey", marker_size=5)
1332
1333        n_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1334
1335        # Keep track of max absolute y position to ensure data is not cut off by axis limits.
1336        fibre_max_y = 0
1337
1338        # Plot each cluster.
1339        for cluster_no in range(n_clusters):
1340            self._plot_cluster_points(
1341                cluster_no,
1342                n_clusters,
1343                ax,
1344                pt_size=pt_potentials_size,
1345                pt_alpha=pt_potentials_alpha,
1346                cmap=cmap,
1347                lw=lw,
1348                threeD=True,
1349            )
1350            # Max y
1351            mu_max_y = np.max(
1352                np.abs(
1353                    self.fibre_centres[
1354                        (self.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_clusters"] == cluster_no), 1
1355                    ]
1356                )
1357            )
1358            fibre_max_y = max(fibre_max_y, mu_max_y)
1359
1360        # Add legend.
1361        if plot_legend:
1362            lgnd = ax.legend(
1363                bbox_to_anchor=(1.2, 1.0),
1364                loc="upper left",
1365                frameon=False,
1366                handletextpad=0.25,
1367                fontsize=legend_label_size,
1368            )
1369            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
1370                h._sizes = [legend_pt_size]
1371                h.set_alpha(1)
1372
1373        # Set y axis and z-axis limits.
1374        max_y = max(fibre_max_y * y_buff, max_y)  # Adjust max_y based on data
1375        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
1376        ax.set_zlim(-max_z, max_z)
1377
1378        # Equal aspect ratio for x and y coordinates
1379        if axis_equal:
1380            ax.set_aspect("equalxy", adjustable="box")
1381
1382        return fig, ax

def remove_outliers_iqr( self, intervals: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]]) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.int64]], int]: 
1384    def remove_outliers_iqr(
1385        self, intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1386    ) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int64], int]:
1387        """
1388        Parameters
1389        ----------
1390        intervals: npt.NDArray[np.int]
1391            Array of time intervals.
1392
1393        Returns
1394        -------
1395        npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1396            Array of time intervals with outliers removed.
1397
1398        """
1399
1400        # Calculate interquartile range.
1401        q25, q75 = np.nanpercentile(intervals, 25), np.nanpercentile(intervals, 75)
1402        iqr = q75 - q25
1403
1404        # Calculate the outlier cutoff.
1405        cut_off = iqr * 1.5
1406        lower, upper = q25 - cut_off, q75 + cut_off
1407
1408        # Replace outliers with nan.
1409        ans = np.array([np.nan if x < lower or x > upper else x for x in intervals])
1410        num_of_outliers = np.count_nonzero(((intervals < lower) | (intervals > upper)))
1411
1412        return ans, num_of_outliers
Parameters
  • intervals (npt.NDArray[np.int]): Array of time intervals.
Returns
  • npt.NDArray[np.int64]: Array of time intervals with outliers removed.
def jitter_analysis( self, mu_jitter_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings): 
1593    def jitter_analysis(self, mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings):
1594        """
1595        Calculate jitter between all pairs of fibres.
1596        For each fibre pair:
1597        Firstly a vector of time differences (intervals) are
1598        calculated, one interval for each MUP. If there is more than one fibre
1599        potential assigned to a fibre for a MUP then the one that is closest to the
1600        median (over all fibre potentials in that fibre) is chose. If there are no
1601        fibre potentials for that fibre and MUP then an interval cannot be record so
1602        is NAN.
1603        Secondly, the consecutive differences are calculated, the difference
1604        between intervals that are in adjacent MUPs. If an interval does not exist
1605        then NAN is recorded.
1606        Finally, the mean consecutive differences is calculated to measure the jitter.
1607        The median consecutive differences is also calculated to try and account
1608        for poor data.
1609
1610        Parameters
1611        ----------
1612        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
1613            The setting to use for the jitter analysis.
1614
1615        Returns
1616        -------
1617        None.
1618
1619        """
1620
1621        # Set jitter settings.
1622        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
1623
1624        # Check that localisation and fibre clustering has been run.
1625        if (
1626            not self.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]
1627            or not self.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]
1628        ):
1629            raise RuntimeError(
1630                "Localisation analysis and fibre cluster analysis"
1631                + "must be performed before jitter analysis!"
1632            )
1633
1634        # Check there is data to do the calculation.
1635        if self.n_potentials < 2:
1636            raise RuntimeError("Not enough MUPs to perform jitter analysis!")
1637
1638        # Get the number of clusters.
1639        n_fibre_clusters = self.fibre_clustering_results["n_fibre_clusters"]
1640
1641        # The number of jitter calculations to do between fibres.
1642        number_of_jitter_calcs = int(n_fibre_clusters * (n_fibre_clusters - 1) / 2)
1643
1644        # Calculations to report.
1645        fibre1_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1646        fibre2_numbers = np.full(number_of_jitter_calcs, 0)
1647        mean_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1648        median_consecutive_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1649        fibre_potential_time_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1650        consecutive_diffs = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials - 1))
1651        number_of_differences = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1652        number_of_cons_diffs = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1653        number_of_differences_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1654        number_of_cons_diffs_outliers = np.zeros(number_of_jitter_calcs)
1655        fibre1_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1656        fibre2_pots_used_idx = np.zeros((number_of_jitter_calcs, self.n_potentials))
1657
1658        # Loop thro' each fibre pair and perform the jitter analysis.
1659        # Fibre pair count.
1660        count = 0
1661        for fibre1_num in range(n_fibre_clusters - 1):
1662            for fibre2_num in np.arange(fibre1_num + 1, n_fibre_clusters):
1663                # Do jitter analysis between fibre1 and fibre2.
1664                (
1665                    mean_consecutive_diffs[count],
1666                    median_consecutive_diffs[count],
1667                    fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :],
1668                    consecutive_diffs[count, :],
1669                    number_of_differences_outliers[count],
1670                    number_of_cons_diffs_outliers[count],
1671                    fibre1_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1672                    fibre2_pots_used_idx[count, :],
1673                ) = self._jitter_analysis_between_two_fibres(fibre1_num, fibre2_num)
1674
1675                # Record fibres analysed and some data counts.
1676                fibre1_numbers[count] = fibre1_num
1677                fibre2_numbers[count] = fibre2_num
1678                number_of_differences[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1679                    ~np.isnan(fibre_potential_time_diffs[count, :])
1680                )
1681                number_of_cons_diffs[count] = np.count_nonzero(
1682                    ~np.isnan(consecutive_diffs[count, :])
1683                )
1684                count += 1
1685
1686        # Record final jitter analysis results in dictionary.
1687        self.fibre_jitter_results = {
1688            "fibre1_numbers": fibre1_numbers,
1689            "fibre2_numbers": fibre2_numbers,
1690            "mean_consecutive_diffs": mean_consecutive_diffs,
1691            "median_consecutive_diffs": median_consecutive_diffs,
1692            "differences": fibre_potential_time_diffs,
1693            "consecutive_diffs": consecutive_diffs,
1694            "number_of_differences": number_of_differences,
1695            "number_of_differences_outliers": number_of_differences_outliers,
1696            "number_of_cons_diffs": number_of_cons_diffs,
1697            "number_of_cons_diffs_outliers": number_of_cons_diffs_outliers,
1698            "fibre1_pots_used_idx": fibre1_pots_used_idx,
1699            "fibre2_pots_used_idx": fibre2_pots_used_idx,
1700        }
1701
1702        # Record that the jitter analysis has been performed for this motor unit.
1703        self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"] = True

Calculate jitter between all pairs of fibres. For each fibre pair: Firstly a vector of time differences (intervals) are calculated, one interval for each MUP. If there is more than one fibre potential assigned to a fibre for a MUP then the one that is closest to the median (over all fibre potentials in that fibre) is chose. If there are no fibre potentials for that fibre and MUP then an interval cannot be record so is NAN. Secondly, the consecutive differences are calculated, the difference between intervals that are in adjacent MUPs. If an interval does not exist then NAN is recorded. Finally, the mean consecutive differences is calculated to measure the jitter. The median consecutive differences is also calculated to try and account for poor data.

Parameters
  • mu_jitter_settings (EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings): The setting to use for the jitter analysis.
Returns
  • None.

2043        """

2046
2047        Parameters
2048        ----------

2051        cmap : matplotlib colormap name or object, or list of colors, optional
2052            Colourmap. The default is matplotlib colourmap "magma".
2053        vmax : float, optional
2054            The upper limit for the colourmap, in microseconds. This argument ensures
2055            that outliers do not dramatically skew the colourmap and that colours are
2056            easily comparable across motor units. The default is 100.
2057        clr_background: colour specification, optional

2060        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional

2064        -------
2065        fig : Figure | None

2068            Axes object with the heatmap.
2069        """
2070
2071        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2072        if ax is None:
2073            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
2074        else:
2075            fig = None
2076
2077        # Get number of fibre pairs; return early if none.
2078        n_fibre_pairs = len(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"])
2079        if n_fibre_pairs == 0:
2080            ax.set_axis_off()  # remove plot axes
2081            return fig, ax
2082
2083        n_fibres = int(np.max(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"]) + 1)
2084
2085        # Create data array for the heat plot.
2086        data = np.full((n_fibres, n_fibres), np.nan)
2087
2088        for i in range(n_fibre_pairs):

2090            fib2 = int(self.fibre_jitter_results["fibre2_numbers"][i])
2091
2092            if median:
2093                val = self.fibre_jitter_results["median_consecutive_diffs"][i]
2094            else:

2096
2097            # Convert indices to micro seconds.
2098            if not np.isnan(val):
2099                val = int((val / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2100
2101            # Make heat plot symetrical.
2102            data[fib1, fib2] = val
2103            data[fib2, fib1] = val
2104
2105        # Plotting the heatmap.
2106        str_fibres = [str(x) for x in np.arange(1, n_fibres + 1)]
2107
2108        ax = sns.heatmap(
2109            data=data,
2110            vmin=0,
2111            vmax=vmax,
2112            cmap=cmap,
2113            annot=True,
2114            xticklabels=str_fibres,
2115            yticklabels=str_fibres,
2116            cbar_kws={"label": "\u03bc seconds"},
2117            fmt="g",
2118            ax=ax,
2119        )
2120
2121        ax.set_xlabel("fibre number")
2122        ax.set_ylabel("fibre number")
2123
2124        # Titles (line break ensures that plot is the same size as plot_jitter_heat_plot,

2134                fontweight="bold",
2135            )
2136
2137        # Ensure square, change background colour, and add frame
2138        ax.set_aspect("equal")
2139        ax.set_facecolor(clr_background)
2140        for _, spine in ax.spines.items():
2141            spine.set_visible(True)

def get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> int | None: 
2312    def get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(self, fibre1: int, fibre2: int) -> int | None:
2313        """
2314        Get index of requested fibre pair in the motor unit's jitter results
2315        (fibre_jitter_results attribute). Will return None if the fibre pair is not an
2316        option or if there are multiple matches for that fibre pair in the jitter
2317        results (which should only arrise if there is an error in the analysis code).
2318
2319        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2320
2321        Parameters
2322        ----------
2323        fibre1 : int
2324            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2325        fibre2 : int
2326            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2327
2328        Raises
2329        ------
2330        ValueError
2331            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit.
2332
2333        Returns
2334        -------
2335        fibre_pair_idx : int | None
2336            Index of the specified fibre; can use for extracting the corresponding
2337            results in the motor unit's jitter analysis results. Is None if fibre pair
2338            is not a valid option.
2339        """
2340
2341        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2342        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2343            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2344        else:
2345            # Jitter results
2346            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results
2347
2348        # Determine which fields in jitter_results to use for each fibre
2349        # Lower fibre number is stored in fibre1 results, while higher value is fibre2
2350        if fibre1 < fibre2:
2351            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2352            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2353        else:
2354            fibre2_numbers_field = "fibre1_numbers"
2355            fibre1_numbers_field = "fibre2_numbers"
2356
2357        # Determine index of results for that fibre pair
2358        fibre_pair_idx_bool = np.all(
2359            [
2360                jitter_results[fibre1_numbers_field] == fibre1,
2361                jitter_results[fibre2_numbers_field] == fibre2,
2362            ],
2363            axis=0,
2364        )
2365
2366        # Compute number of matches; if not exactly 1, return None
2367        n_fibre_pair_matches = sum(fibre_pair_idx_bool)
2368        if n_fibre_pair_matches == 1:
2369            fibre_pair_idx = np.flatnonzero(fibre_pair_idx_bool)[0]
2370        else:
2371            fibre_pair_idx = None
2372
2373        # Return fibre pair index
2374        return fibre_pair_idx

Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.

2479        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 10),
2480        axis_label_size: float = 12,
2481        title_size: float = 12,
2482        dpi: int = 100,
2483        downsample_factor: int = 1,
2484    ) -> tuple[Figure | None, Axes | None]:
2485        """
2486        Creates a figure that visualises the jitter analysis of the specified fibre
2487        pair, fibre1 and fibre2. The figure contains three subplots: the EMG traces of
2488        fibre1's and fibre2's potentials (in separate plots) and a raster plot of the
2489        times of the potentials in each motor unit potential. The x-axes of the plots
2490        are aligned.
2491
2492        By default, all times are relative to the timing of fibre1's
2493        potentials in each motor unit.
2494
2495        If there are no jitter results for that fibre pair (e.g., if there were no
2496        consecutive motor unit potentials containing potentials for both fibres),
2497        returns (None, None) instead of the figure and axes.
2498
2499        Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.
2500
2501        Note that these plots still visualise outlier differences that may be removed
2502        from the final mean consecutive difference calculation.
2503
2504        Parameters
2505        ----------
2506        fibre1 : int
2507            Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
2508        fibre2 : int
2509            Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
2510        fibre_clrs : list[Any] | None, optional
2511            List, length two, indicate the colour for the EMG traces for each fibre.
2512            The default is None, in which case default colours (using CartoColor's
2513            "Geyser" palette) are set.
2514        emg_line_lw : float, optional
2515            Linewidth of the EMG traces. The default is 1.
2516        emg_line_alpha : float, optional
2517            Alpha of the EMG traces. The default is 0.25.
2518        emg_y_perc : float, optional
2519            The percentile (across MUPs) of the min and max EMG values to use for
2520            determining the y-axis range for the EMG plots (so outlier values are
2521            ignored). 100 - emg_y_perc is used to find the min value. Must be between
2522            0 and 100 inclusive. The default is 95.
2523        emg_y_buff_prop : float, optional
2524            The buffer to add around the min and max y values computed using emg_y_perc.
2525            The final y axis limits for the EMG traces are computed by multiplying the
2526            difference of those values by emg_y_buff_prop. The default is 0.2.
2527        time_marker_size : float, optional
2528            Size of the markers for the fibre potential times. The default is 2.
2529        align_times_to_fibre1 : bool, optional
2530            Whether to re-align the times so fibre1's potentials always occur at 0. If
2531            false, times are instead relative to each MUP's onset. The default is True.
2532        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
2533            Size of the figure, in inches. The default is (10, 10).
2534        axis_label_size : float, optional
2535            Font size of the axis labels. The default is 12.
2536        title_size : float, optional
2537            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
2538        dpi : int, optional
2539            Plot resolution (dots per inch). The default is 100.
2540        downsample_factor : int, optional
2541            How much to downsample the EMG traces (recommend max of 2). The default is 1.
2542
2543        Raises
2544        ------
2545        ValueError
2546            Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit or
2547            if the requested fibre pair is not a valid option.
2548
2549        Returns
2550        -------
2551        fig : Figure | None
2552            The figure to which the plot belongs.
2553        ax : Axes | None
2554            The axes to which the plot belongs.
2555
2556        """
2557
2558        # First check that jitter analysis has been performed
2559        if not self.analysis_performed["fibres_jitter_computed"]:
2560            raise ValueError("Jitter has not yet been computed for this motor unit.")
2561        else:
2562            jitter_results = self.fibre_jitter_results  # jitter results dictionary
2563
2564        # Default colours for fibre EMG traces
2565        if fibre_clrs is None:
2566            fibre_clrs = ["#008080", "#ca562c"]
2567
2568        # Get index of the fibre pair in the jitter results
2569        fibre_pair_idx = self.get_jitter_fibre_pair_idx(fibre1, fibre2)
2570        if fibre_pair_idx is None:
2571            raise ValueError("Requested fibre pair is not an option.")
2572
2573        # Get mean consecutive difference of that fibre pair
2574        # If doesn't exist, return early with no figure
2575        mcd = jitter_results["mean_consecutive_diffs"][fibre_pair_idx]
2576        if np.isnan(mcd):
2577            return None, None
2578        else:  # convert to microseconds
2579            mcd = int((mcd / self.fs) * 1e6 + 0.5)
2580
2581        # Boolean array of which MUPs were analysed and the indices (in
2582        # fibre_potential_times) of the corresponding fibre potentials
2583        analysed_mup, analysed_fibres_idx = self._get_jitter_analysed_mups_and_fibres(
2584            fibre1, fibre2
2585        )
2586
2587        # Get
2588        # 1) mode of the peak channels of fibre 1 and fibre 2 and
2589        # 2) times of the fibre potentials in the each MUP (nan if not analysed)
2590        n_fibres = 2
2591        fibres_peak_chan = np.full(n_fibres, 0)
2592        analysed_fibre_t = np.full((self.n_potentials, n_fibres), np.nan)
2593        for i in range(n_fibres):  # for each fibre
2594            # int indices of the analysed fibres, without nan (so can use for indexing)
2595            idx = analysed_fibres_idx[i, :]
2596            idx_no_nan = idx[~np.isnan(idx)]
2597            idx_no_nan = idx_no_nan.astype(int)
2598
2599            # Peak channel for each fibre and mode of peak channels
2600            chan = self.fibre_potential_peak_chan[idx_no_nan]
2601            mode_i = scipy.stats.mode(chan)
2602            fibres_peak_chan[i] = int(mode_i[0])
2603
2604            # Fibre times for each mup if mup was analysed (i.e., idx is not nan)
2605            # Otherwise, set to nan
2606            analysed_fibre_t[~np.isnan(idx), i] = self.fibre_potential_times[idx_no_nan]
2607
2608        # Convert fibre times to ms
2609        MS_MULTIPLIER = 1000
2610        analysed_fibre_t = (analysed_fibre_t / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2611
2612        # Create time vectors for EMG traces
2613
2614        # Create time vectors (ms) for x-axis of MUP EMG traces (analysed MUP only)
2615        # Will create a separate column for each trace so can align based on fibre potential
2616        # times if requested
2617        mup_t = (np.arange(1, self.n_samples_window + 1) / self.fs) * MS_MULTIPLIER
2618        mup_t = np.transpose(
2619            np.tile(mup_t, [self.n_potentials, 1])
2620        )  # repeat and transpose (column = mup)
2621
2622        # If requested, re-align times so fibre1 times = 0 ms
2623        if align_times_to_fibre1:
2624            # Subtract fibre1 times from MUP times
2625            n_t = mup_t.shape[0]
2626            mup_t = mup_t - np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_t, 1])
2627
2628            # Subtract fibre1 times from analysed fibre times
2629            # (must be done second since need original fibres times for changing MUP times)
2630            analysed_fibre_t = analysed_fibre_t - np.transpose(
2631                np.tile(analysed_fibre_t[:, 0], [n_fibres, 1])
2632            )
2633
2634        # Plot EMG traces
2635
2636        # Set up plot
2637        fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=figsize, height_ratios=[1, 1, 4], sharex=True)
2638        fig.dpi = dpi
2639
2640        # Labels for fibres (add 1 to count from 1)
2641        fibre_labels = [fibre1 + 1, fibre2 + 1]
2642
2643        # Arrays for storing a percentile of the min max values of each EMG trace in
2644        # each fibre
2645        perc_of_max_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2646        perc_of_min_y = np.zeros(n_fibres)
2647
2648        # Plot MUPs of each fibre in each fibre's "peak" channel
2649        for i in range(n_fibres):
2650            fibre_mups = np.squeeze(
2651                self.all_spikes[analysed_mup, fibres_peak_chan[i], 0::downsample_factor]
2652            )
2653            axs[i].plot(
2654                mup_t[0::downsample_factor, analysed_mup],
2655                np.transpose(fibre_mups),
2656                lw=emg_line_lw,
2657                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2658                alpha=emg_line_alpha,
2659            )
2660
2661            # Compute min and max and the specified percentiles
2662            perc_of_max_y[i] = np.percentile(np.max(fibre_mups, axis=1), emg_y_perc)
2663            perc_of_min_y[i] = np.percentile(np.min(fibre_mups, axis=1), 100 - emg_y_perc)
2664
2665            # Title/axis labels (add one to channel indices so count is from 1)
2666            # No x-axis label since shared across all plots
2667            axs[i].set_title(
2668                f"Motor unit {self.motor_unit_number + 1}, "
2669                + f"fibre {fibre_labels[i]}, channel {fibres_peak_chan[i] + 1}",
2670                fontsize=title_size,
2671                fontweight="bold",
2672            )
2673            axs[i].set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2674
2675        # Link y-axes of two EMG plots
2676        axs[1].sharey(axs[0])
2677
2678        # Set limits based on percentiles of min/max
2679        emg_y_min = np.min(perc_of_min_y)
2680        emg_y_max = np.max(perc_of_max_y)
2681        emg_y_buff = (emg_y_max - emg_y_min) * emg_y_buff_prop
2682        axs[0].set_ylim([emg_y_min - emg_y_buff, emg_y_max + emg_y_buff])
2683
2684        # Fibre timing
2685
2686        # Plot times of the two fibre potentials in each MUP
2687        mup_number = np.arange(self.n_potentials) + 1  # sets y axis location of each tick
2688        ax_times = 2  # axis to use for plot
2689        for i in range(n_fibres):
2690            axs[ax_times].scatter(
2691                analysed_fibre_t[:, i],
2692                mup_number,
2693                s=time_marker_size,
2694                marker="|",
2695                color=fibre_clrs[i],
2696            )
2697
2698        # Axes (x-axis changes will apply to all plots)
2699        axs[ax_times].set_ylim([1, max(mup_number)])
2700        axs[ax_times].set_yticks([])  # no ticks
2701        axs[ax_times].invert_yaxis()  # first MUP at the top of the plot
2702        axs[ax_times].set_xlim([np.nanmin(mup_t), np.nanmax(mup_t)])  # tight x-axis limits
2703
2704        # Labels
2705        axs[ax_times].set_title(
2706            f"Fibre potential times (mean consecutive difference: {round(mcd, 2)} \u03bcs)",
2707            fontsize=title_size,
2708            fontweight="bold",
2709        )
2710        axs[ax_times].set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
2711
2712        return fig, axs

Creates a figure that visualises the jitter analysis of the specified fibre pair, fibre1 and fibre2. The figure contains three subplots: the EMG traces of fibre1's and fibre2's potentials (in separate plots) and a raster plot of the times of the potentials in each motor unit potential. The x-axes of the plots are aligned.

By default, all times are relative to the timing of fibre1's potentials in each motor unit.

If there are no jitter results for that fibre pair (e.g., if there were no consecutive motor unit potentials containing potentials for both fibres), returns (None, None) instead of the figure and axes.

Fibre1 and fibre2 do not need to be in ascending order.

Note that these plots still visualise outlier differences that may be removed from the final mean consecutive difference calculation.

Parameters
  • fibre1 (int): Number of the first fibre (counting from 0).
  • fibre2 (int): Number of the second fibre (counting from 0).
  • fibre_clrs (list[Any] | None, optional): List, length two, indicate the colour for the EMG traces for each fibre. The default is None, in which case default colours (using CartoColor's "Geyser" palette) are set.
  • emg_line_lw (float, optional): Linewidth of the EMG traces. The default is 1.
  • emg_line_alpha (float, optional): Alpha of the EMG traces. The default is 0.25.
  • emg_y_perc (float, optional): The percentile (across MUPs) of the min and max EMG values to use for determining the y-axis range for the EMG plots (so outlier values are ignored). 100 - emg_y_perc is used to find the min value. Must be between 0 and 100 inclusive. The default is 95.
  • emg_y_buff_prop (float, optional): The buffer to add around the min and max y values computed using emg_y_perc. The final y axis limits for the EMG traces are computed by multiplying the difference of those values by emg_y_buff_prop. The default is 0.2.
  • time_marker_size (float, optional): Size of the markers for the fibre potential times. The default is 2.
  • align_times_to_fibre1 (bool, optional): Whether to re-align the times so fibre1's potentials always occur at 0. If false, times are instead relative to each MUP's onset. The default is True.
  • figsize (tuple[float, float], optional): Size of the figure, in inches. The default is (10, 10).
  • axis_label_size (float, optional): Font size of the axis labels. The default is 12.
  • title_size (float, optional): Font size the titles. The default is 12.
  • dpi (int, optional): Plot resolution (dots per inch). The default is 100.
  • downsample_factor (int, optional): How much to downsample the EMG traces (recommend max of 2). The default is 1.
Raises
  • ValueError: Raised if jitter analysis has not yet been performed for this motor unit or if the requested fibre pair is not a valid option.
Returns
  • fig (Figure | None): The figure to which the plot belongs.
  • ax (Axes | None): The axes to which the plot belongs.

2905            are plotted, the default colour scheme or given cmap is used.

2929            Dots per inch. The default is 300.

2933            The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute
2934            y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure
2935            that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
2936        y_buff: float, optional
2937            Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to
2938            determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points
2939            along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
2940        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional

2943        Returns
2944        -------

2947        ax : Axes
2948            The axes to which the plot belongs.
2949
2950        """
2951
2952        # Check value of location_type is valid
2953        if location_type not in ["potentials", "fibres"]:
2954            raise ValueError(
2955                f"location_type of {location_type} is not valid - must be 'potentials' or 'fibres'"
2956            )
2957
2958        # If not specified, determine point style based on location_type
2959        match location_type:
2960            case "potentials":
2961                if not pt_size:
2962                    pt_size = 10
2963                if not pt_alpha:
2964                    pt_alpha = 0.5
2965            case "fibres":
2966                if not pt_size:
2967                    pt_size = 75
2968                if not pt_alpha:
2969                    pt_alpha = 1
2970
2971        # Default colormap - will use if colors not specified.
2972        if cmap is None:
2973            cmap = colormaps["tab10"].colors
2974
2975        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
2976        if ax is None:
2977            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
2978            fig.dpi = dpi
2979        else:
2980            fig = None
2981
2982        # Motor unit(s) to plot.
2983        if motor_unit_idx is not None:
2984            if motor_unit_idx < 0:
2985                motor_units = []
2986            else:
2987                motor_units = [self.motor_units[motor_unit_idx]]
2988        else:
2989            motor_units = self.motor_units
2990

2994

2996        fibre_max_y = 0

2999            # Colour for motor unit - differs depending on motor unit.
3000            # Face colour: default only used for plotting potentials
3001            if (pt_facecolor is None) and (location_type == "potentials"):
3002                # Use same colour scheme as cluster colours for motor units.
3003                mu_pt_facecolor = mu.get_cluster_colour(
3004                    mu.motor_unit_number, self.n_motor_units, cmap
3005                )
3006            elif not pt_facecolor:
3007                mu_pt_facecolor = "none"
3008            else:
3009                mu_pt_facecolor = pt_facecolor
3010
3011            # Edge colour: default only used for plotting fibres
3012            if (pt_edgecolor is None) and (location_type == "fibres"):
3013                # Use same colour scheme as cluster colours for motor units.
3014                mu_pt_edgecolor = mu.get_cluster_colour(
3015                    mu.motor_unit_number, self.n_motor_units, cmap
3016                )
3017            elif not pt_facecolor:
3018                mu_pt_edgecolor = "none"
3019            else:
3020                mu_pt_edgecolor = pt_edgecolor
3021
3022            # Data to plot
3023            if (location_type == "potentials") and (mu.analysis_performed["fibres_localised"]):
3024                # Use fibre potential locations
3025                mu_fibre_locations = mu.fibre_centres
3026
3027            elif (location_type == "fibres") and (mu.analysis_performed["fibres_clustered"]):
3028                # Use fibre locations
3029                mu_fibre_locations = mu.fibre_clustering_results["fibre_centres_median"]
3030
3031            else:
3032                # if analyses have not been performed, no fibres locations
3033                mu_fibre_locations = None
3034
3035            # Plot locations and compute max absolute y location
3036            if mu_fibre_locations is not None:
3037                ax.scatter(
3038                    mu_fibre_locations[:, 0],
3039                    mu_fibre_locations[:, 1],
3040                    pt_size,
3041                    alpha=pt_alpha,
3042                    linewidth=pt_linewidth,
3043                    facecolor=mu_pt_facecolor,
3044                    edgecolor=mu_pt_edgecolor,
3045                    label=f"motor unit {mu.motor_unit_number + 1}",
3046                )
3047
3048                # Max absolute y location
3049                mu_max_y = np.max(np.abs(mu_fibre_locations[:, 1]))
3050                fibre_max_y = max(fibre_max_y, mu_max_y)
3051
3052        # Plot legend
3053        if plot_legend:
3054            lgnd = ax.legend(
3055                bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1),
3056                loc="upper left",
3057                frameon=False,
3058                handletextpad=0.25,
3059                fontsize=legend_label_size,
3060            )
3061            for h in lgnd.legend_handles:
3062                h._sizes = [max(min_legend_pt_size, pt_size)]
3063                h.set_alpha(1)
3064
3065        # Axis and tick labels.
3066        ax.set_xlabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
3067        ax.set_ylabel("position (mm)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
3068        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
3069        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=tick_label_size)
3070        max_y = max(fibre_max_y * y_buff, max_y)  # Adjust max_y based on data
3071        ax.set_ylim(-max_y, max_y)
3072
3073        # Equal aspect ratio.
3074        if axis_equal:
3075            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
3076
3077        return fig, ax

Create 2D scatter plot of either

1) fibre localisations estimated from all fibre potentials (i.e., before clustering step).

or

2) fibre locations (median locations determined by clustering step, with one location per fibre).

The data plotted is determined by location_type: location_type = "potentials" returns the fibre potential localisations, while location_type = "fibres" returns the final estimated location of each fibre.

Can either plot fibre locations of all motor units or one, specified motor unit potential.

Default point colour depends on the motor unit number.

Parameters
  • location_type (str): Either "potentials" or "fibres" (see above).
  • motor_unit_idx (int, optional): Motor unit index. The default is None.
  • plot_electrodes (bool, optional): Whether to plot electrodes or not. The default is True.
  • pt_size (float, optional): Size of the points for the fibre locations. The default is 10 for potentials and 75 for fibres.
  • pt_alpha (float, optional): Alpha value for the points, [0, 1] (transparency). The default is 0.5 for potentials and 1 for fibres.
  • pt_facecolor (Any, optional): Colour of point centres. The default is None. If fibre potential locations are plotted, the default colour scheme or given cmap is used.
  • pt_edgecolor (Any, optional): Colour of point outlines. The default is None. If fibre locations are plotted, the default colour scheme or given cmap is used.
  • pt_linewidth (float, optional): Linewidth of points. Only used if pt_edgecolor is not None. The default is 3.
  • axis_equal (bool, optional): Whether aspect ratio should be plotted equal. The default is True.
  • figsize tuple[float, float], optional: Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
  • axis_label_size (float, optional): size of axis label. The default is 14.
  • tick_label_size (float, optional): Size of tick labels. The default is 12.
  • plot_legend (bool, optional): Plot the legend or not. The default is True.
  • min_legend_pt_size (float, optional): Minimum size of points in legend - if pt_size is less than min_legend_pt_size, this value will be used for the legend point size. The default is 30.
  • legend_label_size (float, optional): Size of labels in legend. The default is 12.
  • dpi (int, optional, optional): Dots per inch. The default is 300.
  • cmap (Any, optional, optional): Colour map to use. The default is None.
  • max_y (float, optional): The minimum positive and negative limits for the y-axis. The max absolute y axis location * y_buff is used instead if it exceeds this value to ensure that data points are not cut out of the plot. The default is 1.
  • y_buff (float, optional): Factor by which to multiple the max absolute y axis location in order to determine y-axis limits (see max_y argument). Controls buffer around points along the y-axis. The default is 1.75, which provides room for larger points.
  • ax (plt.axes.Axes, optional): Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
Returns
  • fig (Figure): The figure to which the plot belongs.
  • ax (Axes): The axes to which the plot belongs.
